items.desc: JOB DESCRIPTION About the Project SAFER PLUS is a £1.25 million Innovate UK-funded project developing Pakistan's first full-scale plant for converting agricultural waste cotton stalks and sugarcane bagasse into engineered bio-coal pellets through torrefaction. The bio-coal directly replaces imported fossil coal in textile mill boilers and brick kilns at 40–50% lower cost, with substantially reduced emissions. The demonstration hub is being established at the University of Kamalia, South Punjab, in partnership with Eco Research Limited and Pakistani textile industry partners. Northumbria University is now recruiting two Research Associates to join the SAFER PLUS team. These are distinct but complementary roles, and candidates should clearly indicate in their application which post they are applying for. Post 1: Research Associate in Thermochemical Conversion and Biomass Processing The Role You will lead the scientific characterisation and optimisation of the torrefaction process for Pakistani agricultural waste feedstocks. Working directly with the Principal Investigator, you will design and conduct experiments, produce validated fuel quality data, and generate the technical evidence base that underpins SAFER PLUS's commercial and regulatory case. Key Responsibilities Conduct thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) at multiple heating rates to characterise cotton stalk and sugarcane bagasse pyrolysis and torrefaction kinetics Develop and validate kinetic and thermodynamic models for the torrefaction process under industrially relevant conditions Characterise feedstocks and bio-coal products using XRD, FTIR, BET surface area analysis, SEM-EDS and proximate/ultimate analysis Determine gross calorific value (GCV), moisture, ash, volatile matter and sulphur content of bio-coal products under varying process conditions Investigate the effect of feedstock blend, moisture content, torrefaction temperature and residence time on bio-coal quality and consistency Contribute to peer-reviewed publications and project reports Support knowledge transfer activities with the University of Kamalia and industrial partners in Pakistan Essential Requirements MS/PhD in Chemical Engineering, Materials Engineering, Energy Engineering or a closely related discipline (or equivalent research experience) Demonstrated experience in thermochemical conversion of biomass, specifically pyrolysis, torrefaction or gasification Proficiency in TGA, kinetic modelling and thermodynamic analysis Experience with materials characterisation techniques including FTIR, XRD, SEM-EDS or BET Strong publication record commensurate with career stage Ability to work independently and manage experimental programmes Excellent written and verbal communication in English Desirable Requirements Experience with agricultural residue feedstocks particularly cotton stalk, sugarcane bagasse or wheat straw Familiarity with Pakistani or South Asian agricultural and industrial contexts Experience with proximate and ultimate fuel analysis for industrial applications Knowledge of cement, textile or brick kiln combustion requirements Further information about the requirements of the role is available in the person specification . Post 2: Research Associate in Machine Learning and Systems Integration for Clean Energy The Role You will develop and apply machine learning and data-driven modelling approaches to optimise the integrated SAFER PLUS energy system from feedstock characterisation through torrefaction to downstream combustion performance. You will work with experimental data generated by the project team and operational data from the demonstration plant to build predictive models that maximise bio-coal quality and system performance. Key Responsibilities Develop ML predictive models (including but not limited to Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, Neural Networks) to predict bio-coal quality from feedstock properties and process parameters Build and validate process optimisation models integrating torrefaction conditions, feedstock blend and downstream combustion performance Design and implement a data acquisition and management framework for the SAFER PLUS demonstration plant at the University of Kamalia Develop real-time process monitoring tools and dashboards for plant operators in Pakistan Apply Python-based data science tools for model training, validation and deployment Collaborate with the thermochemical team (Post 1) to identify key process variables and translate model outputs into actionable operating guidance Contribute to peer-reviewed publications, particularly at the intersection of ML and biomass energy systems Support digital capacity building with Pakistani partner institutions Essential Requirements MS/PhD in Chemical Engineering, Data Science, Energy Systems, Computer Science or a closely related discipline (or equivalent research experience) Demonstrated experience in machine learning applied to engineering or energy systems classification, regression and …

Do the applied engineering that makes AI work in practice. Own evaluation as a first-class deliverable. items.desc: Supercell Helsinki Ohjelmointi Lisätty: 26.10.2026 Voimassa: 24.1.2027 Hae tästä Vanhentunut? Our AI team is looking for an individual who is exceptional at the applied end of the craft: taking modern models and turning them into features and tools that hold up in production, at Supercell scale, under real deadlines. The challenge at the centre of this role is the distance between a demo and a product. A model that works in a notebook is not a feature that works for hundreds of millions of players, or a tool a game team trusts with their daily work. Help us Close that gap: the evaluation that tells you it's actually good, the latency and cost envelope that makes it viable, the failure modes you find before players do, and the plumbing that makes it boring to operate. We're not looking for someone who wants to train a frontier model. We're looking for someone who gets unreasonable results out of the ones that exist. We are looking for someone to build and ship: AI features in live games, and the internal tools that give superpowers to Supercellians. Some of that work will take you inside a game or central team for a while, close enough to their craft to build the right thing with them. In our team, you'll work closely with our AI Platform Engineers, AI/ML engineers, Clients Programmers, Cloud Engineers. You’ll also collaborate with other teams including Data, QA, Engine and game teams. What You'll Be Doing Build and ship AI features and systems end to end into live games and internal tools, at production quality and under real deadlines. Do the applied engineering that makes AI work in practice. Own evaluation as a first-class deliverable. Write and maintain the benchmarks, evals, and regression suites that tell you whether something is genuinely good, across the modalities you're working in. Fine-tune, adapt, and distill models where it pays off, and have the judgment to know when a better prompt, better retrieval, or a smaller model beats training anything. Make sound trade-offs on inference, including on-device where it matters, against real parameter, latency, and battery targets, without losing the feel players expect. Take on the harder applied problems, such as making autonomous agents reliable and accurate enough to trust with real work. Work close to game and central teams, sometimes embedded with them for a stretch, and build things that stay in use after you move on. Mentor our more junior AI/ML engineers through code review, pairing, and design discussion, and raise the technical bar around you. Stay at the frontier by reading the literature and following the major conferences, and bring back what is genuinely useful. What You Have Strong, current command of modern generative methods at the applied level: you know what today's models are actually good at, where they break, and how to build reliably on top of them. A track record of shipping LLM or generative AI applications that real users used, in production, not prototypes. We value this far above a publication record. Real software engineering depth. You write code others can maintain, and you own things in production rather than handing them off. items.desc: About The Role An exciting opportunity is available for a Postdoctoral Research Fellow to join the School of Psychology at the University of Sussex and contribute to cutting-edge research on the neural basis of misophonia. This full-time position is available from January 2027 and will run until 30 September 2028. Misophonia is a poorly understood condition in which specific everyday sounds, such as chewing, breathing, or tapping, trigger intense emotional and physiological reactions that can profoundly affect quality of life. This project aims to transform our understanding of misophonia by revealing how the brain processes and represents the acoustic and semantic properties of sounds, and how these neural representations differ between individuals with and without the condition. Working as part of a world-leading research team studying anomalous perceptual experiences, you will contribute to a project funded by the Ream Foundation that combines cognitive neuroscience and advanced neuroimaging methods. The successful candidate will contribute independently to all stages of the project, publish high-quality research, and advance understanding of an important but underexplored condition. About You You will hold a PhD in cognitive neuroscience, psychology, audiology, or a related discipline, with expertise in sensory perception (e.g. hearing or vision), attention, or a closely related area. You will have experience in the acquisition and analysis of EEG data and a strong interest in understanding the neural mechanisms that give rise to perceptual experience. The ideal candidate will be a motivated and collaborative researcher capable of working independently. You will be excited by the opportunity to contribute to an emerging field, work as part of an internationally recognised research team, and help advance our understanding of the cognitive and neural mechanisms underlying misophonia. About Our Faculty Our Psychology school has a rich history extending over half-a-century, marked from the start by our variety of research and courses. From the ground-breaking work of scholars such as Stuart Sutherland and Marie Jahoda, we've grown to cover all areas of psychology. The School was formally established in 2009, bringing together academics across biological, cognitive, developmental, clinical and social psychology into one School. We've now entered the second decade of our existence as one of the largest and most influential academic communities for psychology in the country! Anchored by our core values of kindness, integrity, inclusion, collaboration and courage, our research and teaching address societal challenges to create a better world. Please find further information regarding the School of Psychology. The School of Psychology is proud to hold a Silver Athena Swann Award. Why work here Our university is situated off the A27, next to the beautiful South Downs where you will enjoy everything that our 150-acre campus has to offer. We are accessible by public transport; Falmer train station is a five-minute walk to campus and several bus stops are located within campus. We also have dedicated cycling paths and encourage our staff to use these with our offering of a cycle to work scheme. Sussex is a renowned, multi-accredited, research-led International University and this is only possible because of the people that work here. Whether you are a member of Faculty, part of a Professional Services team or a Student, it’s our people that make us great and we want you to be part of that. Find Out More About Our Reward And Benefits Package. Find out about our equality, diversity and inclusion. Further Key Information Please contact Ediz Sohoglu (E.Sohoglu@sussex.ac.uk) for informal enquiries. The University of Sussex values the diversity of its staff and students, and we welcome applicants from all backgrounds. Please consult our Skilled Worker Visa information page for further information about Visa Sponsorship. The University requires that work undertaken for the University is performed in the UK.

We’re solving hard problems with people we respect - we make the most of our time together, we make it special. We are not another “polished” SF startup . Understand how users interpret interfaces. Study attention, expectations and mental models: what users notice first, what they overlook, and where interfaces conflict with their expectations. items.desc: Research Associate in AI Department : Department of Infectious DiseasesAbout the roleKing’s College London is a world leading research-intensive university with a strong international profile and a long-standing commitment to addressing major societal and global challenges.This role is based within the Faculty of Life Sciences & Medicine, in the School of Immunology & Microbial Science in the Department of Infectious Diseases. Ready to apply Before you do, make sure to read all the details pertaining to this job in the description below. It brings together expertise across microbiology, immunology, clinical sciences, data science and artificial intelligence.The Department offers a highly interdisciplinary and collaborative environment, with strong links to clinical partners and access to outstanding research infrastructure and cross faculty initiatives.About usThis is an exciting project Supported by the BBSRC. Antibiotic resistance (ABR) is one of the biggest public health challenges of our time. In 2019, 1.27 million deaths were attributed to antibiotic resistant bacteria. The gut microbiome is composed of harmless symbionts, commensal bacteria, and opportunistic pathogens, all of which play crucial roles in human and animal health and disease. In physiological conditions the gut microbiome is stable, but when perturbative events occur (e.g., dietary changes, infections, stress, antibiotic administration) the population of microbiota changes, influencing health and protection against further colonisation. These changes may involve new resistant bacteria becoming permanent residents or transferring resistance to the commensals). The core concepts underlying our project are: to gaining a better understanding of how the gut microbiome changes as consequence of infection, co-infection, or treatment (including the development of resistant traits) is a fundamental starting point towards understanding the mechanisms of inception and spread of endemic diseases and antimicrobial resistance.The research associate will be responsible for developing, implementing and applying artificial intelligence, machine learning, deep learning and data-mining methods to address complex research questions. items.desc: Giotto.ai is a Swiss AI research lab, founded in 2017 by EPFL mathematicians. items.desc: THE ROLE The Fundamental Research team at The Alan Turing Institute is advancing Sovereign Language Modelling, developing trusted national capability across the training, adaptation, fine-tuning, distillation, evaluation and assurance of language models. This work aims to strengthen national resilience and support the safe and accountable deployment of AI in areas of public value. We are looking for a Distinguished Scientist, Sovereign Language Modelling to provide scientific and strategic leadership for this high-priority research area. You will shape and lead an ambitious research portfolio spanning compliant data pipelines, model pre-training, reinforcement learning and post-training, advanced distillation, agentic systems and efficient deployment. Leading a multidisciplinary team of researchers and research engineers, you will take research from foundational questions through to demonstrators and deployment, while building partnerships across academia, government and industry. ABOUT YOU You will be an internationally recognised research leader in Natural Language Processing and/or Machine Learning, with deep, hands-on expertise across areas such as model training, reinforcement learning and post-training, distillation and model compression, agentic systems, efficient inference and distributed training. You will bring an outstanding and sustained record of research contributions, alongside experience setting strategic research direction, leading complex collaborations and translating research into real-world impact. We are looking for someone with proven experience leading research software and infrastructure at scale, securing significant external funding and communicating complex technical work to senior, specialist and non-specialist audiences. You will combine hands-on technical expertise with strong scientific leadership, strategic judgement and a commitment to responsible, safe and open AI research. HOW YOU WILL MAKE AN IMPACT Set the scientific direction for Sovereign Language Modelling, defining and developing an ambitious research agenda aligned with Fundamental Research priorities. Build and lead a high-quality research portfolio, taking programmes from foundational research questions through to demonstrators and deployment. Build, lead and mentor multidisciplinary teams of researchers and research engineers, developing technical capability as priorities and partnerships evolve. Provide hands-on scientific leadership, working alongside technical teams and partners to tackle challenging methodological problems, maintain scientific quality and model excellent research practice. Translate research into real-world resilience impact, applying Sovereign Language Modelling research to operational problems, data and constraints, including secure, classified or sensitive environments where required. Develop strategic partnerships and secure resources, building collaborations across academia, government and industry and helping secure the funding, data, compute, facilities and partner commitments needed to deliver the portfolio. Represent the Institute as a senior scientific authority for Sovereign Language Modelling, communicating evidence clearly to partners, boards and research audiences and monitoring emerging developments in the field Please see our portal for a full breakdown of the role. items.desc: Would you like to develop AI-based methods to understand and predict recovery after traumatic brain injury? We welcome applications for a researcher position at Uppsala University. The Department of Medical Sciences is a large clinical institution with more than 250 employees and over 900 additional coworkers connected via the Uppsala University Hospital. The Department of Medical Sciences has a broad research profile with strong research groups in a number of different areas. The research carried out at the department is performed in close connection with the clinical activities at the Uppsala University Hospital, which includes both basic studies on the causes of a variety of illnesses and the development and evaluation of improved diagnostics and new treatment methods. More information about the Department of Medical Sciences can be found at https://www.uu.se/en/department/medical-sciences. The neurotrauma research group at Uppsala University and Uppsala University Hospital conducts clinical and translational research focusing on individual differences in recovery following traumatic brain injury. Our research combines clinical patient data, continuous physiological monitoring from neurocritical care, neuroimaging and advanced data analytics. This project aims to develop and validate AI-based models for dynamic outcome prediction and improved understanding of secondary brain injury, with the long-term goal of supporting personalised care. Duties The position involves developing, implementing and evaluating machine learning and artificial intelligence methods for research data from patients with traumatic brain injury (TBI). Main duties include: Processing and integrating longitudinal clinical data, physiological time series (e.g. ICP, CPP and blood pressure), laboratory data and imaging-derived variables. Developing and externally validating predictive models of clinical outcomes and physiological changes during intensive care. Developing reproducible analytical pipelines, quality assurance, documentation and secure data workflows. Conducting scientific analyses, preparing manuscripts and presenting findings in interdisciplinary collaboration with clinicians and researchers. Requirements PhD in computer science, artificial intelligence, machine learning, bioinformatics or another field relevant to the position. Documented experience developing and evaluating machine learning or deep learning models. Strong Python programming skills and experience with relevant machine learning frameworks, such as PyTorch. Experience in quantitative data analysis and scientific research, including the ability to document and communicate results. Ability to work independently and in interdisciplinary teams, and excellent English communication skills. Additional qualifications Experience in generative artificial intelligence, including diffusion models, synthetic data generation and data augmentation techniques. ⁠Experience in high-performance computing (HPC), GPU acceleration, and the development and optimization of scalable machine learning and deep learning workflows. Experience in computer vision, medical or scientific image analysis, and multimodal machine learning involving heterogeneous data sources. About the employment The employment is 12 months . Scope: full-time . Starting date: as agreed. Placement: Uppsala . For further information about the position, please contact: Elham Rostami, elham.rostami@uu.se . We develop intelligent aquaculture technology for the removal of salmon lice 24/7 using machine vision and laser, as well as monitoring lice levels, measuring fish welfare and growth. Apply science and data to real-world aquaculture challenges We are now looking for a Research Data Scientist to strengthen our Research team and help turn complex biological and operational information into scientific insight and practical applications. Aqua Research builds and shares knowledge across Stingray and the wider aquaculture sector. Your work will contribute directly to creating tools and capabilities used by our customers and employees. Analyzing extensive biological and operational datasets and developing statistical models to identify and evaluate meaningful patterns, relationships, and opportunities for improvement. Defining data requirements and independently retrieving, combining, and quality-assuring large and heterogenous data sets to build reproducible analytical workflows and reusable data pipelines, ensuring traceability and appropriate documentation throughout the process. Interpreting and communicating findings to internal and external audiences, translating complex results into practical insights that support fact-based decision-making and further development. Most importantly, we are looking for someone who enjoys working across disciplines. You can discuss biological hypotheses with scientists, independently investigate the underlying data, and work with software engineers and customer contacts to determine how a promising research method can become a reliable functional capability. A solid understanding of applied research methodology, experimental design, statistical modeling and result validation. items.desc: We're looking for a hands-on engineer to build two foundations of the Tricorder product: the evaluation harness and training data pipeline behind our AI models, and a clinical knowledge base grounded in tactical combat care, SNOMED CT and ICD-10. Most healthcare technology assumes a hospital: reliable power, connectivity and a clinician at a desk. Care increasingly happens somewhere else - in the field, in transit, in remote and contested environments, and in the critical minutes before a patient reaches a ward. Tricorder builds the deployable clinical infrastructure for that world: a rugged, self-contained hardware and software platform that lets clinical teams capture, monitor and act on patient data anywhere, even when the network or the grid can't be relied on. It is a dual-use venture serving defence medical and civilian pre-hospital care. Our prototype product is already in user testing. Edge AI sits at the core: multimodal language models that turn video, sensor data and clinical notes into patient records, drive predictions and inform data-driven learnings across deployments. To trust those models in the field, we need rigorous data and evaluation - that's where you come in. What you'll do You'll own two workstreams, working day to day with the founder and the FF build team. 1. Data pipeline and evaluation harness Build the data foundations that tell us whether our models are good enough for clinical use. Data labelling: design labelling schemas and guidelines, set up tooling, and run labelling with clinical input, including quality checks and inter-annotator agreement. Data processing: build reproducible pipelines to ingest, clean, de-identify and transform multimodal data (video, sensor streams, text). Video data organisation: structure, version and catalogue video datasets so clips, annotations and metadata stay searchable and traceable. Training dataset preparation: assemble balanced, well-documented train, validation and test splits, with clear lineage from raw data to model input. Eval harness: build an automated harness that benchmarks vision-language and NLP models against clinically meaningful metrics, tracks regressions and supports build-vs-buy model decisions. 2. Clinical knowledge base Build the structured clinical knowledge base that turns unstructured input into coded, interoperable records. Database design: design the schema and stand up the data store for clinical concepts and their relationships. Clinical terminologies: ingest and map TC3, SNOMED CT, ICD-10 and related NHS standards, including cross-mappings between them. Natural language processing: extract entities and relationships from clinical text and link them to coded concepts. Document handling: parse and structure clinical documents (PDFs, notes, forms) into the database. Clinical knowledge: work with clinicians to make sure the database reflects real-world clinical reasoning and pre-hospital workflows. By the end of the first 3 months, we'd expect a working eval harness in use for model decisions, a labelled and versioned core dataset, and a first version of the knowledge base linked to the product. What we're looking for We don't expect one person to be expert in everything below. Strong candidates will be deep in one workstream and credible in the other. Must-haves Strong Python and data engineering skills, with a track record of shipping production data or ML pipelines, not just research notebooks. Hands-on experience building ML evaluation frameworks, benchmarks or test harnesses, ideally for vision, video or language models. Experience running data labelling and training-data preparation, including annotation tooling and quality control. Working knowledge of databases and data modelling. Practical NLP experience: entity extraction, entity linking or document parsing. Comfort handling sensitive data under data protection and clinical safety constraints. Pragmatism and speed: you can work with ambiguity, make good build-vs-buy calls and ship in weeks, not quarters. Nice to have Experience with SNOMED CT, ICD-10, dm+d or other NHS clinical terminologies and coding. A background in health-tech, clinical informatics or another regulated domain such as defence. Experience with video data at scale (frame sampling, temporal annotation, multimodal datasets). Familiarity with FHIR or HL7 interoperability standards. Experience working with LLMs and VLMs, including edge or on-device deployment. Early-stage startup experience, especially as a founding or early engineer. Probably not the right fit if You need detailed specs and a large team around you to be effective. You prefer pure research over building tools people use every day. This is a high urgency opening, and we are flexible to consider applicants either on a more flexible consultancy agreement (rolling by mutual agreement, with a competitive day rate); or a long term permanent employment contract with shares as part of the package and scope to grow into a longer-term …

items.desc: Location: Munich Type: Full-time The Role: We’re partnering with an ambitious robotics start-up developing autonomous warehouse robots that are already operating in live customer environments. With a growing fleet and increasing demand, the business is expanding its research and engineering capabilities to bring advanced robotic manipulation into real-world production. We’re looking for a Research Engineer specialising in Reinforcement Learning (RL) and robotic manipulation to develop policies that enable robots to perform precise, contact-rich tasks. You’ll work across simulation, control and real-world deployment, training policies in large-scale simulated environments before transferring them onto physical robotic systems. This is a hands-on research role where your work moves beyond experimentation. You’ll tackle genuine customer use cases, work directly with deployed hardware and iterate against real-world feedback. The objective is to turn cutting-edge research into reliable robotic capabilities that can be rolled out across an expanding fleet. Key Responsibilities Reinforcement Learning: Develop and train RL policies for precise robotic manipulation, including contact-rich tasks that require accurate force, position and motion control. Simulation & Sim-to-Real: Build and scale simulation-based training environments, transferring learned policies to physical robots and addressing the challenges of sim-to-real generalisation. Robot Control: Combine reinforcement learning with classical control methods and learned controllers to improve precision, robustness and operational safety. Policy Optimisation: Design experiments, evaluate performance and refine policies against real-world task requirements and deployment constraints. Simulation Infrastructure: Work with modern robotics simulation frameworks to support large-scale training, testing and evaluation. Real-World Deployment: Integrate successful policies into the robotics autonomy stack and validate their performance on deployed hardware. Applied Research: Translate emerging techniques in robotic learning into practical capabilities, balancing research innovation with reliability and production readiness. Skills & Experience Hands-on experience developing reinforcement learning methods for robotic control and manipulation. Experience training policies in simulation and deploying them on physical robotic hardware. Strong understanding of sim-to-real transfer, including domain randomisation, system dynamics and policy generalisation. Experience with large-scale robotics simulation environments such as NVIDIA Isaac Sim, Isaac Lab, MuJoCo or equivalent. Strong foundations in robotics, control theory, dynamics and motion planning. Proficiency in Python and modern machine learning frameworks, with the ability to develop robust, production-quality research code. Evidence of practical research output, such as deployed robotic policies, open-source projects or relevant academic publications. Ability to work experimentally, diagnose failure modes and iterate quickly between simulation and real-world testing. Desirable Experience Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models and learning-based robotic manipulation. Imitation learning, behavioural cloning or learning from demonstrations. Code-as-Policy approaches to robotic task execution. Experience with real-world robotic arms and contact-rich manipulation. A PhD in robotics, machine learning, computer science or a related field, supported by a strong research track record. Publications at leading robotics and machine learning conferences, including ICRA, CoRL, ICLR or CVPR. The Opportunity Work on physical AI systems already deployed in real customer environments. Take ownership of the full research-to-deployment lifecycle, from simulation and policy training through to real-world execution. Solve challenging manipulation problems with direct commercial relevance. Work at the intersection of reinforcement learning, robot control and autonomous systems. See research translated into operational capabilities on a short development cycle. How to Apply We’re particularly interested in candidates who can demonstrate their work beyond a CV. When applying, include a link to a trained policy running on a real robot, a relevant research paper or an open-source repository showcasing your technical contributions.

items.desc: Research Associate in Human-Robot Interaction Department : EngineeringAbout usWe are recruiting a motivated Postdoctoral Research Associate to join CO-STAR (CO-designing Socially inTelligent Assistive Robots for Future Healthcare), a research programme bringing together King’s College London, Guy’s and St Thomas’ NHS Foundation Trust, and the Royal Academy of Engineering. Check all associated application documentation thoroughly before clicking on the apply button at the bottom of this description. CO-STAR aims to advance socially intelligent assistive robots for future healthcare, combining cutting-edge research in artificial intelligence and robotics with human-centred co-design and real-world clinical deployment. We are looking for a candidate who can join the project in January 2027 or soon thereafter.The successful candidate will join the Department of Engineering at King’s College London and become a member of the Social AI & Robotics Lab (SAIR), led by Dr Oya Celiktutan. They will work closely with researchers, engineers, healthcare professionals, patients and other stakeholders at Guy’s and St Thomas’ NHS Foundation Trust (GSTT), providing a unique opportunity to conduct cutting-edge robotics research in close partnership with a major NHS organisation.SAIR conducts research in multimodal machine learning and human-centred embodied AI, with a particular focus on developing autonomous agents that can perceive, understand and interact effectively with humans. The lab’s research addresses challenges in multimodal perception, human behaviour understanding and forecasting, robot learning, navigation and manipulation, and socially aware human–robot interaction.SAIR’s research has been supported by the Royal Academy of Engineering, EPSRC, the Royal Society, and EU Horizon programmes, as well as through industrial collaborations. The lab’s research has received several distinctions, including the Best Paper Award at IEEE RO-MAN 2022, the NVIDIA CCS Best Student Paper Award Runner-Up at IEEE FG 2021, and First Place and Honourable Mention Awards at the ICCV UDIVA Challenge 2021. About the roleImagine a future where robots meaningfully assist people with limited mobility and support patients and clinicians across healthcare environments. Assistive robotics has the potential to transform independence, wellbeing, and the delivery of care. Advances in AI are rapidly expanding what robots can perceive, understand, and do, bringing this future closer than ever. Yet a critical gap remains between technical capability and real-world deployment: robots still struggle to understand human behaviour, adapt to complex social situations, and operate safely and appropriately alongside people. Using the hospital as a living lab to advance human–robot interaction and integration with clinical workflows, the CO-STAR project aims to bridge this gap.CO-STAR will engineer the next generation of socially intelligent assistive robots that can interact naturally with people while meeting the demands of real-world healthcare environments. The successful candidate will play a key role in shaping and delivering the research programme, working across human–robot interaction, machine learning, socially intelligent AI, and healthcare robotics. They will contribute to the design, development, and evaluation of robotic and AI systems and work closely with the multidisciplinary CO-STAR team and Guy’s and St Thomas’ NHS Foundation Trust to translate research advances into real-world healthcare settings. Please refer to the Job Description for further details about the role and the required application documents.The successful candidate will be expected to:shape and conduct high-quality multidisciplinary research in collaboration with the CO-STAR project team;develop novel research in human–robot interaction, machine learning, and socially intelligent robotics;contribute to the design, development, implementation, and evaluation of robotic and AI systems within the scope of the project;disseminate research findings through high-quality publications and presentations at leading international conferences and journals;contribute to activities that maximise the academic, clinical, and societal impact of the research.This is a full-time, fixed-term post for 21 months, with the potential for extension up to a total of 42 months, subject to funding arrangements. items.desc: Rejoignez les activités Advanced Computing d’ANEO ANEO est un cabinet de conseil tech-first qui accompagne depuis plus de vingt ans des entreprises du CAC 40, des ETI et des start-up dans leurs transformations technologiques et organisationnelles. Notre singularité : intervenir à la croisée du calcul scientifique, du software, du HPC, du cloud, de l’IA et des systèmes distribués. Cette annonce ne correspond pas à un poste unique. Elle constitue une porte d’entrée vers les activités Advanced Computing d’ANEO, pour des profils techniques aux parcours et aux niveaux d’expérience variés. Nos équipes conçoivent, modernisent et industrialisent des plateformes et des applications de calcul complexes. Nous intervenons de la compréhension du besoin jusqu’au passage à l’échelle : architecture, optimisation, migration vers le cloud, mise en production et exploitation de workloads critiques. Cette expertise se prolonge avec ArmoniK, notre orchestrateur open source de calcul distribué, conçu pour exécuter des workloads intensifs dans des environnements on-premise, cloud et hybrides. Quelques projets représentatifs Plateformes IA hybrides et multi-GPU : Concevoir et industrialiser une plateforme capable de gérer l’entraînement distribué de modèles sur plusieurs GPU, avec des enjeux de performance, de scalabilité, de robustesse et de mise en production. Migration et bursting HPC vers le cloud : Faire évoluer une plateforme de calcul afin d’absorber des pics de charge dans le cloud, tout en maîtrisant les coûts, la résilience et l’exploitation des workloads. Optimisation de codes scientifiques : Améliorer les performances de codes de calcul sur CPU et GPU dans des environnements massivement parallèles, en travaillant sur le profilage, la parallélisation et l’utilisation des accélérateurs. Calcul distribué et ArmoniK : Contribuer au développement d’ArmoniK et à l’orchestration de workloads intensifs entre environnements on-premise, cloud public, cloud souverain et multi-cloud. Ces projets illustrent la diversité des sujets traités chez ANEO : développement scientifique, architecture, infrastructure, cloud, systèmes distribués, plateformes IA et passage à l’échelle. Selon les missions, vous pourrez travailler avec des chercheurs, des développeurs, des équipes data science, des experts infrastructure et cloud, des métiers et des décideurs. Si vous souhaitez en savoir plus, c’est ici . Les profils que nous souhaitons rencontrer Nous sommes ouverts à des parcours variés : jeunes docteurs et post-doctorants souhaitant appliquer leur expertise à des problématiques industrielles ; ingénieurs et développeurs scientifiques ; spécialistes du HPC, du GPU, du cloud ou des infrastructures de calcul ; experts des plateformes IA et des systèmes distribués ; architectes et leaders techniques capables de porter des choix structurants. Vous n’avez pas besoin de maîtriser l’ensemble de ces domaines. Nous recherchons avant tout une expertise ou un potentiel technique réel, de la curiosité et l’envie de comprendre des systèmes complexes dans leur globalité. Votre périmètre, votre niveau d’autonomie et vos responsabilités seront définis en fonction de votre expérience, de vos aspirations et des opportunités identifiées. Ce qui fera la différence Au-delà de votre expertise technique, nous recherchons des personnes capables de comprendre avant de proposer, d’expliquer clairement leurs choix et de construire avec les équipes et les clients. Une expérience du conseil est un plus, pas un prérequis. Un anglais professionnel est attendu. La maîtrise parfaite du français n’est pas indispensable à votre arrivée, dès lors que la communication est fluide. Informations pratiques Contrat : CDI Localisation : Boulogne-Billancourt Organisation du travail : hybride Prise de poste : à partir de 2027 Les candidatures sont étudiées tout au long de l’année. Certaines opportunités correspondent à des besoins immédiats ; d’autres peuvent se construire en fonction de votre expertise, de votre projet professionnel et de votre disponibilité. Vous terminez une thèse, un post-doctorat ou un projet structurant ? Nous pouvons commencer à échanger dès maintenant. Parcours de recrutement Le parcours est adapté à votre niveau d’expérience et au type de contribution envisagé. Il comprend généralement : un premier échange avec l’équipe recrutement ; une rencontre technique avec un membre de la communauté Advanced Computing ; un échange de projection sur votre parcours et votre place chez ANEO. Chez ANEO, chacun et chacune a sa place. Nous recrutons dans le respect de l’égalité des chances.

items.desc: Het handmatig invullen van pensioenformulieren is niet alleen foutgevoelig, maar ook inefficiënt. In deze opdracht ga je een mobiele app ontwikkelen die gegevens uit documenten automatisch scant en invoert met behulp van multimodale AI. Je werkt een Proof of Concept uit waarin je de functionaliteit van de app en de bescherming van persoonsgegevens demonstreert. Hierbij leg je de nadruk op het ontwikkelen van een gebruiksvriendelijke en privacy vriendelijke oplossing. Deze afstudeeropdracht maakt onderdeel uit van het project ‘Van GRIJSpensioen naar GROENpensioen’. Met dit project geven we de pensioenwereld een digitale boost door het optimaliseren van digitale infrastructuren en processen. Zo maken we pensioenfondsen efficiënter en duurzamer, met beter datamanagement, sterke privacybescherming en gepersonaliseerde dienstverlening. Het handmatig overnemen van gegevens uit identiteitsdocumenten, werkgeversverklaringen en financiële overzichten naar pensioenformulieren is niet alleen monotoon en saai, maar ook foutgevoelig en inefficiënt. Fouten kunnen leiden tot onjuiste pensioenopbouw en -uitkeringen, met mogelijk aanzienlijke financiële gevolgen voor de betrokkenen. Daarnaast is het essentieel om de privacy van pensioengegevens te waarborgen, aangezien deze gevoelige financiële en persoonlijke informatie bevatten die beschermd moet worden tegen ongeautoriseerde toegang en datalekken. De opdracht Ontwikkel een mobiele applicatie die gebruikmaakt van multimodale AI om het invullen van pensioenformulieren te automatiseren. Dit doe je door documenten te scannen met de camera van een smartphone en de relevante informatie automatisch in het formulier te plaatsen. De applicatie moet zowel gebruiksvriendelijk als privacy vriendelijk zijn, met een sterke focus op de beveiliging van persoonsgegevens. Jouw taak is om een Proof of Concept te ontwikkelen dat niet alleen de functionaliteit demonstreert, maar ook hoe de applicatie de privacy van de gebruiker waarborgt. Over Info Support Info Support is specialist in maatwerksoftware, data/AI solutions, beheer en trainingen en actief in de sectoren Finance, Industry, Agriculture, Food & Retail, Mobility & Public en Healthcare. Wij bieden solide en innovatieve oplossingen voor complexe en bedrijfkritische softwarevraagstukken. Onze hoofdkantoren zijn gevestigd in Veenendaal (NL) en Mechelen (BE). Op dit moment zijn er circa 500 medewerkers bij Info Support in dienst. De werkwijze van Info Support kenmerkt zich door een aantal kernwaarden: soliditeit, integriteit, vakmanschap en passie. Deze kernwaarden zijn verweven in ons werk en de manier waarop we met elkaar omgaan. Om te zorgen dat alle medewerkers altijd op de hoogte kunnen zijn van de nieuwste ontwikkelingen beschikt Info Support over een inhouse IT Academy waar graag wordt voldaan aan de honger naar meer of andere kennis en vaardigheden. Om deze opdracht te kunnen doen is B2-taalvaardigheid in het Nederlands vereist.

items.title: Quantitative / Machine Learning Engineer
items.card: you will join a highly technical and collaborative environment at the intersection of energy trading, quantitative modelling, machine learning and software engineering . You will contribute directly to the development of models and algorithms used to identify and capture opportunities in European power markets, working closely with quantitative analysts, algorithmic traders, data scientists and IT specialists. The
items.desc: Contexte et environnement TotalEnergies is developing its activities across the power value chain, with a growing portfolio of renewable generation, flexible assets and power supply activities across Europe. Within Trading & Shipping, our algorithmic trading teams are building advanced quantitative and machine-learning solutions to support trading and optimization activities in European short-term power markets. As a Quantitative / Machine Learning Engineer , you will join a highly technical and collaborative environment at the intersection of energy trading, quantitative modelling, machine learning and software engineering . You will contribute directly to the development of models and algorithms used to identify and capture opportunities in European power markets, working closely with quantitative analysts, algorithmic traders, data scientists and IT specialists. The role offers significant exposure to fast-moving energy markets and the opportunity to work on models that move from research and back-testing through to live production and ultimately contribute to trading performance. Activités As part of the Algorithmic Trading team, you will: Develop quantitative and machine-learning models supporting algorithmic trading strategies in European power markets. Build models across the full lifecycle, from data preparation and feature engineering through model training, optimization, validation and live deployment. Design new indicators, signals and features to improve quantitative and machine-learning trading models. Analyse large and complex datasets to identify patterns, relationships and trading signals. Conduct quantitative research on European power markets and translate market observations into actionable modelling ideas. Monitor the performance and robustness of models in both simulated and live trading environments. Continuously assess model behaviour and identify opportunities to improve forecasting accuracy and trading performance. Contribute to rigorous back-testing, validation and model-performance methodologies. Work with cross-functional teams to bring models into production and ensure their reliability, scalability and maintainability. Collaborate closely with algorithmic traders and technology teams to turn quantitative research into operational trading solutions. Contribute your data science expertise to broader modelling and optimization topics within the team. Profil du candidat You have a strong quantitative background and enjoy applying advanced modelling techniques to complex, real-world problems. We are looking for someone with: An engineering degree, Master's degree or PhD in a quantitative field such as Mathematics, Physics, Machine Learning, Computer Science or a related discipline. Approximately 2–3 years of professional experience working with machine-learning models in production, ideally involving live forecasting or other real-time applications. Strong proficiency in Python. Experience with MongoDB, SQL and Shell scripting. A solid understanding of software architecture and production-quality development practices. Experience with Docker and familiarity with DevOps/MLOps environments, including CI/CD pipelines. Strong knowledge of machine-learning techniques, including supervised and unsupervised learning. Practical experience with time-series modelling and analysis. The ability to analyse complex systems and identify direct and indirect relationships between multiple signals and datasets. Strong communication skills and the ability to explain quantitative results clearly to both technical and business stakeholders. The ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, collaborative trading environment. Additional Assets The following would be considered an advantage: Previous exposure to energy, commodities or financial markets. Understanding of European power markets, power generation or energy supply mechanisms. Experience working with trading signals, forecasting models or optimization problems. Familiarity with project-management and collaborative tools such as Jira, Asana or Monday.com. Why Join Us? This role offers the opportunity to work at the forefront of data science and algorithmic trading within the energy sector . You will work on advanced quantitative models with a direct connection to live markets and trading decisions, while collaborating with experienced professionals across trading, quantitative research and technology. You will join an international environment where machine learning and quantitative analysis play an increasingly important role in optimizing TotalEnergies' activities across European power markets.

items.card: You will bridge systems operations and academic inquiry: keep the infrastructure performant and reliable through daily operations while contributing to research on cloud architectures, virtualization, AI-driven operations (AIOps) and software execution environments. You will use operational challenges to inform research, and hands-on experiments and prototypes to evaluate new system concepts. The role calls for
items.desc:
Join our Team
 About the Opportunity 
The Lund section of Research Area Compute and Software is a team of 11 working on distributed systems, reliability, real-time computing and standardization. We operate a state-of-the-art OpenStack cloud and compute environment used around the clock by hundreds of Ericsson and academic users. It is both a reliable service and our primary research testbed.
You will bridge systems operations and academic inquiry: keep the infrastructure performant and reliable through daily operations while contributing to research on cloud architectures, virtualization, AI-driven operations (AIOps) and software execution environments. You will use operational challenges to inform research, and hands-on experiments and prototypes to evaluate new system concepts. The role calls for practical engineering, debugging and active systems management alongside scientific curiosity—not theory alone.
 What You Will Do 
• Operate and evolve the OpenStack cloud and compute environment used by Ericsson and academic researchers.
• Troubleshoot complex distributed systems, investigate root causes, and help ensure reliable services.
• Design, prototype and evaluate system concepts, software execution environments, performance and reliability.
• Contribute to and drive research studies in compute systems, cloud architectures, virtualization and AIOps, including collaboration on scientific publications.
• Automate repetitive tasks, improve workflows and scale infrastructure; work across operations, engineering and research to turn practical challenges into real-world solutions.
 The Skills You Bring 
• A research-oriented degree, such as a Ph.D., or equivalent experience in a research-intensive role.
• Demonstrated research contribution in compute, cloud virtualization or software systems, for example through publications, patents, technical reports or working prototypes.
• Hands-on Linux administration and systems engineering experience, with a solid understanding of cloud technologies, Kubernetes, data-center operations and networking fundamentals.
• Experience with containers (Docker or Podman) and orchestration with Kubernetes.
• Ability to research, instrument and maintain compute environments with AI capabilities supporting workflows, monitoring and intelligent observability.
• A hands-on “doer” mindset; analytical and scientific curiosity; strong troubleshooting and root-cause analysis; and a drive to automate and improve workflows.
• Strong collaboration skills across operational, engineering and research teams.
• It is an advantage to bring or develop skills in Ansible, Terraform or Helm; advanced OpenStack operations; HPC or accelerators (GPUs, DPUs or FPGAs); and research collaboration or patenting processes.

items.title: Researcher Sorting Technologies & AI for Circular Plastics
items.card: responsibilities Design, execute and optimize experiments using NIR-HSI, RGB imaging, 3D sensing and automated sorting systems. Develop and validate machine learning, chemometric and data analytics models for material classification and process optimization. Analyze complex datasets and translate findings into practical solutions for industry. Develop and improve data acquisition, processing and visualization tools.
items.desc: We are looking for a driven and innovative researcher with expertise in plastics recycling and sorting technologies, combined with strong capabilities in AI, machine learning, optical sensing and data-driven process optimization. NTCP is a dynamic, forward‑thinking applied research organisation leading the way in circular plastics. From our bold and colourful facility in Heerenveen, the Netherlands, we run unique industrial-scale setups that support independent R&D across the full plastics lifecycle – from product characteristics and post‑consumer collection to sorting, washing, mechanical and chemical recycling, and finally new product creation. We hold a strong position in the plastics recycling landscape, backed by a broad network of partners spanning waste management, FMCG brands, universities, NGOs, technology providers, polymer and chemical producers, water‑treatment specialists, and government bodies. Our strength lies in our rare combination of sensor‑equipped industrial‑scale sorting and washing lines, pilot setups for decontamination, pyrolysis and extrusion, a dedicated laboratory, and - most importantly - a team of around 25 experts. We are looking for a driven and innovative researcher with expertise in plastics recycling and sorting technologies, combined with strong capabilities in AI, machine learning, optical sensing and data-driven process optimization. Researcher Sorting Technologies & AI for Circular Plastics Key responsibilities Design, execute and optimize experiments using NIR-HSI, RGB imaging, 3D sensing and automated sorting systems. Develop and validate machine learning, chemometric and data analytics models for material classification and process optimization. Analyze complex datasets and translate findings into practical solutions for industry. Develop and improve data acquisition, processing and visualization tools. Execute and lead R&D projects in sorting technologies, optical sensors and AI-driven material identification. Present results to customers, partners and scientific audiences. Identify new research opportunities and contribute to proposals and innovation projects. What you bring BSc or MSc degree in Engineering, Materials Science, Experimental Physics, or a related field, with at least 2-3 years of relevant industrial R&D experience. Hands-on experience with optical sensing technologies (NIR-HSI, RGB vision and/or 3D imaging systems), and/or machine learning, chemometric and computer vision applications (e.g. YOLO, PLS-DA). Strong proficiency in Python programming and data analytics, with the ability to develop data-driven insights and solutions for industrial applications. Experience with software development, data platforms, sensor data processing and visualization tools is a plus. Ability to understand industrial challenges and translate them into research questions, project plans and innovative solutions. Strong passion for and affinity with plastics recycling and circular economy. Excellent communication skills in English (written and spoken); knowledge of Dutch is an advantage but not required. Eligibility to work in the Netherlands. What we offer We offer the opportunity to work in a creative and innovative environment where your work makes a real impact on the circular use of resources. You will work on innovative national and international R&D projects together with leading industrial and academic partners. Depending on project objectives, you will have opportunities to publish results and present your work at conferences, workshops and industry events. NTCP is committed to fostering an inclusive working environment where everyone has equal opportunities to grow, develop, and be themselves. Benefits Salary aligned with the responsibilities of the role and the candidate’s level of expertise A one-year contract, with outlook on a permanent position 25 leave days plus national holidays with a possibility to purchase 5 additional days Commuter allowance. Interested? Please apply by sending your CV and motivation letter (in English) to Martine Brandsma (Director at NTCP): mbrandsma@ntcp.nl and Marjon Claes ( mclaes@ntcp.nl ). For further information, feel free to contact Martine directly.

items.card: The role will involve both theoretical research and practical implementation, leveraging access to quantum hardware platforms. This is a unique opportunity to contribute to cutting-edge quantum research while applying quantum algorithms on real devices, helping to push the boundaries of what is possible with near-term quantum computing. items.desc: Phasecraft is the quantum algorithms company. We are building the mathematical foundations for quantum computing applications that solve real-world problems. Founded in 2019 by Toby Cubitt, Ashley Montanaro and John Morton, we are based in London and Bristol in the UK and opened an office in Washington DC in 2024, led by Steve Flammia. In 2025 we completed a $34m Series B funding round co-led by Plural, existing investor Playground Global, and Novo Holdings’ Quantum Fund in its first direct quantum software investment. Phasecraft’s unprecedented access to today’s best quantum computers – through partnerships with Google, IBM, Quantinuum and QuEra – provides us with unique opportunities to develop foundational IP, inform the development of next-generation quantum hardware, and accelerate commercialization of high-value breakthroughs. We are looking to hire a Quantum Algorithms Scientist to join our team, in a role focusing on implementing and executing experiments on cutting-edge quantum computing hardware. The ideal candidate will have experience in implementing quantum algorithms on real quantum hardware, in addition to exposure to the theory of quantum algorithms for gate-model quantum computers or related topics in quantum computing theory, quantum information theory, or related areas of quantum theory. Their work will contribute to Phasecraft’s goal of developing quantum algorithms for near-term quantum computers and may encompass topics such as algorithm optimization and design, quantum error-correction, resource analysis, error mitigation, and hardware benchmarking. The role will involve both theoretical research and practical implementation, leveraging access to quantum hardware platforms. This is a unique opportunity to contribute to cutting-edge quantum research while applying quantum algorithms on real devices, helping to push the boundaries of what is possible with near-term quantum computing. Requirements Job Description Develop and implement quantum algorithms on state-of-the-art quantum hardware platforms, optimizing performance and resource usage. Undertake both theoretical and applied research on near-term quantum computing algorithms, applications, and enabling technologies. Contribute to research on error mitigation, circuit optimization, and benchmarking techniques for quantum hardware. Help to author publications, presentations, patent applications, and similar research outputs. Work collaboratively in a small international team made up of full-time staff and affiliated PhD students. Contribute to the broader growth and success of Phasecraft through research, development, and technical leadership. Essential Criteria Expertise in quantum algorithms and quantum information theory with a strong foundation in quantum computing. PhD (or soon to receive one) in quantum information, quantum computation, computer science, physics, or a closely related field. Extensive experience in implementing quantum algorithms on quantum hardware. Strong understanding of quantum circuit design, compilation, and optimization techniques. Ability to work independently on research projects while contributing to a collaborative team environment. Strong publication track record in relevant disciplines. Proficiency in quantum programming languages such as Qiskit, Cirq, PennyLane, or similar. Flexibility to work across different aspects of quantum software, algorithms, and underpinning theory. Desirable Criteria Experience in developing and/or benchmarking error mitigation techniques for quantum algorithms. Knowledge of classical simulation methods for quantum circuits and hybrid quantum-classical approaches. Strong software development skills, including experience with Python, C++, or other programming languages used in quantum computing. Experience working with industrial quantum hardware providers or in industry-academic collaborations. Enthusiasm for learning, research, and translating theoretical quantum computing advances into practical applications. Excellent communication skills, with the ability to present complex concepts to diverse audiences. The closing date for applications is 8 November 2026.

items.desc: Imagine working with cutting-edge machine learning models, crunching high frequency data sets and sparring with exceptional and fun colleagues, all while taking part in scaling our business even further. Does this sound highly appealing to you? Then you might be our new Machine Learning Researcher at Alipes. At Alipes, we have been the market leader in automating the financial markets since we started back in 2008, shaping a fully automatic natural language processing system for reading and interpreting financial news. To accomplish our mission of being the best at what we do, we understand the importance of elevating our predictive modeling standards to the highest levels. Your work will involve leading the efforts in creating a world class modeling workflow, enabling the team to seamlessly turn massive data sets of financial information into mathematical models that accurately predict movements in the financial markets. In doing so, you will get a chance to tackle a variety of software infrastructure challenges, such as: Development and optimization of calibration and benchmarking frameworks Building out and implementing best practices for data preparation and dataset generation pipelines Prototyping and releasing novel predictive architectures, especially with respect to time-series models. You will get instant validation of your work and experience short feedback cycles, where going from inception to deployment can be a matter of hours. There will be no red tape to cut and no sales people to consult. About the team All of this will happen in an informal atmosphere where technical discussions are valued, and you are encouraged to take ownership of, and pride in, your work. You will impact the direction of the team, prioritize your work and choose the tools that get the job done. We are a tight-knit modeling team with fourteen passionate quantitative researchers covering 6 nationalities – eleven PhD’s and three MSc’s with expertise in statistical analysis, mathematical modeling and machine learning. We enjoy collaboration and are always willing to lend a helping hand. We are working alongside two other teams of software developers and traders that implement and conceive the mathematical models together with us. What makes this constellation work great is that all of the individual team members write code and understand that a seemingly trivial change can actually require a lot of work, and vice versa. About you Fluency within mathematics and statistics. Experience working with the full Machine Learning stack from data generation through model calibration and real-life validation and monitoring. Programming experience with Python, in particular data-wrangling and numerical programming. Proficiency with computer science fundamentals. A scientific and inquisitive mind. Nice to have Experience working with ‘out-of-core’ datasets. Experience working with tools like PyTorch, Tensorflow, XGBoost and/or Catboost. Programming experience with languages like C# and C/C++. PhD or MSc degree in engineering, physics, computer science, mathematics or economics. What we can offer you Competitive benefits, including pension, health insurance, and 30 days of vacation. A modern, harbour front office in Copenhagen (Nordhavn) with a flexible hybrid work model. A flat hierarchy with high levels of trust, autonomy, and freedom to make decisions. A valued role with unique responsibilities and plenty of room for creativity. Fast feedback and recognition of your contributions in a high-growth company. Strong team spirit - successes are celebrated with company events and trips. Practicalities To apply, please send us your CV and, in lieu of providing a cover letter, concisely answer the questions on the application. If your profile looks like a good match, we will get in touch to coordinate an online technical test as a first step in the interview process. Should you have questions about the role that you would like clarified before applying, you're welcome to send an email to quant_jobs@alipescapital.com. Please note that applications should not be sent to the email address but rather via the job link.

items.desc: At Corsearch, we are dedicated to creating a world where consumers can trust the choices they make. As a global leader in Trademark and Brand Protection, we partner with businesses to safeguard their most valuable assets in an increasingly complex digital environment. Our comprehensive solutions, powered by AI-driven data and deep analytics, enable brands to establish, monitor, and protect their presence against infringement and counterfeiting. Why Choose Corsearch? Innovative Solutions: We combine cutting-edge technology with expert judgment to deliver market-leading services in trademark clearance, brand protection, and anti-counterfeiting. Global Impact: Trusted by over 5,000 customers worldwide, including 73 of Fortune's Top 100 companies, our work has a meaningful impact on businesses and consumers alike. Collaborative Culture: With a team of over 1,900 professionals across multiple global offices, you'll be joining an inclusive environment where diverse perspectives thrive. Mission-Driven Purpose: Our commitment to protecting consumers and their trust in brands drives everything we do, making Corsearch a force for good in the world. ✅The Role As an ML Engineer you’ll play a crucial role in advancing our shared mission of protecting and enhancing the world’s most valuable brands. You will design and optimize AI models that power our state-of-the-art image search engine and other innovative solutions. Collaborating with Corsearch’s global team of data scientists, engineers, and brand protection experts, you’ll help drive innovation in brand protection and online content monitoring , ensuring our clients stay ahead in a rapidly evolving digital landscape. ✅Responsibilities And Duties Develop and optimize machine learning models with a focus on computer vision (e.g., image recognition, object detection) and NLP (e.g., text classification, sentiment analysis, entity recognition). Train and fine-tune deep learning models (e.g., CNNs, RNNs, Transformers) for tasks such as reverse image search, image-text matching, and online content analysis. Collaborate with cross-functional teams to improve product and system performance. Research and implement state-of-the-art algorithms and techniques to improve the accuracy and performance of AI solutions. Build scalable data pipelines for the ingestion and processing of image and text data for model training and evaluation. Continuously monitor the performance of models in production, identify bottlenecks, and propose optimizations. ✅Essential Proven experience as a Machine Learning Engineer with at least 3 years of professional experience. Strong proficiency in machine learning frameworks such as CatBoost, TensorFlow, PyTorch, or Keras. Experience with image processing, feature extraction, and text preprocessing techniques. Solid understanding of algorithms for tasks such as object detection, image classification, text extraction, and sentiment analysis. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to translate business challenges into technical solutions. Full professional English proficiency Corsearch is an equal opportunity and inclusive employer and does not tolerate discrimination of any kind. Your code will run on every device that uses Apple Intelligence — and the bar for correctness, performance, and privacy is set accordingly. You will be a key
items.desc:
The Private Cloud Compute (PCC) team builds Apple's privacy-preserving cloud inference platform — the system that lets generative-AI features on iPhone, iPad, Mac, and Vision Pro reach into the cloud without compromising user privacy. We are looking for a Software Engineer to join the team that builds the on-device client side of that pipeline: the system frameworks and sandboxed services that every Apple Intelligence and Foundation Models request flows through before it ever leaves the device.
This is system-level Apple platform work. You will design and ship the Swift frameworks that turn high-level inference requests into a compact wire protocol, manage long-lived connections, stream multimodal output back to client apps - all under strict process isolation and privacy guarantees. Your code will run on every device that uses Apple Intelligence — and the bar for correctness, performance, and privacy is set accordingly.
You will be a key contributor to the Swift frameworks and XPC services that connect on-device apps and system daemons to PCC. Day-to-day responsibilities include:
Designing and evolving the on-device client SDKs and the XPC services they sit behind, balancing API ergonomics for client teams with the strict process-isolation and attestation guarantees required by PCC.
Implementing high-throughput, low-latency request paths: protobuf serialization of inference payloads, payload compression, multi-turn session state and lifecycle, retry/cancellation semantics, and streaming of incremental model output back to clients.
Owning concurrency and resource management across async/await, AsyncStream, and GCD — including correct cancellation, back-pressure, and lifetime management of long-lived XPC connections.
Building the telemetry, signposts, and privacy-audited logging that let on-call engineers diagnose request failures across device, cloud, and inference layers without exposing user data.
Collaborating closely with the PCC server-side, Foundation Models, attestation, and platform-frameworks teams; writing design documents, leading reviews, and mentoring engineers on Apple platform fundamentals.
Profiling on real hardware with Instruments and driving down memory, latency, and energy costs in the request path — these libraries run on every device, on every inference, so every microsecond matters.
Experience developing complex, system-level frameworks, daemons, or background services for iOS and macOS (beyond standard UI-focused app development).
Strong programming proficiency in Swift, alongside experience with Objective-C or C/C++ for lower-level system integration.
Deep understanding of concurrency (Swift Concurrency, GCD), memory management, and asynchronous network programming.
Experience designing or evolving wire protocols (e.g., Protocol Buffers), data-streaming pipelines, or connection management.
Hands-on experience with Apple's Inter-Process Communication (XPC) to bridge sandboxed applications and system services.
Familiarity with secure communication protocols, cryptography, or privacy-preserving architectures.
Working knowledge of ML concepts and frameworks and proficiency in performance profiling with Instruments, and experience implementing robust client-side telemetry and logging using native Apple APIs.
Familiarity with end-to-end systems that span device, network, and server tiers, and comfort reasoning about failure modes across that boundary.

items.title: Product ML Engineer
items.card: ABOUT THE ROLE - Embed directly within a product team. Work closely with the SMB, Scaler or Enterprise team on focused ML problems tied to clear customer and business outcomes. - Own ML projects end to end. Frame the problem, choose the approach, execute the plan, ship the feature and monitor its performance in production. - Make the build vs. buy decision. Determine when to fine-tune or build a model yourself
items.desc:
ABOUT US

Founded in 2019 and part of Y Combinator's 2020 cohort, Photoroom https://www.photoroom.com is the leading visual solution for e-commerce.

We've raised Series B funding and reached 300+ million users worldwide, processing over 5 billion images annually and serving both small businesses and major enterprises like Amazon, DoorDash, and Decathlon through our mobile app, web platform, and API.

We're a team of 100+ passionate builders giving e-commerce businesses superpowers to create visuals that help them grow, making the hardest parts of selling online disappear. We focus on craft, innovation, and collaboration to create exceptional impact for e-commerce businesses worldwide.




ROLE SUMMARY

We're looking for a Product ML Engineer to join one of our product experience teams — SMB, Scaler or Enterprise — and own the ML side of short, high-impact projects.

You'll work on focused ML problems with a clear product outcome, sometimes fine-tuning one of our models, sometimes integrating the best externally available model, but always choosing the fastest and most effective path to customer value.

You'll bring the technical depth of an Applied Scientist while operating with the pace and pragmatism of a product engineer. You'll own the journey from framing the problem through to shipping, measuring and iterating on the feature in production.

This is not a research role. Your time horizon is weeks rather than quarters, and success is measured by what reaches users and the impact it creates.



ABOUT THE ROLE

 - Embed directly within a product team. Work closely with the SMB, Scaler or Enterprise team on focused ML problems tied to clear customer and business outcomes.

 - Own ML projects end to end. Frame the problem, choose the approach, execute the plan, ship the feature and monitor its performance in production.

 - Make the build vs. buy decision. Determine when to fine-tune or build a model yourself versus integrating an external model, API or existing library.

 - Move from idea to production quickly. Work on projects scoped in weeks rather than quarters, prioritising rapid iteration and customer impact.

 - Work closely with the ML team. Leverage shared infrastructure, evaluation tooling and expertise while remaining embedded in the product team's priorities and cadence.

 - Stay close to users. Get rapid feedback from customers, monitor how people use what you've shipped and use those insights to drive the next iteration.

 - Balance technical depth with pragmatism. Know when deeper modelling work is necessary and when an existing solution is already good enough to ship.

 - Write production code. Work directly in the product team's codebase rather than operating primarily through research notebooks and experiments.

 - Own quality in production. Build sound evaluations, monitor performance and investigate failures once the feature is live.
   


ABOUT YOU

 - You've shipped ML into production. You have 2+ years of hands-on experience building and shipping ML-powered products, with strong experience in PyTorch or equivalent frameworks such as TensorFlow or JAX.

 - You have applied-science depth. You can fine-tune vision or diffusion models, design meaningful evaluations and debug training runs when necessary.

 - You're a pragmatic builder. You care about solving the customer's problem rather than proving that your own model is the best approach. You'll happily use an external model, API or existing library when that's the fastest route to value.

 - You're product-minded. You measure success through shipped features, user behaviour and business outcomes rather than papers or benchmarks alone.

 - You're comfortable in production codebases. You can move between experimentation and production engineering, writing maintainable code that lives inside a real product.

 - You have strong ownership. You're comfortable taking an ambiguous ML problem, deciding what matters, choosing an approach and driving it through to production.

 - You iterate quickly. You enjoy short feedback loops and would rather ship something useful, learn from users and improve it than spend months optimising something that hasn't reached production.

 - You're curious and collaborative. You can both explain your expertise and learn from the deep technical expertise around you. You value knowledge sharing and humility.

 - You're fluent in English. French isn't required.

Nice to have: experience shipping generative image models or diffusion models into production; experience evaluating third-party AI APIs against internal alternatives; experience working in a fast-growing startup or directly within a product team.



BENEFITS

 - Competitive salary + meaningful equity

 - Hybrid working from our Paris headquarters

 - Visa sponsorship and relocation support up to €10,000

 - MacBook Pro and full home office setup

 - 30 days annual leave

 - Private healthcare

 - Regular company off-sites and team retreats

 Learn the skills required for hardware development. This includes developing practical skills in advanced design techniques for aerospace applications, understanding of key technologies, develop experience using ECAD tools and test equipment.

 Experience training, some of which will be delivered via on-the-job experience work on real production hardware within projects groups delivering sensor systems to our customers.
