Job Description: 
 Your impact 
 Are you ready to launch your career and make an impact on real-world projects from day one? 
 At Leonardo, based on our Edinburgh or Newcastle sites, we’re looking for graduates who want to be part of something extraordinary—shaping innovation, advancing technology, and enhancing global safety. Joining the Leonardo Graduate Scheme is the opportunity to be part of the next generation of our business.
 You will be provided with a wealth of development opportunities in both virtual and applied working environments. On our programme you will engage with challenging and exciting project work and deliver innovative business or technical solutions as part of a team of subject matter experts. Throughout the programme you will receive coaching and support from your team to achieve your objectives as well as your personal development goals. We are committed to developing our graduates into leading technical professionals, and as such we will also support you through your preferred route for chartership. 
 Our 18-month Graduate Programme gives you the opportunity to work on exciting and challenging projects alongside subject matter experts. On joining, you will receive a starting salary of £34,000 per annum, plus a £1,000 welcome bonus. You’ll also be eligible for a £1,000 exit bonus upon successful completion of the programme. In addition, you may be eligible for a Temporary Accommodation Allowance (TAA), subject to specific criteria.
 You will be expected to spend at least three or four days each week on site, to integrate with your team and maximise your learning experience by designing, testing or integrating RF & Microwave designs on the Edinburgh or Newcastle sites. 
 During the programme, you will: 
 Be encouraged to gain experience of all aspects of the development lifecycle, including requirements analysis, design, implementation, integration, applied research and test.
 Closely liaise with engineers from other disciplines, such as Systems, Software and Mechanical. Opportunities may also arise to interface with customers and end users.
 As a Graduate RF/Microwave Engineer you will: 
 Develop lifelong skills in microwave and RF circuit design, working on frequencies up to 40GHz, with mentorship from world-class experts in the field ensuring high performance and reliability, ensuring compliance with system specifications and safety and environmental standards
 Use state-of-the-art simulation and modelling tools to design products such as transmit/receive modules (TRMs), up/down converters, antennas, filters as well as highly integrated RF and digital boards.
 Contribute to the design and development of key components in high-performance avionic sensor systems
 Test and assess designs in our well-equipped laboratories and anechoic chambers, ensuring robust performance in extreme environmental conditions for long-term use
 Collaborate with cross disciplinary teams – mechanical, systems, test and manufacture - to ensure seamless integration of RF and microwave components into larger systems
 Prepare technical documentation and present findings to internal and external stakeholders
 Contribute to technical reviews. Your role may even take you across the UK or abroad for technical reviews.
 Support continuous improvement initiatives for hardware design processes and methodologies
 What you’ll bring: Entry Requirements 
 We are looking for graduates who are enthusiastic about hardware design and eager to work in a fast-paced, collaborative environment.
 Minimum of a 2:2 Bachelor’s, Integrated Master’s degree, or higher degree (MSc or PhD) in Electrical Engineering, Electronics, or a related discipline. 
 For the Graduate RF/Microwave Engineer role, the preferred degrees are: Electrical and Electronic Engineering, Communications Engineering, Engineering Physics, Mathematical Sciences, Physics and Mathematics
 Strong interest in microwave and RF design, with basic familiarity with design tools like CST, HFSS, ADS or similar being desirable but not required as training will be provided
 Strong problem-solving abilities, with excellent communication skills and a desire to work collaboratively in a team. A proactive approach to learning new technologies is crucial
 Security Clearance 
 Many of our roles are subject to security and export control restrictions set by UK Government Security requirements and customer obligations. As a result, and in line with the UK Government Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) requirements, all successful applicants will be asked to provide evidence of identity, eligibility to work in the UK, criminal record declaration information and employment and/or education history verification for the previous five years.

2 Research Assistant Positions in Understanding heterogeneity in the AUTISMS - IT | Istituto Italiano di Tecnologia 
 2 Research Assistant Positions in Understanding heterogeneity in the AUTISMS 
 Italy 
 Commitment & contract: fellow position, collaboration contract 
 Location: Rovereto (TN), CNCS@UniTn - Trento 
 Step into a world of endless possibilities, together let’s leave something for the future! 
 At IIT, we are committed to advancing human-centered Science and Technology to address the most urgent societal challenges of our era. We foster excellence in both fundamental and applied research, spanning fields such as neuroscience and cognition, humanoid technologies and robotics, artificial intelligence, nanotechnology, and material sciences, offering a truly interdisciplinary scientific experience. Our approach integrates cutting-edge tools and technology, empowering researchers to push the limits of knowledge and innovation. With us, your curiosity will know no bounds.
 We are dedicated to providing equal employment opportunities and fostering diversity in all its forms, creating an inclusive environment. We value the unique experiences, knowledge, backgrounds, cultures, and perspectives of our people. By embracing diversity, we believe science can achieve its fullest potential.
 THE ROLE 
 The Neurodevelopmental Disorders Research Unit at Istituto Italiano di Tecnologia - IIT (https://www.iit.it/research/lines/neurodevelopmental-disorders), led by Dr. Michael Lombardo, is looking for 2 talented Research Assistants as part of ongoing research understanding multilevel heterogeneity in the autisms.
 The research program aims to identify stratification markers that delineate important distinctions within the population of individuals with autism. The work will require successful candidate to aid other lab personnel (PhD students, Post-docs, PI) in actions relevant to the research program’s aims. The laboratory uses multidisciplinary methods such as observation behavioral methods, neuropsychological testing, eye tracking, EEG, MRI, and fMRI.
 Successful candidates will work with the PI, other lab members, and international collaborators on a variety of research-focused actions focused on identifying important subtypes of patients with ASD. The main tasks are, but not limited to, recruitment of participants for new scientific studies, collection of research data in experiments that include eye tracking, EEG and fMRI methodologies.
 ESSENTIAL REQUIREMENTS 
 Possession of a Bachelors or Masters in a discipline related to the work we do in the lab (e.g., psychology, psychiatry, neuroscience, cognitive science)
 Good command of both Italian and English languages and good organizational skills
 Prior research experience working with children and/or adults with neurodevelopmental disorders
 ADDITIONAL SKILLS 
 Training or experience on existing neuropsychological and/or clinical assessments such as IQ assessments and/or the ADOS.
 Computational skills (e.g. statistics, coding skills in MATLAB, R, Python)
 High motivation and ability to work both independently and as part of a team
 Knowledge of the field of autism and neurodevelopmental disorders
 Motivation to pursue a career in academic research
 COMPENSATION PACKAGE 
 A yearly gross salary of about 22,500 €
 Candidates from abroad or Italian citizens who have carried scientific research activity permanently abroad and meet specific requirements, may be entitled to a deduction from taxable income of up to 90% from 6 to 13 years.
 Please submit your application using the online form and including a detailed CV, cover letter explaining your fit and motivation for the position, and 2 reference letters.
 Application’s deadline: November 30th, 2026 or until position is filled. 
 To discover more about life at IIT, visit the dedicated section here: https://www.iit.it/en/work-at-iit

items.desc: Le descriptif de l’offre ci-dessous est en Anglais Type de contrat : CDD Niveau de diplôme exigé : Thèse ou équivalent Fonction : Ingénieur scientifique contractuel Contexte et atouts du poste This research engineer position is part of the PILOT (Practices and Infrastructure for Long-Term Collaboration) project within the French national research programme PEPR eNSEMBLE (Future of Digital Collaboration). Running from 2023 to 2030, PILOT is coordinated by Claudia-Lavinia Ignat (Inria), Myriam Lewkowicz (Université de Technologie de Troyes), and François Charoy (Université de Lorraine). The project brings together 15 partner institutions and approximately 25 research teams. PILOT aims to design and develop the next generation of collaborative technologies that support sustainable, secure, and interoperable collaboration across organizational boundaries. By combining research in distributed systems, Computer-Supported Cooperative Work (CSCW), Human-Computer Interaction (HCI), and social sciences, the project seeks to develop collaborative infrastructures grounded in actual work practices and organizational needs. A central objective of PILOT is to overcome the limitations of existing collaborative platforms, particularly their dependence on centralized services, limited interoperability, and restricted user control over shared data. The project investigates alternative approaches that enable organizations and individuals to collaborate while preserving their autonomy, privacy, and control over their data and tools. The successful candidate will join the LORELEY research team at the Inria Centre at the University of Lorraine in Nancy. They will work at the intersection of academic research and software engineering, collaborating closely with researchers, PhD students, postdoctoral researchers, and engineers from the PILOT consortium. The position offers the opportunity to contribute to cutting-edge research on distributed collaborative systems and to transform scientific results into open-source software components, integrated prototypes, and demonstrators. Mission confiée The Research Engineer will contribute primarily to two complementary research axes of PILOT: Axis 2 – Open Technical Frameworks and Protocols for Long-Term Collaboration, which develops new algorithms, protocols, and software components for secure, distributed, and interoperable collaborative systems. Axis 4 – Actionable Guidelines and Demonstrators for Long-Term Collaboration, which aims to translate research outcomes into practical solutions, demonstrators, technical guidelines, and reusable software artifacts supporting future forms of collaboration. The main mission will be to design, implement, integrate, and evaluate research prototypes of distributed and secure collaborative applications, working closely with the PhD students and postdoctoral researchers developing the underlying algorithms and protocols. The Research Engineer will also contribute to transforming these individual research prototypes into more comprehensive demonstrators illustrating how different technologies can be combined to support real-world collaborative scenarios. An important part of the position will involve the development and maintenance of an open-source repository of PILOT software components, prototypes, and demonstrators, together with their technical documentation, deployment instructions, and associated use cases. This repository will contribute to the broader PILOT platform, which brings together research findings, collaborative practices, technical components, and guidelines for long-term collaboration. The position therefore combines hands-on software development, research prototyping, system integration, and interdisciplinary collaboration. Principales activités The Research Engineer will contribute to the development, integration, and dissemination of technologies supporting secure, interoperable, and long-term collaboration, with a particular focus on Axes 2 and 4 of PILOT. The main responsibilities will include: Development of research prototypes (Axis 2): Work closely with PhD students, postdoctoral researchers, and other consortium members to implement and evaluate novel technologies for distributed collaborative systems, including collaborative editing, data synchronization, decentralized architectures, interoperability, and security. Integration and development of demonstrators (Axis 4): Combine research prototypes into functional demonstrators illustrating new forms of long-term collaboration, particularly across organizational boundaries and in application domains studied within PILOT. Development and maintenance of the PILOT technical repository: Organize, document, and maintain open-source software components, prototypes, and demonstrators, ensuring their accessibility, reusability, and sustainability. items.desc: A propos de nous Le Shom, service national d’hydrographie et d’océanographie, fournit la connaissance physique de l’océan. Il mesure et décrit les niveaux de la mer, les courants, les sédiments marins, la houle, la température de la mer, la salinité, les bruits sous-marins, les reliefs, les champs magnétiques… et en prévoit l’évolution. Son expertise, reconnue internationalement, éclaire les décisions des usagers de la mer et des acteurs du monde maritime. Ses produits et services répondent aux besoins des forces armées, garantissent la sécurité des navigateurs, guident les politiques publiques de la mer et du littoral, accompagnent le développement de l’économie bleue et contribuent à la préservation de l’environnement marin. Dans un environnement en constante mutation, le Shom innove et se transforme. Drones maritimes, intelligence artificielle et jumeaux numériques sont appelés à renforcer ses moyens d’acquisition et ses capacités de traitement et de modélisation des données collectées. Établissement public à caractère administratif de premier rang au niveau mondial, le Shom est implanté à Brest (siège social), Saint-Mandé, Toulouse, Papeete et Nouméa. Ses 550 collaborateurs, civils et militaires, allient excellence, rigueur, capacités d’adaptation et esprit d’équipe pour relever, aux côtés de nombreux partenaires, les défis de la connaissance de l’océan. Contexte et description du poste : Le poste est rattaché au laboratoire intelligence artificielle du Shom (Brest), au sein de la Direction de la Recherche, de l’Innovation et des Programmes (DRIP/LAB). Ce laboratoire a pour objectif de bénéficier des ruptures technologiques (comme l’apprentissage machine et profond) pour moderniser / prototyper de nouveaux produits et services. Ce poste est également en interaction forte avec le département Océanographie Régionale, Côtière et Littorale (ORCL) du Shom. Le poste vise à intégrer et évaluer des outils d’élaboration de l’information numérique de l’environnement marin, en particulier pour la lutte sous la mer. Ces outils logiciels ont été développés dans le cadre d’un Projet de Technologie de Défense (PTD FASCINATION) en collaboration de recherche avec l’IMT Atlantique. Conçus pour répondre au concept d’Océanographie Nomade, ils sont basés sur des méthodes d’IA (intelligence artificielle) et ont des degrés de maturité différents : un outil de mapping 2D (4DVARNET) qui permet de faire à partir de données éparses et d’un apprentissage sur une base de connaissances, la reconstruction d’un champ complet ; un outil de compression-décompression de champs scalaires 3D (MLIC++) basé sur une minimisation de la perte d’information métiers (mesurée à l’aune de métriques dédiées) ; un outil d’identification des incertitudes dans un champ donné permettant d’optimiser les actions d’acquisition de nouvelles observations en les concentrant aux endroits les moins bien connus. Mission proposée Les missions du poste sont les suivantes : exploiter les conclusions de précédentes évaluations menées sur 4DVARNET et MLIC++ pour en tirer des axes d’optimisation et d’implémentation logicielle ; poursuivre l’évaluation de ces outils sur des situations métiers proches de ceux ayant servi à leur mise au point mais aussi dans de nouveaux contextes (transfert géographique, données de simulations numériques différentes, champs scalaires différents) pouvant requérir de nouveaux apprentissages / des modifications logicielles ; réaliser des développements compatibles avec les capacités d’expérimentation à des fins opérationnelles, en particulier dans le cadre des systèmes SOAP4 et le DataHub embarqué sur les unités de la Marine. Au sein du service DRIP/LAB, vous serez en charge de : Activités principales : Structurer le pipeline et concevoir l’architecture du banc d’essais logiciels Intégrer les outils logiciels en : Analysant les résultats des travaux (CDD, thèse) précédemment menés au sein du PTD FASCINATION ; Reprenant et optimisant l’existant des méthodes et composants logiciels ; Poursuivre les développements en facilitant si possible une intégration future dans les systèmes opérationnels. Évaluer et garder un regard critique sur les résultats, afin d’identifier des améliorations et évolutions (voire corrections) compte-tenu des exigences des besoins opérationnels ; Participer aux expérimentations en relation avec les équipes de production et les opérationnels, Assurer la veille scientifique du domaine et valoriser scientifiquement les travaux (rédaction de publications, participation à des colloques). Poste à pourvoir à partir du 4 janvier 2027, contrat de projet d'une durée estimée à 24 mois (convention PDT Fascination) Salaire : à partir de 35 800 € brut annuel. Plus particulièrement sur les domaines suivants : la télésanté, l’interopérabilité biomédicale, l’imagerie médicale, l’entrepôt de données de santé, l’interopérabilité. items.desc: Date de publication : Oct 26, 2026, 2:23PM Durée du contrat : 6 mois Au sein du Data Studio, vous contribuerez à des travaux de Data Science et de Machine Learning appliqués à la compréhension des comportements clients et à la prédiction du churn (résiliation client). Dans le secteur des télécommunications, anticiper les résiliations et comprendre les facteurs associés aux départs des clients constituent des enjeux majeurs pour améliorer la connaissance client et accompagner les stratégies de fidélisation. Au-delà de la performance prédictive des modèles, l’objectif est de mieux comprendre les comportements de résiliation et d'identifier les facteurs qui contribuent aux prédictions des algorithmes. Vous travaillerez sur une problématique concrète de churn, notamment sur une typologie de clients spécifique, en combinant analyse de données, modélisation prédictive et méthodes d’explicabilité. Dans cette optique, vos principales missions seront : Comprendre les problématiques métier et les comportements clients : vous familiariser avec les activités télécoms, les offres, les usages et les parcours clients afin d'appréhender les enjeux et les mécanismes de résiliation étudiés. Explorer et analyser les données : extraire, manipuler et analyser les données clients à l'aide de SQL et d'outils tels que BigQuery, puis réaliser des analyses exploratoires en Python (Pandas, NumPy, etc.) afin d'identifier les tendances et les spécificités des populations étudiées. Développer des modèles de prédiction du churn : mettre en œuvre et comparer différentes approches de Machine Learning, notamment des algorithmes de classification, afin de prédire les risques de résiliation. Étudier l’explicabilité des modèles : explorer et appliquer des méthodes d’interprétabilité telles que la feature importance, SHAP ou d’autres approches d’explicabilité afin de comprendre les contributions des différentes variables aux prédictions. Identifier et analyser les facteurs associés au churn : approfondir l’analyse des résultats des modèles, étudier les interactions entre variables et caractériser les comportements spécifiques de certaines typologies de clients churners. Évaluer et valoriser les résultats : confronter les analyses aux réalités métier, étudier leur robustesse, synthétiser les enseignements et présenter les conclusions aux équipes Data Science et aux interlocuteurs métier. Selon l’avancement du stage, d’autres pistes pourront être explorées. Vous préparez un diplôme de niveau Bac +5, en école d’ingénieur ou Master 2, avec une spécialisation en Data Science, Intelligence Artificielle, Machine Learning ou Mathématiques appliquées. Vous maîtrisez Python et les principales bibliothèques de Data Science (Pandas, NumPy, Scikit-learn), pour la manipulation de données, l'analyse statistique et la modélisation prédictive. Vous disposez d'une bonne maîtrise de SQL pour l'extraction et la manipulation de données, idéalement dans un environnement BigQuery. Vous possédez de solides connaissances en statistiques et en Machine Learning, notamment sur les principaux algorithmes de classification (régression logistique, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, etc.). Vous comprenez les principes de fonctionnement des algorithmes de Machine Learning, leurs hypothèses, leurs limites et les principales méthodologies d'évaluation des performances. Vous êtes à l'aise avec l'analyse exploratoire de données, la visualisation et l'interprétation de résultats statistiques. Des connaissances en méthodes d'explicabilité des modèles (SHAP, feature importance, etc.) constituent un plus. Vous faites preuve de curiosité scientifique, de rigueur, d'autonomie et d'un esprit analytique. Vous aimez approfondir les analyses, comprendre le fonctionnement des modèles et résoudre des problématiques complexes. Vous disposez de bonnes capacités d’analyse, de synthèse et de communication, et savez vulgariser des résultats techniques auprès d'interlocuteurs métier. Vous appréciez le travail en équipe et savez faire preuve d'initiative. Travailler sur des problématiques concrètes de Data Science au cœur des activités d'un grand opérateur télécom, avec des enjeux forts autour de la connaissance client et de la fidélisation. Approfondir votre expertise en Machine Learning et en intelligence artificielle explicable, en expérimentant différentes approches de modélisation et d'interprétabilité. Développer une double compréhension technique et métier, en reliant les résultats des algorithmes aux comportements clients et aux enjeux opérationnels. Évoluer dans une équipe internationale et pluridisciplinaire, au contact d'experts en Data Science et Intelligence Artificielle. items.desc: Your role We are looking for a highly motivated Machine Learning Scientist to help develop world-leading machine learning models for weather and climate and ensure these are built on an efficient, scalable and sustainable software infrastructure. The work requires technical expertise to create state-of-the-art and sustainable machine learning models but also to develop the required underlying software infrastructure. It necessitates excellent soft skills to work seamlessly in an international, interdisciplinary, and highly diverse working environment. The role will, in particular, support the scientific and technical development of a machine-learned Earth system model and contribute to Anemoi, the software library for machine learning-based weather forecasting and Earth system modelling developed by ECMWF and its member states. It will also contribute the maintenance of the WeatherGenerator code base that is used in the EarthGenerator project and help increase the HPC efficiency of the model. The position will also support the CLAIMA project, which develops infrastructure for machine learning climate models, and wider developments around the WeatherGenerator. About the Team The position will be located in the Machine Learning Modelling Team in the Earth System Modelling Section of the Research Department. The Machine Learning Modelling Team focuses on the development and application of machine learning for Earth system modelling. This includes developments for ECMWF’s operational Artificial Intelligence Forecasting System (AIFS), machine learning models to represent Earth system components such as ocean, sea ice and land, and methodological developments such as foundation modelling and generative machine learning. The advertised position will work in very close collaboration with physical modellers and several other teams and sections within ECMWF. It will also have a direct impact on operational weather prediction at ECMWF and the creation of Digital Twins as part of Destination Earth. At ECMWF, you will find a passionate community, collectively aiming to build world-leading global Earth system models for numerical weather prediction. This effort supports ECMWF’s strategy of producing cuttingedge science and world-leading weather predictions and monitoring of the Earth system. About the Project This role is funded through two major European initiatives: Destination Earth (DestinE) and EarthGenerator. Destination Earth, an initiative of the European Commission, is developing Digital Twins of the Earth and a machine-learned Earth system model for weather and climate applications. This includes learned ocean, wave, sea-ice, land surface and hydrology models developed using Europe's largest EuroHPC supercomputers. The WeatherGenerator Horizon Europe project builds a European foundation model for weather and climate. The EarthGenerator Horizon Europe project extends the concept of the WeatherGenerator and explores foundation models for Earth sciences that can be applied to long prediction timescales from multiple years to decades. The CLAIMA Horizon Europe project will compare different machine learning models for use cases in the area of climate modelling. Your responsibilities You will: Contribute to an efficient and sustainable software infrastructure for world-leading machine learning models at ECMWF and the ECMWF Member and Co-operating States Support the evolution of Anemoi while ensuring that the code meets the highest standards and is long-term sustainable Support maintenance and improvements to the WeatherGenerator code base, ensuring its long-term viability Explore new machine learning architectures and capabilities for Earth system modelling for operational weather predictions and Earth system modelling more generally Implement and evaluate new models and training protocols for weather forecasting and Earth system modelling in the context of both AIFS and the WeatherGenerator What we are looking for You will bring: Excellent interpersonal and communication skills with the ability to collaborate effectively across interdisciplinary teams (machine learning engineers and scientists, domain scientists, operations) and external partners Ability to work on and contribute effectively to large software projects following modern coding practices, including writing tests and reviewing code Experience with the development and evaluation of machine learning models, including model design, implementation, training, and scaling Experience with the application of machine learning in the wider context of Earth system modelling would be an advantage Experience in designing for and optimizing performance of machine learning tools for training and inference on single GPUs and large HPCs would be an advantage Your profile - Education, experience, knowledge and skills (including language) Advanced university degree (EQ7 level or above) in a physical, mathematical, data/machine learning or environmental science, or …

The project APORIA (“Augmenting Poiesis: Relational Inquiries in the Age of AI”), led by Dr Maxime Le Calvé and funded by the European Research Council (ERC Starting Grant), studies everyday AI practices in three epistemic communities where making and knowing are deeply embodied yet increasingly digital: neurosurgery, design and anthropology. items.desc: The role The successful applicant will join the School of Geographical Sciences, but will work across the University and with cross-disciplinary research institutes such as the Cabot Institute for the Environment, the Elizabeth Blackwell Institute for Health, and Jean Golding Institute for Data Science. We are open to applicants in all areas of climate change and health, but evidence of strong connections and understanding of both the ‘climate change’ and ‘health’ sectors is important. We would welcome applications from candidates with interests in the primary application of data science and AI to research questions in climate change and health. Research interests might include: human health for different climate and adaption scenarios; fine-scale weather/climate hazard modelling relevant for health; different health, data, and AI models that complement and add to our existing ones, for instance related to lifetime exposures or impacts on chronic health outcomes; linked data and digital health; lived experience; different types of methods of assessment for climate and health impacts. What will you be doing? Develop and sustain funding support for their own areas of research. Independently identify relevant research objectives for a research team to pursue and, where appropriate, contribute effectively to faculty research programmes, ensuring that outputs meet the quality and quantity expectations for the School and/or Faculty. Lead research funding bids and research teams. Take a leading role in the successful dissemination, nationally and internationally, of research findings. Develop knowledge of, and contacts with, appropriate funding bodies external to the University. Provide expert advice on research issues to research fellows and other colleagues. Play a leading role in, and/or help to create, networks of researchers active in their area of scholarship and help create opportunities for collaborative work with other research centres. Peer review manuscripts for publication and/or research bids. Participate actively in the development of the School’s research strategy. Make a significant contribution to the School’s research reputation and income. Develop effective activities to achieve engagement with research, and/or impact beyond academia. Where appropriate, develop relations with communities relevant to the research, and public and private enterprises in order to capitalise on intellectual property and collaboration. You should apply if You have extensive academic experience, which includes contributions in research, related leadership and administration. Role holders will be expected to be leading collaborative research bids, research teams or scholastic projects (e.g. editing journals or academic books). You will have an established reputation within your academic discipline and will be producing research of national, if not international, quality. You will be making a significant leadership and/or management contribution within your school or the wider University. You will have completed your PhD and will have demonstrated excellence in scholarship, research, teaching, and administration appropriate to your career stage. The role of Research Fellow in Climate Change and Health is a fixed 3-year Pathway 2 position. We expect the role holder will develop their research including actively seeking opportunities to fund their research beyond the 3 years and publish their research findings, contribute to doctoral supervision, and support the activities of the School in an administrative role. Closing Date: 09 November 2026 The Role We are delighted to offer an exciting opportunity for a Post Doctoral Research Associate (Evaluator) to our team at the John Walton Muscular Dystrophy Research Centre, Newcastle University, working on a Myositis UK funded project to validate MRI-based diagnostic biomarkers for inclusion body myositis (IBM). You will join an internationally recognised neuromuscular research environment in Newcastle and work closely with Professor Giorgio Tasca, Professor Jordi Diaz-Manera, and collaborating international referral centres contributing anonymised muscle MRI datasets to the study. IBM is the most common acquired myopathy in people over 40 years of age, but diagnosis is often delayed or incorrect because robust diagnostic biomarkers are lacking. This project, “Validation and AI implementation of MRI Diagnostic Criteria for Inclusion Body Myositis: establishing imaging biomarkers to improve diagnostics and trial recruitment”, will provide the first large-scale external multicentre validation of refined MRI diagnostic criteria and compare expert visual assessment with AI-assisted MRI analysis. The postholder will have a central role in the blinded MRI reading phase of the study and will provide expert evaluation of muscle MRI scans collected from international neuromuscular centres. You will apply refined IBM MRI diagnostic criteria, undertake semiquantitative scoring across approximately 40 muscles per scan, and contribute repeat assessments for intra-rater reproducibility analyses, helping to establish structured muscle MRI as a reliable diagnostic biomarker for IBM. We are particularly keen to hear from candidates with expertise in muscle MRI assessment, strong analytical skills, and experience working with complex clinical research datasets in neuromuscular or closely related disorders. The successful candidate will be comfortable working both independently and as part of a collaborative translational research team, with the ability to interpret imaging data rigorously and communicate findings clearly to academic and clinical audiences. The role will also involve active engagement with national and international collaborators and may support dissemination of findings at scientific meetings. As part of our commitment to career development for research colleagues, the University has developed 3 levels of Research Innovation Role Profiles.pdf. These profiles set out firstly the generic competencies and responsibilities expected of role holders at each level and, secondly, the general qualifications and experiences needed for entry at a particular level. The successful candidate will report to Giorgio Tasca, Clinical Professor of Neuromuscular Sciences. For an informal discussion about the role, please contact him at Giorgio.tasca@newcastle.ac.uk Please submit a CV and covering letter, highlighting your relevant experience in sample preparation and analysis, omics research, experimental workflow development and collaborative, multi-site research. Find out more about the Faculty of Medical Sciences here: https://www.ncl.ac.uk/medical-sciences/ Find out more about our Research Institutes: https://www.ncl.ac.uk/medical-sciences/research/institutes/ This is a fixed term post for 8 months. items.desc: About AMI We are building a new breed of AI systems that (1) understand the real world, (2) have persistent memory, (3) can reason and plan, and (4) are controllable and safe. We are a team of scientists and engineers building frontier world model-based AI. We combine the scientific rigor of a top-tier research institute with focus on engineering excellence and execution. We are a global company, with offices in Paris, Montreal, New York, and Singapore. Come build the future of AI with us! AMI believes AI agents should predict and plan using an internal model of the world — their world model. We’re looking for new team members to advance the state-of-the-art in world modeling. We believe that video is a rich and abundant source of data reflecting how the world works, and that in general models need to be able to process continuous, high-dimensional data from a variety of sensors to: (a) understand context about the current state of the physical world, (b) make predictions about how the world will evolve, possibly as a result of actions taken, and (c) plan and adapt sequences of actions to complete complex tasks, possibly in dynamic, complex environments. You will work with a team on world model research efforts, including: Self-supervised learning methods to efficiently learn from video and other continuous, high-dimensional signals New architectures that efficiently learn to predict world dynamics from video and other high-dimensional signals Scalable algorithms for pre-processing and curating video data Evaluations for benchmarking world model understanding, prediction, and planning Efficient algorithms for model-based planning and reasoning Minimum Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience in Computer Science or a related field Proficiency in Python Ability to design, run, and analyze experiments independently Understanding of machine learning fundamentals, large-scale training, and accelerator-based (GPU or TPU) compute environments Preferred Qualifications: Deep expertise in at least one of the following: self-supervised learning, video and multimodal model architectures, planning algorithms Demonstrated record of contributing to advanced research projects via publications and/or major model releases Experience developing evaluation frameworks for world models Experience releasing and maintaining open-source projects Proficiency in a deep learning framework (PyTorch or JAX)

Rejoignez nous pour une carrière pleine d'opportunités , où vous pouvez faire la différence et où aucun jour ne se ressemble Vos missions Vous rejoignez une équipe de recherche dédiée à la conception de solutions de Physical AI et de robotique cognitive , capables de percevoir, raisonner, apprendre, décider et agir dans des environnements complexes. Concevoir des architectures de Physical AI combinant perception multimodale, World Models, modèles Vision-Langage-Action (VLA) et génération d’actions. Développer des solutions robotiques sous ROS 2, de la communication entre capteurs et modèles d’IA jusqu’aux systèmes de commande et actionneurs. Développer et évaluer des approches d’apprentissage robotique pour la navigation autonome, la manipulation mobile, la locomotion et l’interaction humain-robot. Créer et exploiter des environnements de simulation robotique, notamment avec MuJoCo, NVIDIA Isaac Sim ou des outils équivalents, et travailler sur le transfert simulation-réalité. Tester et fiabiliser les solutions développées, analyser leurs performances, documenter les résultats et contribuer à la valorisation des travaux de recherche. Votre profil Vous êtes diplômée ou diplômé d’un Bac+5 ou d’un doctorat en robotique, automatique, ingénierie ou dans un domaine connexe. Vous disposez d’une première expérience concrète en développement robotique, acquise en entreprise, en laboratoire ou au travers de projets techniques aboutis. La fiche de poste ne fixe pas de nombre minimum d’années d’expérience. Vous maîtrisez Python et son écosystème scientifique, notamment NumPy, SciPy, PyTorch ou équivalents, ainsi que ROS 2 et les fondamentaux de la robotique : cinématique, dynamique, commande, planification du mouvement et intégration de capteurs. Vous avez une expérience pratique d’un environnement de simulation robotique, idéalement MuJoCo ou NVIDIA Isaac Sim, et êtes à l’aise avec les méthodes d’apprentissage appliquées à la robotique ainsi qu’avec Linux, Git, les tests et la documentation. Vous savez évoluer dans un environnement de recherche collaboratif, faire preuve d’adaptabilité et partager vos travaux avec différents interlocuteurs. Un niveau d’anglais professionnel est attendu afin d’évoluer dans un environnement scientifique et technologique international. 3 raisons de nous rejoindre Qualité de vie au travail : accord de télétravail en France et à l’international, accord sur l’égalité professionnelle, la parentalité, l’équilibre des temps et la mobilité durable. Apprentissage en continu : certifications et formations en libre accès, accompagnement sur mesure avec votre career manager, parcours d’intégration sur 9 mois. Avantages groupe & CSE : plan actionnariat, activités à tarifs préférentiels, remboursement partiel vacances, remboursement de votre abonnement sportif ou culturel. En nous rejoignant, vous intégrez un collectif qui valorise la diversité, développe le potentiel de ses talents, s’engage dans des initiatives solidaires avec ses partenaires, et se mobilise pour réduire son impact environnemental sur tous ses sites et auprès de ses clients. It is a responsible and diverse group of 340,000 team members in more than 50 countries. With its strong over 55-year heritage, Capgemini is trusted by its clients to unlock the value of technology to address the entire breadth of their business needs. It delivers end-to-end services and solutions leveraging strengths from strategy and design to engineering, all fueled by its market leading capabilities in AI, generative AI, cloud and data, combined with its deep industry expertise and partner ecosystem.

items.desc: About CommonAI CIC CommonAI CIC is a non-profit membership organisation, founded on a belief in collaborative engineering for the safe and responsible development of foundational AI technologies. A place where AI startups, enterprises large and small, public sector bodies and academia can share resources and knowledge, to codevelop and grow businesses, fast. We are led by experienced founders, investors and engineers who believe that collaborative engineering drives faster AI innovation and are backed by a mix of UK Government and private funding in order to design, build and deploy innovative AI systems. The Opportunity We are seeking an AI Security Researcher with the mindset of an attacker: someone who enjoys finding out how systems can be broken, misused or circumvented. Our research team works on reducing the complexity of large language models while retaining their performance. You will support our High Assurance programme, which works on the accuracy, explainability and accountability of AI systems used in regulated environments such as financial services. You will track the research that matters to the programme, challenge its technical decisions, and help test whether the simpler, more interpretable models emerging from our frontier research are easier to audit in practice. What You'll Do Track key research and developments relevant to the High Assurance programme, including attacks on AI models, defences against them, and the security of the systems that serve them Report on what these developments mean for the programme and our Members, through written briefings and presentations Review the programme's technical decisions and directions from an attacker's point of view, and propose stronger alternatives Threat-model AI systems used in regulated settings, covering model weights, training data, inference serving, and the tools and agents built on them Red-team the systems we build, within an agreed scope, and report findings through a clear disclosure process Help develop interpretability methods for the simpler models produced by our frontier research, and test their limits, for example by trying to hide behaviour the methods should detect Build internal expertise by sharing what you learn with colleagues and helping answer technical questions from our Members Requirements Proven experience in security research, offensive security or adversarial machine learning (e.g. red-teaming, penetration testing, vulnerability research, or attacks on ML models) A strong understanding of how modern AI systems work, including how large language models are trained, deployed and served Familiarity with attacks on AI systems (e.g. jailbreaks, prompt injection, data poisoning, backdoors, model extraction) Strong Python, and the ability to build your own tools and experiments Excellent written communication: you can turn complex technical findings into clear involvement in that community Knowledge of hardware and side-channel security (e.g. timing attacks, risks in shared GPU and inference infrastructure) Familiarity with AI assurance standards and items.desc: Your role We are looking for a highly motivated Machine Learning Scientist to help develop world-leading machine learning models for weather and climate and ensure these are built on an efficient, scalable and sustainable software infrastructure. The work requires technical expertise to create state-of-the-art and sustainable machine learning models but also to develop the required underlying software infrastructure. It necessitates excellent soft skills to work seamlessly in an international, interdisciplinary, and highly diverse working environment. The role will, in particular, support the scientific and technical development of a machine-learned Earth system model and contribute to Anemoi, the software library for machine learning-based weather forecasting and Earth system modelling developed by ECMWF and its member states. It will also contribute the maintenance of the WeatherGenerator code base that is used in the EarthGenerator project and help increase the HPC efficiency of the model. The position will also support the CLAIMA project, which develops infrastructure for machine learning climate models, and wider developments around the WeatherGenerator. About The Team The position will be located in the Machine Learning Modelling Team in the Earth System Modelling Section of the Research Department. The Machine Learning Modelling Team focuses on the development and application of machine learning for Earth system modelling. This includes developments for ECMWF’s operational Artificial Intelligence Forecasting System (AIFS), machine learning models to represent Earth system components such as ocean, sea ice and land, and methodological developments such as foundation modelling and generative machine learning. The advertised position will work in very close collaboration with physical modellers and several other teams and sections within ECMWF. It will also have a direct impact on operational weather prediction at ECMWF and the creation of Digital Twins as part of Destination Earth. At ECMWF, you will find a passionate community, collectively aiming to build world-leading global Earth system models for numerical weather prediction. This effort supports ECMWF’s strategy of producing cutting‐edge science and world-leading weather predictions and monitoring of the Earth system. About The Project This role is funded through two major European initiatives: Destination Earth (DestinE) and EarthGenerator. Destination Earth, an initiative of the European Commission, is developing Digital Twins of the Earth and a machine-learned Earth system model for weather and climate applications. This includes learned ocean, wave, sea-ice, land surface and hydrology models developed using Europe's largest EuroHPC supercomputers. The WeatherGenerator Horizon Europe project builds a European foundation model for weather and climate. The EarthGenerator Horizon Europe project extends the concept of the WeatherGenerator and explores foundation models for Earth sciences that can be applied to long prediction timescales from multiple years to decades. The CLAIMA Horizon Europe project will compare different machine learning models for use cases in the area of climate modelling. Your Responsibilities You will: Contribute to an efficient and sustainable software infrastructure for world-leading machine learning models at ECMWF and the ECMWF Member and Co-operating States Support the evolution of Anemoi while ensuring that the code meets the highest standards and is long-term sustainable Support maintenance and improvements to the WeatherGenerator code base, ensuring its long-term viability Explore new machine learning architectures and capabilities for Earth system modelling for operational weather predictions and Earth system modelling more generally Implement and evaluate new models and training protocols for weather forecasting and Earth system modelling in the context of both AIFS and the WeatherGenerator What We Are Looking For You will bring: Excellent interpersonal and communication skills with the ability to collaborate effectively across interdisciplinary teams (machine learning engineers and scientists, domain scientists, operations) and external partners Ability to work on and contribute effectively to large software projects following modern coding practices, including writing tests and reviewing code Experience with the development and evaluation of machine learning models, including model design, implementation, training, and scaling Experience with the application of machine learning in the wider context of Earth system modelling would be an advantage Experience in designing for and optimizing performance of machine learning tools for training and inference on single GPUs and large HPCs would be an advantage Your profile - Education, experience, knowledge and skills (including language) Advanced university degree (EQ7 level or above) in a physical, mathematical, data/machine learning or environmental science, or …

items.desc: Fetcherr builds responsible AI that transforms market complexity into measurable profit growth. At the core of the company is the Market Model - a proprietary AI-powered model delivering accurate, granular demand predictions with 96% forecast accuracy and real-time decision intelligence for commercial teams. Built on a glass-box architecture, it uses market data - not personal data - with full transparency into logic and outcomes. First deployed in global aviation, the technology is industry-agnostic and scales across volatile markets. Fetcherr delivers a consistent average profit uplift of 7%, with corporate partners including Delta, Virgin Atlantic, WestJet, Viva, and Azul. The Large Market Modeling (LMM) team is the engine underneath Fetcherr's pricing intelligence. We're the ones who actually build and train the models — taking a chaotic world of market signals, customer behavior, and competitive dynamics and turning them into reliable, production-ready demand models. Other teams at Fetcherr work with the models; we're the ones who bring them to life. Think of us as the team that teaches Fetcherr's AI how people buy — so it can always recommend the right price at the right moment. We are seeking a talented and self-driven experienced Data Scientist to help advance our machine learning capabilities.This is a key role for someone passionate about leveraging machine learning to solve complex, real-world problems and deliver measurable business impact. Responsibilities: Develop and implement state-of-the-art econometric and machine learning models for demand forecasting. Conduct research and experimentation to evaluate novel approaches for improving accuracy, robustness, and scalability. Collaborate with cross-functional teams (including product, data engineering, MLOPS and Platform) to deploy ML systems in production. Clearly communicate complex technical findings to non-technical stakeholders, including product leaders and executives. Requirements: 5+ years of hands-on experience in data science and machine learning with a proven record of leveraging modeling into business outcomes. Proficiency in Python and its ML/data stack (e.g., PyTorch or TensorFlow, Pandas, NumPy, Scikit-learn). Expertise in time-series forecasting, ideally Deep Learning based, preferably in demand prediction or related areas. Feature engineering, feature importance testing, explainability based experience. Master’s or PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Statistics, Engineering or a relevant field. Solid understanding of ML production workflows (versioning, testing, reproducibility, and deployment). Excellent communication and collaboration skills. Nice to have: Publications in top-tier, peer-reviewed ML/AI venues (e.g. ICLR, ICML, NIPS, etc.) Experience applying ML in domains like finance, trading, revenue management etc. Familiarity with cloud based solutions on GCP platform (e.g., Vertex AI, PubSub, Cloud Run Functions). Strong data visualization and exploratory data analysis skills. Familiarity with code optimization, containerization (e.g., Docker), CI/CD, or cloud-native architectures. Participation in competitive programming or data science challenges (e.g., Kaggle). If you're excited about building impactful AI systems in a high-growth startup environment, and want to help redefine how industries price, forecast, and optimize, we’d love to hear from you.

Job Position Siamo alla ricerca di una figura altamente qualificata da inserire nel team che sviluppa soluzioni data-driven per il controllo avanzato, la stima e l'ottimizzazione di sistemi ingegneristici complessi. La risorsa sarà coinvolta nelle seguenti attività: sviluppo di algoritmi di machine learning applicati al controllo e alla stima: modelli data-driven e ibridi (physics-informed), sensori virtuali, identificazione di sistemi dinamici, MPC learning-based e adattativo, ottimizzazione bayesiana per il tuning dei controllori, reinforcement learning; progettazione di strategie di controllo avanzato e di ottimizzazione numerica, anche per sistemi distribuiti, multi-agente o in rete, con attenzione a vincoli, robustezza e requisiti real-time; implementazione e validazione degli algoritmi su sistemi reali: prototipazione in MATLAB/Simulink e Python, test in simulazione, hardware-in-the-loop e su banco prova, analisi dei dati sperimentali; supporto al trasferimento degli algoritmi su piattaforme embedded ed edge, in collaborazione con il team software; redazione di documentazione tecnica, report di progetto e pubblicazioni, e presentazione dei risultati a clienti, partner e valutatori; collaborazione con università, centri di ricerca e partner industriali nello sviluppo tecnico dei progetti. Chi stiamo cercando Laurea Magistrale in Ingegneria dell'Automazione, Ingegneria Matematica, Elettronica, Informatica, Fisica o discipline affini; Dottorato di ricerca (PhD) in controlli, ottimizzazione, matematica applicata o machine learning, oppure esperienza equivalente; Solida preparazione in teoria del controllo (controllo ottimo, MPC, stima e identificazione) e in ottimizzazione numerica; Esperienza comprovata nell'applicazione di tecniche di machine learning alla modellazione, alla stima o al controllo di sistemi dinamici; Esperienza nella stesura di documentazione tecnica e/o di articoli scientifici per riviste e conferenze internazionali; Esperienza pratica su progetti applicativi o industriali, con implementazione e validazione degli algoritmi su dati e sistemi reali; Ottima conoscenza di Python e MATLAB/Simulink e dei principali framework di machine learning (es. PyTorch, scikit-learn). Costituiscono un plus: partecipazione a progetti finanziati con ruoli tecnici o di coordinamento; esperienza su sistemi in rete o multi-agente, controllo distribuito o federated learning; conoscenza di C/C++ e di strumenti di generazione automatica del codice per target embedded; esperienza in ambito automotive o aerospace, o conoscenza degli standard di settore formazione o esperienza in project management; Cosa ci piacerebbe trovare Eccellenti capacità di scrittura tecnica e di sintesi, in italiano e in inglese; Capacità di tradurre problemi industriali in soluzioni tecniche concrete; Ottime capacità comunicative e relazionali, anche nel confronto con clienti e partner; Capacità di gestire più attività in parallelo rispettando scadenze stringenti; Approccio proattivo, autonomo e orientato ai risultati. L'attività si svolge in un contesto internazionale: è richiesta un'ottima conoscenza della lingua inglese scritta e parlata, anche per la redazione della documentazione tecnica, oltre alla buona conoscenza della lingua italiana. Perché scegliere Modelway Entrando in Modelway troverai: progetti innovativi e tecnologicamente sfidanti; flessibilità organizzativa, con possibilità di smart working e autonomia nella gestione delle attività; percorsi di formazione tecnica e trasversale; programma di mentoring dedicato alla crescita professionale; sede strategica nel centro di Torino; buoni pasto da 10 € per ogni giornata lavorata in presenza. La retribuzione sarà commisurata all'esperienza e al livello di seniority della persona. I dettagli economici saranno approfonditi durante il processo di selezione per assicurare un accordo in linea con le aspettative di entrambe le parti (30-36K). Modelway ha una politica che vieta esplicitamente qualsiasi forma di discriminazione basata su sesso, nazionalità, etnia o altro, ai sensi della legge (L. 903/77 e D.Lgs. n. 198/2006, art. 27). Our approach is entirely mission-focused, enabling customers to see more, decide faster, and act with confidence across complex domains. We deliver situational awareness and information advantage across C5ISR, fusing cyber, geospatial, and kinetic data into an operational picture. This transforms fragmented data into a shared understanding of the battlespace, delivering actionable insight when it matters most. Our solutions are secure-by-design, built from the ground up to protect sensitive information and ensure resilience in contested environments. The role focuses on applying data science and AI techniques to operational intelligence challenges, including large-scale data analysis, predictive modelling, pattern recognition, and automated decision support. The successful candidate will work within multi-disciplinary agile teams, collaborating with data engineers, software engineers, mission analysts and operational users to develop and deploy analytics solutions that enable insight and mission advantage. Data visualisation skills and experience communicating insights through analytical tools and dashboards. items.desc: Research Software Engineer – Environment & Sustainability for the Research Software Sustainability programme (2-year contract) The Netherlands eScience Center is looking for a Research Software Engineer (RSE) to join our dynamic team and collaborate on exciting research projects within the context of the Research Software Sustainability Programme. Join us in harnessing the power of technology to drive innovative research forward. Supported by the Open Science NL Infrastructure programme, which strengthens open science infrastructure in the Netherlands, we are offering a temporary two-year position. The fixed-term contract reflects the project-based nature of the role and its associated funding. The preferred start date is 1 March 2027 or 1 April 2027. If you are driven to continuously improve software and contribute to scientific progress, are creative and communicative, and enjoy tackling complex challenges, this could be the perfect opportunity for you. Who are we? The Netherlands eScience Center is the national center for innovative software solutions in academic research. We aim to bridge the gap in knowledge and expertise between digital technologies on the one hand and scientific and scholarly inquiry on the other. We create tools and digital methodologies that enable researchers across all disciplines to answer research questions, harnessing our unique blend of academic expertise and software development skills. We attach great importance to software quality and sustainability, and academic recognition of research software. We stand for a research-focused, professional, collaborative, open and resourceful approach to everything we do, and we require that our staff can identify with these eScience Center values. Our people have a diverse background in education, gender, nationality, and ethnicity. Together, we form an inclusive group with a common drive. Our Research Software Engineers are distributed into four different sections, Natural Sciences & Engineering, Social Sciences & Humanities, Life Sciences, and Environment & Sustainability, with opportunities to exchange knowledge between the different sections. We always work at the crossroads of digital technologies and academic research with projects ranging from machine learning for climate science to GPU for high-energy physics or linked data for digital humanities. What will you do? This position sits within the Research Software Sustainability Programme (RSSP), which the eScience Center runs on behalf of Open Science NL to improve the sustainability of existing research software. You will be assigned to 2 or 3 projects funded under this programme's 2026 call. The exact tasks vary by project but typically fall into a few categories: software engineering work such as refactoring, modularisation, and improving test coverage and packaging; documentation and training, including writing tutorials and onboarding materials; and community-building activities, such as boosting adoption, extending contributor base, or helping set up governance structures for the project. A typical day may include discussing project progress with researchers and developers, developing and testing software, exploring new computational approaches, improving existing workflows, or contributing to research outputs such as publications, documentation, and open-source software. You will participate in local, national and international events, acting as ambassador of your projects and the tools you contribute to. Who are you? You are motivated to tackle complex research challenges using digital approaches. You enjoy working at the intersection of research and technology and take pride in enabling researchers to answer cutting-edge questions through robust and innovative software solutions. You are curious, proactive, and collaborative, and you communicate effectively with both academic researchers and technical experts. You bring a strong sense of ownership to your work, while remaining flexible and open to learning new tools, domains, and methodologies. You value software quality, sustainability, and reproducibility, and are eager to contribute to an open and inclusive research environment. Furthermore: You hold a master's degree or higher in Earth and Environmental Sciences. You have demonstrated experience in academic research and in development of research software, methodologies, or open-source frameworks for research purposes. You have proven experience in developing research software, including testing, documenting, and applying FAIR principles to research software, and you have an interest in building sustainable software which is adopted by others. You have experience with computational environmental research, including geospatial data, environmental modelling, scientific workflows, and data-intensive analysis. Familiarity with GIS, hydrology, climate and sustainability applications, ecological or agricultural modelling, and the broader Earth-system science ecosystem is …

Interest-free travel loan for train and car park season tickets. Volunteer leave to make a positive impact. Plus more.... About The Role What does the average day look like? The Rail industry is changing as we move into Great British Railways and is understanding the power of data more than ever before. This is driving more investment and support for our requirements on the data foundations and structures. You will be pushing the data landscape forward to allow us to answer the questions that need answering. The Data & Development Portfolio is a new and developing team within the Performance & Simulation Team (P&ST). items.desc: The role The successful applicant will join the School of Geographical Sciences, but will work across the University and with cross-disciplinary research institutes such as the Cabot Institute for the Environment, the Elizabeth Blackwell Institute for Health, and Jean Golding Institute for Data Science. We are open to applicants in all areas of climate change and health, but evidence of strong connections and understanding of both the ‘climate change’ and ‘health’ sectors is important. We would welcome applications from candidates with interests in the primary application of data science and AI to research questions in climate change and health. Research interests might include: human health for different climate and adaption scenarios; fine-scale weather/climate hazard modelling relevant for health; different health, data, and AI models that complement and add to our existing ones, for instance related to lifetime exposures or impacts on chronic health outcomes; linked data and digital health; lived experience; different types of methods of assessment for climate and health impacts. What will you be doing? Develop and sustain funding support for their own areas of research. Independently identify relevant research objectives for a research team to pursue and, where appropriate, contribute effectively to faculty research programmes, ensuring that outputs meet the quality and quantity expectations for the School and/or Faculty. Lead research funding bids and research teams. Take a leading role in the successful dissemination, nationally and internationally, of research findings. Develop knowledge of, and contacts with, appropriate funding bodies external to the University. Provide expert advice on research issues to research fellows and other colleagues. Play a leading role in, and/or help to create, networks of researchers active in their area of scholarship and help create opportunities for collaborative work with other research centres. Peer review manuscripts for publication and/or research bids. Participate actively in the development of the School’s research strategy. Make a significant contribution to the School’s research reputation and income. Develop effective activities to achieve engagement with research, and/or impact beyond academia. Where appropriate, develop relations with communities relevant to the research, and public and private enterprises in order to capitalise on intellectual property and collaboration. You should apply if You have extensive academic experience, which includes contributions in research, related leadership and administration. Role holders will be expected to be leading collaborative research bids, research teams or scholastic projects (e.g. editing journals or academic books). You will have an established reputation within your academic discipline and will be producing research of national, if not international, quality. You will be making a significant leadership and/or management contribution within your school or the wider University. You will have completed your PhD and will have demonstrated excellence in scholarship, research, teaching, and administration appropriate to your career stage. The role of Research Fellow in Climate Change and Health is a fixed 3-year Pathway 2 position. We expect the role holder will develop their research including actively seeking opportunities to fund their research beyond the 3 years and publish their research findings, contribute to doctoral supervision, and support the activities of the School in an administrative role. items.desc: Reference: ICCF26II Start date: 17/09/2026 0:00:00 Expiration Date: 05/11/2026 23:59:00 The Flow Cytometry Core Unit at the Spanish National Cancer Research Centre (CNIO) is seeking an outstanding and highly motivated scientist to join our dynamic and innovative Core Facility as Staff Scientist. Working closely with the Head of the Unit, the successful candidate will contribute to the scientific, technical, and strategic development of the facility, ensuring the delivery of high-quality services and expert support to a diverse portfolio of research programmes. The role will involve supporting researchers in the design, execution, and analysis of advanced cytometry experiments, while contributing to the adoption of emerging technologies, development of best practices, and continuous enhancement of the Unit’s capabilities. The successful candidate will also be expected to provide leadership for the Unit in the absence of the Head, ensuring continuity of its scientific and operational activities and contributing to its strategic development CNIO is one of Europe's leading cancer research institutions, dedicated to advancing cancer research through excellence in basic, translational, and clinical science. The Flow Cytometry Core Unit provides expert technical support, scientific consultation, and access to state-of-the-art cytometry technologies for CNIO researchers. The facility is equipped with three high-speed cell sorters, including the latest BD FACSDiscover™ S8, with full spectral and imaging capabilities, as well as four analytical cytometers encompassing both high-parameter conventional and full-spectrum technologies. This advanced platform supports a broad range of applications, including multiparametric phenotyping, high-dimensional analysis, imaging, and sophisticated cell. Selection Criteria A PhD in Immunology, Cancer Biology, Biomedical Sciences, or a related discipline, together with at least four years of relevant postdoctoral research experience, is required. A minimum of five years of hands-on experience in flow cytometry, with extensive expertise in cell sorting and advanced analytical cytometry, including full-spectrum and imaging flow cytometry, is required. Experience in core facility operations, user support and training, method development, and implementation of new cytometry technologies will be highly valued. Demonstrated expertise in high-speed cell sorting and advanced analytical flow cytometry. Experience with instrumentation available in the Unit (Influx, FACSAria, FACSDiscover S8, FACSCanto, LSRFortessa, and Cytek Aurora) is highly desirable. Strong hands-on experience with conventional multiparametric, full-spectrum, imaging, and next-generation cytometry platforms. Proven ability to design and optimize complex flow cytometry panels and advanced cytometry workflows. Expertise in immune monitoring applications, with experience in cancer research environments highly desirable. Advanced knowledge of flow cytometry acquisition and analysis software, including OMIQ, FlowJo, FCS Express, FACSDiva, FACSChorus, and SpectroFlo. Tissue culture and hands-on experience in sample preparation for flow cytometry. Familiarity with computational approaches for high-dimensional cytometry data analysis is desirable. Proficiency in English is an absolute requirement. Fluency of Spanish is no needed but could be an advantage. Excellent communication, organizational, and interpersonal skills. Ability to work independently while fostering a collaborative and service-oriented team environment. Previous supervisory, leadership, or facility management experience is highly desirable. The CNIO Offers Incorporation into a Cancer Research Centre of excellence of international relevance. Gross annual salary between €44,091 and €47,481. Social benefits. Flexible compensation (Health insurance, meals, transportation, childcare). Contract linked to a project.

items.desc: Als data scientist bij Trading & Optimization werk je op het snijvlak van energie en AI, op een plek waar je werk direct effect heeft op het energienet. Jouw forecast om 13:00:00 stuurt om 13:00:01 een handelsbeslissing aan, en de impact zie je realtime terug op onze dashboards. Je bouwt niet één geïsoleerd model, maar een samenhangend geheel waarin probabilistische forecasting, optimalisatie en aansturing elkaar versterken. De feedbackloop is kort en meetbaar, wat je vandaag bouwt heeft snel impact. Je werkt in een team waar data scientists, engineers en traders dicht op elkaar zitten. Er is weinig hiërarchie en veel ruimte voor eigen initiatief, maar ook duidelijke verwachtingen over eigenaarschap: jouw modellen draaien live en je bent zelf de eerste die ingrijpt als er iets misgaat. AI-tooling zoals Claude Code is volledig ingeburgerd en versnelt je werk. Zo draagt het team direct bij aan plan Zero: elke MWh die we slimmer verhandelen of efficiënter in een batterij laden of ontladen, is een MWh die niet uit een gascentrale hoeft te komen. Jouw impact bij Zonneplan Jij ontwerpt en bouwt de modellen die onze energiehandel aansturen. Je werkt met meerdere gekoppelde systemen tegelijk: weersvoorspellingen, marktprijzen (day-ahead, intraday, onbalans), klantgedrag en het fysieke gedrag van ons VPP (Virtual Power Plant) van batterijen, laadpalen en zonnepanelen. Je denkt in samenhang en bouwt modellen die elkaar versterken. Jij brengt modellen naar productie en houdt ze scherp. Samen met engineers zorg je voor een vlekkeloze deployment. Je pakt eigenaarschap over je modellen: je monitort performance, waarborgt betrouwbaarheid en optimaliseert continu. Jij vertaalt modelkwaliteit naar commercieel resultaat. Jouw werk verlaagt direct de tradingkosten binnen ons energieportfolio en verhoogt het rendement op de Nexus-thuisbatterij. Door nauwkeurige voorspellingen kunnen we klanten een zonnebonus geven in plaats van een terugleverboete, omdat we weten wanneer hun stroom waardevol is. Jij bereidt onze apparaten voor op een toekomst zonder salderen. Door slim in te spelen op marktontwikkelingen en eigen verbruik zorg je ervoor dat klanten maximaal profiteren. Je vertaalt veranderende marktregels naar concrete modelaanpassingen die direct waarde opleveren voor onze klanten. Jij brengt nieuwe ontwikkelingen naar de praktijk. Je volgt de nieuwste ontwikkelingen in AI en machine learning en vertaalt die proactief naar concrete experimenten. Denk aan nieuwe benaderingen voor probabilistische forecasting. Liever een werkend prototype dan een slide. Dit krijg je van ons Een salaris tussen €4.000 en €6.000 bruto per maand, afhankelijk van je ervaring en senioriteit. 25 vakantiedagen (met de mogelijkheid om er meer bij te kopen) en reiskostenvergoeding. Een Claude Code Max 20x abonnement als secundaire arbeidsvoorwaarde. Je zet het in voor je dagelijkse werk en mag het ook gebruiken voor side projects en persoonlijke ontwikkeling. Een persoonlijk keuzebudget voor sport, boodschappen of iets anders dat bij je past. Vanaf dag één investeren we in jouw groei met de Zonneplan Academy, goede tools en ruimte om te blijven leren. Je kunt doorgroeien naar senior data scientist met specialisatie in energiehandel, batterij-optimalisatie of forecasting. Een pragmatische, no-nonsense werksfeer waarin korte lijnen de norm zijn. Je zit dicht op traders en engineers. Dit neem jij mee Je hebt minimaal 3 jaar ervaring als data scientist en sterke fundamenten in statistiek en machine learning, met aantoonbare ervaring in forecasting of time series. Je schrijft Python op productieniveau en hebt ervaring met het deployen en monitoren van modellen in een live omgeving. Je hebt ervaring met of affiniteit voor AI-ondersteund ontwikkelen, bijvoorbeeld met tools als Claude Code, GitHub Copilot of vergelijkbare AI-assistenten. Je denkt vanuit commerciële impact: je kunt de stap maken van een goed model naar meetbare euro's en onderbouwt je keuzes met data. Je neemt eigenaarschap over wat je bouwt. Jouw modellen draaien live en je bent de eerste die ingrijpt, optimaliseert of bijstuurt wanneer dat nodig is. Je bent nieuwsgierig en proactief: je volgt ontwikkelingen in AI en machine learning op de voet en vertaalt die naar concrete experimenten en kansen. Je spreekt de Nederlandse taal op professioneel niveau. Zo ziet het proces eruit 1. Solliciteer op deze vacature. 2. Telefonisch kennismakingsgesprek met Samer (recruiter). 3. Eerste gesprek met Maarten (direct leidinggevende van de functie) en iemand van het team. 4. Persoonlijkheids- en capaciteitentest, gevolgd door een technische casus met iemand van het team waarin je laat zien hoe je van data naar een forecastingmodel en businessimpact komt. 5. Is er een match? Dan doen we je snel een aanbod. Klaar om jouw modellen in te zetten voor plan Zero? Bij Zonneplan werken we aan één duidelijk doel: een Nederland zonder fossiele energie. Wij noemen dat plan Zero. Geen uitstoot, geen verspilling, geen …
