items.desc: Research Software Engineer – Natural Sciences & Engineering for the Research Software Sustainability programme (2-year contract) The Netherlands eScience Center is looking for a Research Software Engineer (RSE) to join our dynamic team and collaborate on exciting research projects within the context of the Research Software Sustainability Programme. Join us in harnessing the power of technology to drive innovative research forward. Supported by the Open Science NL Infrastructure programme, which strengthens open science infrastructure in the Netherlands, we are offering a temporary two-year position. The fixed-term contract reflects the project-based nature of the role and its associated funding. The preferred start date is 1 March 2027 or 1 April 2027. If you are driven to continuously improve software and contribute to scientific progress, are creative and communicative, and enjoy tackling complex challenges, this could be the perfect opportunity for you. Who are we? The Netherlands eScience Center is the national center for innovative software solutions in academic research. We aim to bridge the gap in knowledge and expertise between digital technologies on the one hand and scientific and scholarly inquiry on the other. We create tools and digital methodologies that enable researchers across all disciplines to answer research questions, harnessing our unique blend of academic expertise and software development skills. We attach great importance to software quality and sustainability, and academic recognition of research software. We stand for a research-focused, professional, collaborative, open and resourceful approach to everything we do, and we require that our staff can identify with these eScience Center values. Our people have a diverse background in education, gender, nationality, and ethnicity. Together, we form an inclusive group with a common drive. Our Research Software Engineers are distributed into four different sections, Natural Sciences & Engineering, Social Sciences & Humanities, Life Sciences, and Environment & Sustainability, with opportunities to exchange knowledge between the different sections. We always work at the crossroads of digital technologies and academic research with projects ranging from machine learning for climate science to GPU for high-energy physics or linked data for digital humanities. What will you do? This position sits within the Research Software Sustainability Programme (RSSP), which the eScience Center runs on behalf of Open Science NL to improve the sustainability of existing research software. You will be assigned to 2 or 3 projects funded under this programme's 2026 call. The exact tasks vary by project but typically fall into a few categories: software engineering work such as refactoring, modularisation, and improving test coverage and packaging; documentation and training, including writing tutorials and onboarding materials; and community-building activities, such as boosting adoption, extending contributor base, or helping set up governance structures for the project. A typical day may include discussing project progress with researchers and developers, developing and testing software, exploring new computational approaches, improving existing workflows, or contributing to research outputs such as publications, documentation, and open-source software. You will participate in local, national and international events, acting as ambassador of your projects and the tools you contribute to. Who are you? You are motivated to tackle complex research challenges using digital approaches. You enjoy working at the intersection of research and technology and take pride in enabling researchers to answer cutting-edge questions through robust and innovative software solutions. You are curious, proactive, and collaborative, and you communicate effectively with both academic researchers and technical experts. You bring a strong sense of ownership to your work, while remaining flexible and open to learning new tools, domains, and methodologies. You value software quality, sustainability, and reproducibility, and are eager to contribute to an open and inclusive research environment. Furthermore: You hold a master's degree or higher in a relevant field. You have demonstrated experience in academic research and in development of research software, methodologies, or open-source frameworks for research purposes. You have proven experience in developing research software, including testing, documenting, and applying FAIR principles to research software, and you have an interest in building sustainable software which is adopted by others. You have experience with bringing existing research software to a more robust, maintainable and reusable state, for example through refactoring, modularisation, improving scalability, or strengthening software quality. Familiarity with scientific workflows, data processing and analysis pipelines and high-performance computing infrastructure …

items.desc: Research Software Engineer – Life Sciences for the Research Software Sustainability programme (2-year contract) The Netherlands eScience Center is looking for a Research Software Engineer (RSE) to join our dynamic team and collaborate on exciting research projects within the context of the Research Software Sustainability Programme. Join us in harnessing the power of technology to drive innovative research forward. Supported by the Open Science NL Infrastructure programme, which strengthens open science infrastructure in the Netherlands, we are offering a temporary two-year position. The fixed-term contract reflects the project-based nature of the role and its associated funding. The preferred start date is 1 March 2027 or 1 April 2027. If you are driven to continuously improve software and contribute to scientific progress, are creative and communicative, and enjoy tackling complex challenges, this could be the perfect opportunity for you. Who are we? The Netherlands eScience Center is the national center for innovative software solutions in academic research. We aim to bridge the gap in knowledge and expertise between digital technologies on the one hand and scientific and scholarly inquiry on the other. We create tools and digital methodologies that enable researchers across all disciplines to answer research questions, harnessing our unique blend of academic expertise and software development skills. We attach great importance to software quality and sustainability, and academic recognition of research software. We stand for a research-focused, professional, collaborative, open and resourceful approach to everything we do, and we require that our staff can identify with these eScience Center values. Our people have a diverse background in education, gender, nationality, and ethnicity. Together, we form an inclusive group with a common drive. Our Research Software Engineers are distributed into four different sections, Natural Sciences & Engineering, Social Sciences & Humanities, Life Sciences, and Environment & Sustainability, with opportunities to exchange knowledge between the different sections. We always work at the crossroads of digital technologies and academic research with projects ranging from machine learning for climate science to GPU for high-energy physics or linked data for digital humanities. What will you do? This position sits within the Research Software Sustainability Programme (RSSP), which the eScience Center runs on behalf of Open Science NL to improve the sustainability of existing research software. You will be assigned to 2 or 3 projects funded under this programme's 2026 call. The exact tasks vary by project but typically fall into a few categories: software engineering work such as refactoring, modularisation, and improving test coverage and packaging; documentation and training, including writing tutorials and onboarding materials; and community-building activities, such as boosting adoption, extending contributor base, or helping set up governance structures for the project. A typical day may include discussing project progress with researchers and developers, developing and testing software, exploring new computational approaches, improving existing workflows, or contributing to research outputs such as publications, documentation, and open-source software. You will participate in local, national and international events, acting as ambassador of your projects and the tools you contribute to. Who are you? You are motivated to tackle complex research challenges using digital approaches. You enjoy working at the intersection of research and technology and take pride in enabling researchers to answer cutting-edge questions through robust and innovative software solutions. You are curious, proactive, and collaborative, and you communicate effectively with both academic researchers and technical experts. You bring a strong sense of ownership to your work, while remaining flexible and open to learning new tools, domains, and methodologies. You value software quality, sustainability, and reproducibility, and are eager to contribute to an open and inclusive research environment. Furthermore: You hold a master's degree or higher in a relevant scientific or technical field, such as Life Sciences, Bioinformatics, Computational Science, Computer Science, or a related discipline. You have demonstrated experience in academic research and in development of research software, methodologies, or open-source frameworks for research purposes. You have proven experience in developing research software, including testing, documenting, and applying FAIR principles to research software, and you have an interest in building sustainable software which is adopted by others. You have experience with computational research in the life sciences and with bringing existing research software to a more robust, maintainable and reusable state, for example through refactoring, modularisation, improving …

items.desc: The role We are seeking a highly motivated and enthusiastic Postdoctoral Research Associate for a Little Princess Trust/Children’s Cancer and Leukaemia Group funded “New Ideas” research project entitled “Using splice-switching oligonucleotides for cancer therapeutics”. The project builds on our recently published work demonstrating the spliceosomal vulnerability of neuroblastoma [Bojko etal, Cancer Letters 2024, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.canlet.2024.217263]. We propose that altering specific mRNA splicing events may selectively kill cancer cells, or sensitize them to chemotherapeutics. The applicant will deploy targeted antisense oligonucleotides to select genes for this purpose. The post will be for up to 12 months (full-time). What will you be doing? This project will require a strong understanding of gene regulation, in particular regulation by post-transcriptional mRNA splicing. You will be expected to show strong initiative and be responsible for the planning, execution, analysis and presentation of the project’s experiments. In addition to molecular/biochemical/cell biology techniques, the project may require expertise in bioinformatic analyses. You should apply if You are highly motivated to impact childhood cancer research. You hold a relevant PhD, or expect to be awarded one very soon. You need to possess high-level molecular/biochemical/cell biology practical skills, including ChIP,RNA immunoprecipitation, co-immunoprecipitation, qPCR, alternative splicing analysis, western-blotting, tissue-culture, confocal microscopy, immunocytochemistry, flow cytometry. You should also have some hands-on experience of bioinformatics for proteomics and transcriptomics Additional information Contract type: Fixed Term Contract - 12 months (Specialist skills) Work pattern: Full time / 35 hours per week Grade: I Salary: £40,704 - £45,641 per annum School/Unit: School of Biochemistry and Biomedical Sciences This advert will close at 23:59 UK time on Monday 16th November 2026 For informal queries please contact: Professor Karim Malik, Professor of Molecular Oncology via email: k.t.a.malik@bristol.ac.uk or tel: +44 (0)117-4550106 Our strategy and mission We recently launched our strategy to 2030 tying together our mission, vision and values. Tecnologías de bases de datos en cloud (p. ej. AWS) y despliegue en infraestructura cloud de datos/analítica. Contenedores y pipelines/microservicios (Docker, Kubernetes). Creemos en una cultura horizontal, sin egos, en un entorno donde se valoran tanto las ideas como las personas. Contrato indefinido y salario entre los 30.000 y 36.000 euros brutos/año de entrada, ajustado según tu experiencia (nuestro plan de carrera incluye 2 revisiones anuales). items.desc: FALU AG in Rüti (ZH) builds and sells swab production machines that run in plants around the world. With FALU PMAS, our cloud based production monitoring and assistance system, every machine reports its state every five seconds. Customers get live dashboards, shift KPIs, downtime analytics and automatic alerts in the browser. The first customer went live in September 2026 with eight machines, and more plants are lined up. The cloud side of PMAS is built and running in production: broker, ingestion service, databases, web app. The path from the PLC inside the machine to the MQTT broker is covered by one engineer who designed and built it. With more machines and more plants coming, that one person is no longer enough. We are looking for a freelancer who adds capacity on exactly this path: PLC software, Raspberry Pi edge devices, site gateway, broker connection. This is a permanent role that we staff on a freelance basis: no project end date, a long term engagement with about 1 week of work per month, with more when a rollout is on. You will work directly with our existing integration engineer, our inhouse engineering team and the CEO. Tasks You work on everything between the machine PLC and the MQTT broker, alongside the engineer who built the current setup. Which parts you take over completely and which you share depends on your strengths. Concretely: PLC and machine side Bring the PMAS message format into the CB1 machine software (Siemens S7, TIA Portal V18 with HMI) and keep it in sync with the payload contract: cumulative counters, machine status, error codes, timestamps from the PLC clock. Decide and implement how data leaves the PLC: MQTT publishing from the PLC itself, or a read on the edge device (S7 protocol or OPC UA) that publishes on its behalf. Pick one, justify it, standardise it. Manage PLC software versions across the fleet, including safe update and rollback procedures for machines already running at customers. Ensure clock discipline on the PLCs (NTP, local time zone per plant), since every duration KPI is computed from PLC timestamps. Edge devices and site gateway Develop and maintain the software on the Raspberry Pi based edge devices next to each machine: MQTT client, buffering and store and forward during uplink outages, unique client IDs, credential handling, health reporting. Develop and maintain the site gateway: isolated machine network, routing and firewall, outbound only TLS and NTP, remote maintenance access, watchdogs, recovery from a spare device. Help turn the current setup into a provisioning process: golden image, per machine configuration, fleet wide updates without a site visit. A new machine goes from unboxing to "visible in the dashboard" in under an hour. Monitor the edge layer so that we know about a degraded device before the customer does. Broker and data contract Administer the HiveMQ Cloud clusters per customer: credentials, topic ACLs, client ID scheme, certificates. Maintain the payload contract together with the existing integration engineer. Changes are versioned and documented. Commissioning and support Onboard new customers and new machines end to end, remotely where possible and on site where needed (primarily Europe and the United States). Act as second line when "the dashboard shows nothing" or "the numbers look wrong" and the cause sits between PLC and broker. Write the documentation you would have wanted on day one: onboarding sheets, runbooks, wiring notes. Requirements Must have Siemens PLC programming in TIA Portal (SCL and LAD, S7-1200/1500 family). You can open an existing machine project, understand it and change it without breaking the machine. Industrial networking: PROFINET, VLANs, static and DHCP setups, firewalls, TLS basics. You have connected a machine to a network that was not built for it. Linux on Raspberry Pi or comparable single board computers: systemd, networking, images, headless operation, remote administration. Solid programming skills in Python or Node.js for edge software, and Git as a daily tool. MQTT in depth: versions 3.1.1 and 5.0, QoS levels, retained messages, last will, TLS, broker ACLs. Proficiency with AI coding tools is a hard requirement. You use Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot or comparable tools every day, you write and maintain project instructions for them, you review their output critically, and you are measurably faster with them than without. Our code and documentation are written with and for these tools. If you see AI tools as optional, this role is not for you. Working proficiency in English (all code, commits and documentation are in English). German is a plus for the machine side. Willingness to travel to customer plants, typically a few days per quarter. Availability of at least two days per week on a permanent basis, with the option to scale up during rollouts. You work as a freelancer (own company or registered self employed) and can invoice FALU AG. Nice to have OPC UA, Snap7 or the Siemens open …

items.desc: Project Description Hiredbuddy is seeking a motivated Machine Learning Engineer to join our remote team. You will build, train, and evaluate machine learning models to solve real-world problems and support data-driven applications. Ideal for entry-level candidates with strong programming, analytical, and problem-solving skills and a passion for artificial intelligence. You'll work with Python, machine learning libraries, and data processing tools while gaining hands-on experience with real-world ML projects. This is a great opportunity to grow your career in a supportive and innovative environment. Full Description Hiredbuddy is looking for a detail-oriented and enthusiastic Machine Learning Engineer to join our growing team. This is an entry-level, remote position perfect for someone eager to launch their career in machine learning and artificial intelligence. You will work closely with data scientists, software engineers, and other teams to develop machine learning solutions that address business and technical challenges. In this role, you will be responsible for preparing datasets, developing machine learning models, evaluating model performance, and helping integrate ML solutions into applications. You will work with structured and unstructured data, identify patterns, and experiment with different algorithms to improve model accuracy and performance. You will also have the opportunity to collaborate with senior engineers and data scientists, gaining valuable mentorship and hands-on experience. Your daily tasks will include collecting and cleaning data, performing exploratory data analysis, preparing features, and training machine learning models using Python and libraries such as Scikit-learn, Pandas, and NumPy. You may work with supervised and unsupervised learning techniques, including classification, regression, clustering, and recommendation systems. You will also assist with model testing, performance evaluation, documentation, and optimization. As you grow in the role, you will have opportunities to work on more advanced projects involving deep learning, natural language processing, computer vision, and model deployment. You may also gain experience with tools and platforms such as TensorFlow, PyTorch, Docker, cloud services, and ML deployment workflows. At Hiredbuddy, we value curiosity, experimentation, problem-solving, and a willingness to learn. We provide a supportive environment where you can develop your technical skills through practical projects, learning resources, regular feedback, and mentorship. Our remote-first culture provides flexibility while encouraging collaboration through virtual meetings and communication tools. If you are passionate about machine learning and want to build intelligent solutions that make an impact, we encourage you to apply. We are looking for individuals who are proactive, analytical, communicative, and eager to grow their skills. Join us and be part of a team focused on innovation and excellence. Requirements Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Artificial Intelligence, Mathematics, Statistics, Engineering, or a related field 0-2 years of experience in machine learning, data science, or a related role (internships and academic projects count) Proficiency in Python programming Basic understanding of machine learning concepts and algorithms Experience with libraries such as Scikit-learn, Pandas, and NumPy Understanding of data preprocessing, feature engineering, and model evaluation Familiarity with supervised and unsupervised learning techniques Basic knowledge of statistics and probability Strong analytical and problem-solving skills Good understanding of algorithms and data structures Familiarity with Git or other version control systems Good communication skills, both written and verbal Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a remote environment Eagerness to learn new machine learning tools and technologies Benefits Professional development budget for courses and certifications Regular team-building activities and virtual events Hands-on experience with real-world machine learning projects Mentorship from experienced engineers and data scientists Opportunity for career growth in AI and machine learning

items.desc: Ben jij gepassioneerd over het omzetten van data naar waardevolle inzichten? Wil je werken aan uitdagende projecten voor toonaangevende enterprise-organisaties? Sluit je aan bij ons team als Data Scientist en help de toekomst van organisaties vorm te geven met innovatieve data-oplossingen die écht impact maken. Voor verschillende enterprise-klanten ontwikkelen we geavanceerde datamodellen en algoritmes om waardevolle inzichten uit uiteenlopende datasets te halen. Daarbij maken we gebruik van moderne technologieën en cloudplatformen zoals Azure, maar we zijn platformonafhankelijk en gaan elke technische uitdaging graag aan. Wat al onze projecten gemeen hebben, is dat data een cruciale rol speelt in de besluitvorming en dat de oplossingen daadwerkelijk in productie worden ingezet. Daarom staan datakwaliteit, betrouwbaarheid en een soepele integratie centraal. Daarnaast monitoren we continu de prestaties van onze oplossingen, zodat eventuele problemen tijdig worden gesignaleerd en opgelost. Je werkt aan uiteenlopende projecten in verschillende sectoren. Daardoor krijg je de kans om verschillende businessvraagstukken en databronnen te leren kennen en zowel je technische als domeinkennis verder uit te breiden. Wat ga je doen? Samenwerken met toonaangevende klanten uit verschillende sectoren en complexe businessvraagstukken oplossen. Geavanceerde machine learning-modellen en datagedreven strategieën ontwikkelen die direct bijdragen aan betere besluitvorming. Samenwerken met multidisciplinaire teams om impactvolle oplossingen te realiseren en succesvol te integreren binnen de IT-omgeving van de klant. Continu innoveren door nieuwe technieken en tools te verkennen en toe te passen, waarmee je zowel de projecten als je eigen ontwikkeling naar een hoger niveau tilt. Daarnaast hebben we een actieve community waarin we tijdens Tech Hours kennis delen, nieuwe tools demonstreren en ervaringen uitwisselen. Bonus op basis van jouw persoonlijke ontwikkeling en de gezamenlijke resultaten. Laptop en telefoon. Toegang tot de Itility Academy voor hard- en softskilltrainingen. Gebruik van professionele sportschool bij Itility. Hybride werken. Dit breng jij mee: Minimaal 3 jaar ervaring als Data Scientist of in een vergelijkbare rol. Ervaring met statistische modellering, predictive analytics en machine learning. Sterke programmeervaardigheden in Python. Ervaring met R, Julia of vergelijkbare programmeertalen is een pré. Ervaring met grote datasets en cloudgebaseerde dataplatformen zoals AWS, Azure of GCP. Het vermogen om businessvraagstukken te vertalen naar innovatieve data-oplossingen. Ervaring met machine learning-frameworks zoals TensorFlow, PyTorch of XGBoost. Ervaring met MLOps-oplossingen zoals MLflow of vergelijkbare tooling. Je bent een teamspeler en communiceert zowel in het Nederlands als in het Engels uitstekend. Een screening maakt onderdeel uit van de sollicitatieprocedure. It houses MareNostrum, one of the most powerful supercomputers in Europe, was a founding and hosting member of the former European HPC infrastructure PRACE (Partnership for Advanced Computing in Europe), and is now hosting entity for EuroHPC JU, the Joint Undertaking that leads large-scale investments and HPC provision in Europe. The mission of BSC is to research, develop and manage information technologies in order to facilitate scientific progress. BSC combines HPC service provision and R&D into both computer and computational science (life, earth and engineering sciences) under one roof, and currently has over 1000 staff from 60 countries. Look At The BSC Experience BSC-CNS YouTube Channel Let's stay connected with BSC Folks! We are particularly interested for this role in the strengths and lived experiences of women and underrepresented groups to help us avoid perpetuating biases and oversights in science and IT research. In instances of equal merit, the incorporation of the under-represented sex will be favoured. We promote Equity, Diversity and Inclusion, fostering an environment where each and every one of us is appreciated for who we are, regardless of our differences. If you consider that you do not meet all the requirements, we encourage you to continue applying for the job offer. items.desc: Fospha is dedicated to building the world's most powerful measurement solution for online retail. For over a decade, we've helped teams make smarter decisions with full-funnel marketing insights, forecasting, and optimisation. With Fospha, every team moves faster and grows smarter. About The Role We're looking for a Data Scientist to join Fospha's Data Science team in London, working within our Stream 3 workstream. Fospha builds marketing measurement products for ecommerce brands — attribution, marketing mix modelling, incrementality testing, and brand impact measurement. Our Data Science team owns the models behind all of it, from methodology through to production code. You will have the chance to work across our technical stack to make real code impacts on codebases. This role suits someone with some commercial data science experience behind them who wants to go deeper. You’ll take on interesting but challenging work with a supportive team structure and a company that rewards high agency with ownership. Team: Data Science Level: Developing (Data Science Career Development Framework) Location: London What you'll do Own moderately difficult tickets end to end — analytical investigations, model backtesting, production bug fixes, and pipeline work, with decreasing need for step-by-step direction Debug systematically across our codebases — including repositories you're only partly familiar with, using AI tooling to get up to speed quickly Write and review production code — Python and SQL that avoids technical debt, plus reviewing AI-assisted code so it lands with minimal bugs Use our QA automation and cloud tooling effectively — running validation properly and understanding the data science parts of our AWS pipelines Communicate with clients and colleagues — explaining methodology and findings directly, with only minor assistance from senior colleagues Push for clarity up front — working directly with other teams to pin down acceptance criteria and requirements, rather than sitting blocked waiting on them Start becoming an internal data science champion — the person other teams come to on the areas you own What we're looking for Essential Some commercial data science experience — typically 1–2 years, or a strong placement/internship record alongside a quantitative degree Strong Python and SQL, with the ability to collaborate on shared code and avoid technical debt Deep knowledge of a handful of machine learning algorithms — not breadth for its own sake, but real understanding of a few methods and when they apply Able to systematically debug unfamiliar code, using AI tooling to accelerate rather than to guess while still understanding problem fully Strong AI fluency — you understand how to optimally start a task with AI, you use it to unblock cross-team dependencies, and you always QA the output for accuracy and brevity before it goes anywhere Confident completing work independently once scope is agreed Able to communicate with clients and colleagues with only minor assistance Genuine attention to detail — much of this work involves noticing when a number is wrong Nice to have Experience with AWS or comparable cloud tooling Familiarity with automated QA tooling and test coverage practices Any experience with marketing, ecommerce, or advertising data Exposure to Bayesian methods, marketing mix modelling, or experimental design Not required You do not need prior experience with marketing mix modelling, attribution methodology, incrementality testing, or Bayesian modelling. These are taught here, and we'd rather hire someone who learns fast than someone who arrives pre-loaded. How You'll Grow We run a published Data Science Career Development Framework with six levels. You'd join at Developing, where the expectations are: AI Fluency & Tooling: Understands how to optimally start all relevant tasks with AI; confident completing work independently; uses AI to push for acceptance criteria and limit cross-department dependencies; always QAs AI output for accuracy and brevity. Machine Learning & Modelling: Deep knowledge of a handful of algorithms, and familiarity with the full Fospha model suite. Engineering & Codebase: Systematically debugs issues with AI support, even in partly familiar repositories; uses supplied AWS tooling efficiently and understands the data science parts of the pipelines; uses existing QA automation effectively; avoids technical debt and collaborates well on code; reviews AI-assisted code so it ships with minimal bugs. Stakeholder & Communication: Communicates with clients and colleagues with minor assistance. Job Complexity: Undertakes moderately difficult tickets while starting to become an internal data science champion. Supervision: Receives detailed instruction, but becomes progressively less dependent on senior colleagues. items.desc: Software Developer — Build Your Own Project with an AI Coding Assistant About The Role What if you could get paid to work on the project you've been meaning to build — with a state-of-the-art AI coding assistant at your side, completely free of charge? We're looking for software developers in the Stockholm area to bring their own projects and build them using an AI-powered coding assistant. You write real code on real projects you care about. We learn from your expert judgment on how the assistant performed. You keep full ownership of everything you build. This is a fully remote, flexible contract role designed for developers who want to ship their own work — and get compensated for it. Organization: Alignerr Type: Hourly Contract Location: Fully Remote Commitment: Flexible What You'll Do Bring a software project you personally own — a side project, a tool, an open-source library, or something you've been meaning to finish Build features, fix bugs, refactor code, write docs, or do whatever your project needs — using an AI coding assistant At each step, compare two versions of the assistant's response, choose the better one, and write a brief explanation of your reasoning Work in your own environment, on your own schedule, with your own tools Who You Are A developer with a software project you personally own, stored in a git repository Comfortable working in the terminal and with git-based workflows Running macOS, Linux, or Windows with WSL2 Able to write clear, honest evaluations — you'll explain your choices in a few sentences Self-motivated and reliable when working independently Open-source maintainers are especially welcome What's Eligible Software projects that you personally and solely own Open-source projects with an approved license If your project has other maintainers, mention it in your application — we'll confirm eligibility What's Not Eligible Work owned by an employer, client, university, company, or startup Projects under NDA AI model training or evaluation projects; ML infrastructure Security exploit tooling Projects that process other people's personal data Good to Know Before starting, you'll sign short contributor terms and we'll approve your project Transcripts of your coding sessions are used to improve AI models and cannot be withdrawn after submission — this covers sessions only, not the rest of your codebase Your ratings and written feedback become part of the project's deliverables During sessions: no passwords, API keys, or other people's personal data — and you write your ratings yourself, without AI help Why You'll Love This Your project, your code — you keep full ownership of everything, including code the assistant writes for you Free AI tokens — your AI usage during sessions is fully covered, no subscription or API bill needed Paid to build what you'd build anyway — real compensation for real development work on your own project Fully remote and flexible — work from your own computer, on your own schedule Shape the future of AI-assisted coding — your expert judgment directly improves the next generation of developer tools Spots are limited — the first cohort is small and starting soon

items.desc: En tant qu'organisateur de forums de recrutement, Talents Handicap accompagne de très nombreuses entreprises & organisations en France dans leurs recrutements de collaborateurs en situation de handicap. Participant actuellement à l'un de nos forums. L'entreprise Wavestone recherche actuellement des profils : Dans un monde où savoir se transformer est la clé du succès, l'ambition de Wavestone est d'apporter à ses clients des réponses uniques sur le marché, en les éclairant et les guidant dans leurs décisions les plus stratégiques. Wavestone est un nouveau cabinet de conseil, issu du rapprochement début 2016 de Solucom et des activités européennes de Kurt Salmon (à l'exclusion de consumer goods & retail en dehors de France). Notre cabinet rassemble 2800 collaborateurs présents sur 4 continents, figure parmi les leaders indépendants du conseil en Europe, et constitue le 1er cabinet de conseil indépendant en France. Pour satisfaire nos clients, nous développons 18 terrains d’excellence, à la fois sectoriels, fonctionnels, et technologiques. Sur chacun d’eux, nous nous engageons à apporter à nos clients une profondeur d’expertise de premier plan. Mais surtout, et c’est là le cœur de notre proposition de valeur, nous combinons ces 18 terrains d’excellence sans couture et sans silos. Enfin, pour enrichir notre offre, nous investissons dans 5 assets à forte valeur ajoutée : le Research Knowledge Center, parce que pour prendre de bonnes décisions il faut de bonnes informations, le Creadesk, qui permet de stimuler la créativité et l’innovation, la Faktory, pour prototyper des idées en mode « test and learn », le Machine Learning et Data Lab, pour exploiter les gisements de valeur qui se cachent dans les données de nos clients et Shake Up', pour accompagner des start-ups dans leur croissance et leur développement. Nous recrutons des talents aux parcours diversifiés, de tous niveaux d'expérience. Des personnalités engagées, reconnues pour leur goût d'entreprendre et leur esprit d'équipe. Venez vivre une expérience unique au sein de Wavestone ! \n\n Description de l'entreprise Rejoignez un cabinet de conseil international qui accompagne les grandes transformations stratégiques. Nous sommes Wavestone : des expert·es passionné·es et orienté·es solutions, qui placent l’humain au cœur de la performance et de la croissance. Ambitieux·ses et en pleine expansion, nous développons sans cesse notre portefeuille de clients et de projets, avec une portée internationale et une réelle volonté de générer un impact positif. Êtes-vous un vrai team player, porté par des valeurs fortes ? Êtes-vous curieux·se et déterminé·e, avec l’envie d’apprendre chaque jour ? Êtes-vous du genre à relever les défis sans hésiter ? Alors vous êtes au bon endroit. Rejoignez Wavestone et exprimez votre potentiel dans un environnement stimulant et collaboratif, où l’on transforme les défis d’aujourd’hui en opportunités de demain. Pour plus d'informations, consulter www.wavestone.com Description du poste Contexte Dans un environnement de plus en plus complexe, l’agilité des chaînes d’approvisionnement est devenue un levier stratégique incontournable pour assurer la résilience et la performance des entreprises. Parallèlement, l’IA connaît une croissance fulgurante et transforme en profondeur les modes de décision, de pilotage et d’anticipation. Ses applications dans la supply chain – de la prévision de la demande à la gestion des stocks, en passant par l’optimisation des transports – suscitent un intérêt croissant. Au-delà de l’analyse du marché, les entreprises cherchent désormais à traduire ces innovations en cas d’usage opérationnels. La création d’agents IA spécialisés peut faciliter l’accès à l’information et l’aide à la décision, tandis que l’amélioration des prévisions sur les lancements de collections constitue un enjeu particulièrement structurant pour les acteurs du Retail et du Luxe. Comment transformer le potentiel de l’IA en usages concrets, fiables et créateurs de valeur pour les processus de planification Supply Chain ? Objectif du stage Encadré.e par un.e chef.fe de projet expérimenté.e, vous aurez l’opportunité de contribuer à un sujet prospectif et innovant au cœur des enjeux actuels de la supply chain, en lien avec l’émergence de l’intelligence artificielle. Votre stage s’articulera autour de deux grands axes : Une étude de fond visant à approfondir les applications actuelles et potentielles de l’IA dans les processus de planification de la supply chain, avec un focus sur la création d’un agent IA pour un cas d’usage précis et sur les prévisions liées aux lancements de collections dans le Retail et le Luxe. Cette étude s’appuiera sur le benchmark existant et aboutira à la formalisation de recommandations et de livrables réutilisables en interne et/ou valorisables sur les canaux de communication de Wavestone. items.desc: About Us We’re living through a Cambrian explosion of intelligence: new models and new chips, each specialised for different tasks, are arriving all at once. The result is a new era for AI, one of radical heterogeneity. Callosum is the Intelligent Systems Company. We believe the next generation of AI won't be defined by any single model or chip, but by intelligent systems in which hardware and intelligence co-evolve. We are building the infrastructure that unifies heterogeneous compute across the full stack. This opens a new axis of scaling intelligence: a dynamic system that tailors itself to what each workload actually needs, whether that's speed, cost, precision, or whatever unit comes next. The last era scaled on a different bet: one bigger model, more of the same chip, more data. That bet is running into structural limits. Frontier models offer extraordinary capability at unsustainable cost, one that today's monolithic infrastructure was never designed to serve. Our founding principle is that intelligence comes from many specialised systems working together, not from any single component. We build the software orchestration layer that co-evolves models, workflows and silicon into one system, delivering inference tailored to every workload, and demonstrating orders-of-magnitude leaps in capability and cost. Because our software spans the full stack, our engineering team works directly with heterogeneous accelerators and frontier silicon, including Cerebras, d-Matrix, Intel, NVIDIA, AMD, Normal Computing, Tenstorrent, GreatSky, and Mixx. We are not stopping at today's chips: each new generation of silicon unlocks algorithms that couldn't run before, and we intend to be first to them, every time. If we get it right, it will belong to everyone building on it - not to any single vendor. In our latest funding round, we raised $100M, led by Atomico with participation from Plural, DCVC and the UK Sovereign AI Fund’s first investment. With this, we are building the infrastructure for the next era of intelligence. We are engineers and scientists based in London, working across the full depth of the stack. We are curious, intellectually honest, and building what doesn't exist yet. If you thrive on uncharted territory and are energised by the scale of the challenge, we'd love to hear from you. About The Role Choosing between algorithmic strategies for multi-step LLM work is a measurement problem, and most teams solve it badly: comparisons run case by case, by whoever needs them that week, on whatever task is closest to hand. That doesn't scale, and it doesn't hold up to outside scrutiny - from a customer, or from a reviewer. Callosum needs one benchmarking system: reproducible, contamination-controlled, and trusted enough to be the evidence that decides which approach ships. This role owns that system. You will build a harness that measures task success, quality, and robustness across motifs, agent topologies, and decomposition strategies, grounded in execution - real commits, real traces, sandboxed grading - rather than self-reported or model-graded scores. The results become the proof points we show customers, the evidence behind the benchmarks we co-publish, and the basis on which an approach ships or doesn't. This is a research hire that builds. We expect the rigour of a strong evaluation paper applied to a production system, and the engineering ability to design, build, and curate it yourself rather than hand it off. What You'll Build Design and build a unified system for evaluating agentic and algorithmic solutions - task success, quality, and robustness across motifs, agent topologies, and decomposition strategies, on workloads that match what customers actually run. Cost per resolved task is an outcome you track, not the object of the exercise. Mine real commits and traces, run sandboxed execution grading, and build task suites that reflect real agentic work: code search, code edit and repair, repository summarisation, tool use. Self-reported or model-graded success isn't enough on its own. Enforce controls against contamination, overfitting to benchmarks, and metric gaming, and keep baselines stable over time - any result should be re-runnable to the same number, by us or by a reviewer Compare algorithmic and agentic approaches honestly, not models or chips - a motif that adds steps, latency, or cost has to earn it in resolved-task quality, and the system says clearly when it doesn't Lead external benchmark co-publications, held to a standard that survives peer and customer review Feed results directly into which approach ships, into the proof points behind customer engagements, and review quality claims across the company before they go out What You'll Bring PhD in computer science, machine learning, or a related field, or an equivalent research track record Authorship or co-authorship of a benchmark or evaluation paper at a recognised venue - NeurIPS Datasets and Benchmarks, ICML, ICLR, ACL - ideally …

About The Role Callosum believes that orders of magnitude improvements in AI systems will come through application-aware orchestration across heterogeneous models and hardware. Our team is developing the science that makes that possible: a principled, evidence-based method for building agentic systems automatically at unprecedented scale. The team tackles these problems on two fronts. We build the tools to analyse and evaluate agentic systems rigorously enough to say where and why they go wrong, and we use what we learn to design better ones. We are not simply building a better harness; the best harness will change with every new model, task and generation of silicon. We are building the layer beneath it, so that design decisions follow from evidence rather than taste. This role owns the first of those fronts. Agentic evaluation today is not up to the job: benchmarks saturate, scores move for reasons unrelated to capability, results fail to reproduce across runs, and a single number tells you nothing about which step went wrong. Every design decision the rest of the team makes rests on the quality of that instrument. You will build measures whose construct we can defend, whose variance we understand, and which localise a failure rather than merely scoring it. The mandate is broad, and most of the questions inside it are still unanswered. You will have wide latitude to choose problems, and your results will shape what the company builds in the future. What You'll Build Design benchmarks and evaluation suites for agentic behaviour – multi-turn, long-horizon, tool-using, operating in non-stationary environments – including the properties that are hard to score, such as reliability and recovery from error Build the methodology as well as the harness: statistical power, variance across runs, contamination and construct validity Be the independent voice on the quality of our own results. items.desc: Au sein du département de R&D « AI In Silico » d’Evotec, plus de 100 scientifiques issus de divers horizons – biologie, informatique, mathématiques et biomédecine – travaillent ensemble pour analyser et interpréter des ensembles de données omiques complexes. En étroite collaboration avec nos chercheurs en laboratoire, nous développons, exploitons et améliorons en permanence des plateformes omiques à haut débit et haute précision. Dans le cadre de programmes multidisciplinaires de découverte de médicaments, nous collaborons avec des experts issus d’un large éventail de disciplines scientifiques au sein d’une organisation mondiale comptant plus de 5 000 collaborateurs à travers le monde. Notre travail couvre la gestion et le contrôle qualité des données omiques, le développement de méthodes et de logiciels, l’analyse avancée des données, ainsi que l’interprétation biologique des résultats. Notre mission consiste à générer des connaissances exploitables qui permettent de prendre de meilleures décisions et d’accélérer le développement de médicaments qui font la différence. Afin de renforcer notre groupe d’oncologie computationnelle, nous recherchons un(e) candidat(e) très motivé(e) Bioinformaticien - biologie computationnelle CDI à temps plein Vos Principales Responsabilités Accompagner les chercheurs en oncologie au sein d’équipes de projet interdisciplinaires en apportant votre expertise en oncologie, en bioinformatique et en analyse de données. Contribuer à des projets de découverte de médicaments grâce à l’analyse de divers ensembles de données omiques générés en interne ou provenant de sources publiques. Vos Qualifications Idéales Doctorat en bioinformatique, biologie computationnelle, oncologie ou dans un domaine connexe, avec au moins 2 ans d’expérience postdoctorale ou en entreprise, de préférence dans la découverte de médicaments. This is your opportunity to deliver end-to-end machine learning solutions that directly impact customer engagement and order growth. We're building JET's recommendation systems, generating personalised carousels of restaurants to help people find their order right on the home page of the app. We're looking for someone who can live our behaviours of lead, deliver and care while bringing technical excellence and innovation. This role sits at the intersection of cutting-edge AI as we integrate, train and develop ML and generative models into a live production environment. Help us compute data at scale for millions of users to help people find the food they want. We need someone who can challenge assumptions, translate ambiguous business problems into elegant technical solutions, and ship production-quality ML systems that make a measurable difference to our customers and partners. Apply generative AI and LLM techniques to personalisation challenges at scale, generating recommendations for millions of customers Own your results by designing, running and interpreting A/B experiments with statistical rigour, measuring real impact on business metrics and holding yourself accountable. Collaborate with ML engineers to productionise models, implementing MLOps best practices and maintaining monitored pipelines that deliver consistent value. Break down silos by translating complex business questions into clear modelling approaches and communicating results effectively to product and commercial stakeholders. Be determined to take end-to-end ownership of well-scoped workstreams, independently framing problems, choosing approaches, running experiments and presenting findings. The position is offered until 31/05/2028 in the
items.desc: Magnesium alloys offer exceptional lightweighting potential for aerospace and space applications, but their wider use in extreme environments is limited by challenges including microstructural instability, temperature fluctuations and irradiation-induced damage. At the same time, oxide inclusions formed during casting and manufacturing are conventionally regarded as detrimental to structural performance. This project seeks to turn these"liabilities into assets" by exploiting solid-state, friction-based manufacturing to create finely dispersed oxide nanoparticles in magnesium alloys, enabling the development of oxide-dispersion-strengthened (ODS) magnesium alloys with enhanced thermal stability, high-temperature performance and radiation resistance. You will work within the research group led by Dr Dikai Guan at the University of Southampton on an NSF-EPSRC research project. The project brings together the University of Southampton, Baylor University, UK National Ion Beam Centre, integrating alloy processing, friction-based manufacturing, multiscale characterisation, modelling and extreme-environment testing. The position is offered until 31/05/2028 in the first instance, with the possibility of extension for up to 1 further year. The Research Fellow will be a major contributor to the experimental research activities at the University of Southampton, including: Feedstock alloy development and characterisation Multiscale microstructure characterisation Cryogenic and thermal-cycling testing Radiation-resistance testing You will have a good track record in carrying out independent and original scientific research, and publication of research papers. You should have the ability to work and communicate efficiently with other members of the team (supervisors, students and postdocs), and collaborators outside the University. Regular reports of research progress are required, and research plans should be adjusted accordingly. Critical analysis of experimental results and problem solving skills are essential to this role. You will also be required to write research papers for publication in high impact research journals and attend/present at relevant conferences. There will be an opportunity to supervisor PhD and Master students as a secondary supervisor. You should hold a PhD (or near completion)/ relevant experience in materials science or a relevant discipline. Research experience in physical metallurgy, metallic materials and advanced microstructure characterisation is particularly relevant to this position. Experience with SEM/EDS and EBSD, together with TEM/STEM or related high-resolution characterisation techniques, is highly desirable. Experience in oxide-dispersion-strengthened materials, metal casting, friction-based processing, cryogenic testing, thermal cycling, ion irradiation, or other advanced characterisation methods would be advantageous. Equality, diversity and inclusion are central to the ethos in the School of Engineering. We give full consideration to applicants who wish to work flexibly including part-time and due consideration will be given to applicants who have taken a career break. The University has onsite childcare facilities and we foster a good work-life balance. We also offer a mentorship programme and the school runs a women-oriented network event on a bi-weekly basis. The University of Southampton is in the top 1% of world universities and the top 10 of the UK’s research-intensive universities. We are committed to sustainability and being a globally responsible university, with the principles of sustainability embedded into all aspects of our individual and collective work, in our business planning, policy-making, and professional activities. For further information please contact Dr Dikai Guan dikai.guan@soton.ac.uk

items.desc: About Us We’re living through a Cambrian explosion of intelligence: new models and new chips, each specialised for different tasks, are arriving all at once. The result is a new era for AI, one of radical heterogeneity. Callosum is the Intelligent Systems Company. We believe the next generation of AI won't be defined by any single model or chip, but by intelligent systems in which hardware and intelligence co-evolve. We are building the infrastructure that unifies heterogeneous compute across the full stack. This opens a new axis of scaling intelligence: a dynamic system that tailors itself to what each workload actually needs, whether that's speed, cost, precision, or whatever unit comes next. The last era scaled on a different bet: one bigger model, more of the same chip, more data. That bet is running into structural limits. Frontier models offer extraordinary capability at unsustainable cost, one that today's monolithic infrastructure was never designed to serve. Our founding principle is that intelligence comes from many specialised systems working together, not from any single component. We build the software orchestration layer that co-evolves models, workflows and silicon into one system, delivering inference tailored to every workload, and demonstrating orders-of-magnitude leaps in capability and cost. Because our software spans the full stack, our engineering team works directly with heterogeneous accelerators and frontier silicon, including Cerebras, d-Matrix, Intel, NVIDIA, AMD, Normal Computing, Tenstorrent, GreatSky, and Mixx. We are not stopping at today's chips: each new generation of silicon unlocks algorithms that couldn't run before, and we intend to be first to them, every time. If we get it right, it will belong to everyone building on it - not to any single vendor. In our latest funding round, we raised $100M, led by Atomico with participation from Plural, DCVC and the UK Sovereign AI Fund’s first investment. With this, we are building the infrastructure for the next era of intelligence. We are engineers and scientists based in London, working across the full depth of the stack. We are curious, intellectually honest, and building what doesn't exist yet. If you thrive on uncharted territory and are energised by the scale of the challenge, we'd love to hear from you. About The Role Callosum believes that the next generation of AI systems will be co-optimised across models, software, and hardware. As we operate across increasingly heterogeneous workloads and accelerators, the number of possible system configurations grows combinatorially. Manually exploring that space does not scale – we need systems that can search it themselves. This role owns Callosum’s program evolution and optimisation loop: an LLM-guided search system that iteratively generates, evaluates, and improves programs against verifiable objectives. We already use this approach across kernels, inference runtimes, scheduling and scaling policies, KV caching strategies, and more. You will develop the loop both as a reusable internal optimisation system and as a research object in its own right, improving how it searches, measuring what makes it effective, and pushing its capabilities on increasingly difficult optimisation and reasoning problems. What You'll Build Develop the core program evolution loop, improving how candidates are generated, evaluated, selected, and evolved over long optimisation runs Design search strategies that balance exploration, exploitation, diversity, and sample efficiency across vast and irregular optimisation spaces Build continuous benchmarks that measure the optimiser across internal workloads and standalone problems, making improvements and regressions empirically visible Turn the system into reliable internal infrastructure that can optimise new verifiable domains as a reusable internal tool that other team members can scale to new problems What Sets You Apart Strong foundations in optimisation and search, including familiarity with evolutionary, stochastic, combinatorial, or other non-gradient-based methods Ability to reason about search itself i.e. exploration versus exploitation, diversity, pruning, objective design, and when different optimisation strategies are appropriate Strong engineering instincts, with experience turning experimental systems into reusable, measurable, and reliable software A demonstrable tendency to draw from techniques across optimisation, algorithms, and machine learning rather than treating LLMs as the solution to every problem What We Offer Competitive Salary, determined by skills and experience Equity & Ownership Private healthcare We offer Visa sponsorship and relocation benefits to hire the best in the world We work in person at our London office. items.desc: We're assembling a group of senior software and ML engineers to work on one of the hardest open problems in AI today: how well can frontier models reason about LLM inference systems, GPU-level performance optimization, and model-serving architecture? Strong Linux skills across RHEL, Rocky Linux, and Ubuntu, combined with shell scripting for automation, benchmark execution, and performance analysis. items.title: Wissenschaftlicher Mitarbeiter/Wissenschaftliche Mitarbeiterin (m/w/d) Else Kröner Fresenius-Zentrum
items.card: Ihre Aufgaben Identifikation, Auswahl und Aufbereitung geeigneter histologischer Bilddatensätze für die Entwicklung und Validierung von KI-Modellen Entwicklung, Implementierung und Optimierung von Deep-Learning-Modellen für histologische Bilddaten mit PyTorch Konzeption und Implementierung effizienter Daten- und Trainingspipelines, einschließlich Datenladen, Vorverarbeitung und Training Optimierung und Portierung
items.desc: Bewerbungsfrist: 25.10.2026 Befristung: 24 Monate Arbeitszeit: Voll- und Teilzeit Stellenanzeigen ID: 2139 Das Universitätsklinikum Carl Gustav Carus und die Medizinische Fakultät bilden gemeinsam die Dresdner Hochschulmedizin. Sie ist zur Exzellenz in der Hochleistungsmedizin, der medizinischen Forschung und Lehre sowie der Gesundheitsdienstleistung für Patient*innen der gesamten Region verpflichtet. Gemeinsam für die Spitzenmedizin von morgen – werden Sie Teil der Hochschulmedizin Dresden. Wissenschaftlicher Mitarbeiter/ Wissenschaftliche Mitarbeiterin (m/w/d) am Else Kröner Fresenius Zentrum für Digitale Gesundheit Die Stelle ist zum nächstmöglichen Zeitpunkt in Voll- oder Teilzeitbeschäftigung für 24 Monate befristet zu besetzen, mit der Option auf Verlängerung und längerfristige Zusammenarbeit. Die Vergütung erfolgt nach den Eingruppierungsvorschriften des Tarifvertrages für den öffentlichen Dienst (TV-L) und ist bei Vorliegen der persönlichen Voraussetzungen in die Entgeltgruppe E13 möglich. Die Stelle ist im Rahmen des Forschungsprojekts “MedSecureAI – Zertifizierbare Chip-Plattform für sichere KI-Akzelerator-Integration in der bildbasierten medizinischen Detektion” zu besetzen. Das Projekt ist Teil des Zukunftsclusters SEMECO und verbindet Forschung aus medizinischer KI, digitaler Pathologie, Edge Computing und vertrauenswürdigen Hardwareplattformen. Ziel des Projekts ist die Entwicklung und Validierung einer modularen, sicheren und ressourceneffizienten Plattform für KI-gestützte medizinische Bildanalyse. Im medizinischen Anwendungsszenario werden KI-Modelle für die digitale Pathologie entwickelt, zunächst auf leistungsfähiger GPU-Infrastruktur trainiert und anschließend für die lokale Ausführung am Mikroskop auf ressourcenbeschränkter Edge-Hardware optimiert. Ein Demonstrator soll die direkte, erklärbare Analyse histologischer Bilddaten am Mikroskop ermöglichen. Die Position wird in einem interdisziplinären und internationalen Forschungsumfeld in der Forschungsgruppe von Marco Gustav, PhD am Else Kröner Fresenius Zentrum für Digitale Gesundheit der TU Dresden angesiedelt sein und eng mit akademischen Einrichtungen und Praxispartnern zusammenarbeiten. items.card: The role You lead our research on AI agents that reason over confidential data across organisations without leaking it. You define what “no leakage” means, how to measure it and how to prove it. You also design the secure link between a private deployment on a customer’s own servers and our public cloud platform, which a distributed-systems engineer in the team builds. Why this role An open problem where formal
items.desc: Make AI privacy provable: define, measure and prove what AI agents can leak when they reason over confidential data. About Serinyx Serinyx builds AI for high-stakes decisions on confidential data. On our decision-intelligence platform, AI agents break a hard question down, research it with checked citations and debate the findings under human review. The result is a verified, cited and signed report. Our second product gives universities and research institutes an always-current, AI-built view of their research. We were founded in Saarbrücken in 2026 and are now building our engineering team. The role You lead our research on AI agents that reason over confidential data across organisations without leaking it. You define what “no leakage” means, how to measure it and how to prove it. You also design the secure link between a private deployment on a customer’s own servers and our public cloud platform, which a distributed-systems engineer in the team builds. Why this role An open problem where formal methods, cryptography and LLMs meet. Your theory goes straight into a working system, built by an engineer in the team. You lead the research agenda and write up the results for a peer-reviewed venue. What you will do in your first year Define, formally, a measurable bound on what a debate between AI agents can leak, and build and validate an estimator for it. Design the link between the private and public sides: the protocol agents use to exchange arguments across it, and the proof that protected data cannot cross it directly. Design, with our CTO, how the checks that protect confidential data can be proven to an outside auditor. Set the measurement method, run the main leakage measurements and write up the results for a peer-reviewed venue. What you bring A PhD (or a submitted thesis) in computer science, security, cryptography or a related field. Formal methods or information-flow control: non-interference, security type systems, protocol verification. Statistics for estimation: confidence bounds, variance reduction. Publications at strong security, formal-methods or machine-learning venues. Enough Python to build and run your own experiments. Nice to have Zero-knowledge proofs; multi-agent LLM systems; Tamarin, ProVerif, TLA+, Lean or Coq. How we work One team, one backlog. Everyone builds from day one and works directly with our CTO, Dr Raja Naeem Akram. Owners, not ticket-takers. Each engineer owns parts of the codebase and leads the AI coding agents working in them: writing their work orders, reviewing every pull request and deciding what merges. A typical week. Much of your time goes into specifying and reviewing work done by AI coding agents; the hardest parts you write yourself. AI agents take the routine platform work. Infrastructure, deployment and monitoring are done by AI agents under engineering review, so your time goes into design and the hard problems. You still own what you build once it is live. Quality is part of the job. You write the tests for your own work and keep CI green. Done means tests pass, security scans are clean, docs are updated and container images are signed. Two-week cycles. Planning on day one, a demo on day ten and a short written retro. English first. English is our working language; German is welcome but not required. What we offer Real ownership. An early role in a small team: you shape the product, the code and how we work, not a ticket queue. A modern stack. Python, FastAPI, Temporal, Kubernetes, React with TypeScript, and the best AI models for each task. Saarbrücken, hybrid. We are based in one of Europe’s leading centres for computer science, and we work hybrid. 30 days of holidays per year. International applicants welcome. If you come from outside the EU, we support you through the work-permit process, usually the EU Blue Card. How to apply Send your CV and one link that shows your work (code, a paper or a project you built) to contact@serinyx.com with the job title in the subject line. English or German is fine. The process has three steps: a call with our CTO, a technical interview on a problem typical of the role, with your usual AI tools, and a conversation with the founders. Equal opportunity We welcome applications from everyone, whatever their ethnic origin, gender, religion or belief, disability, age or sexual identity. You don’t need to include a photo or your date of birth. Job Type: Full-time Pay: 63.600,00€ - 71.200,00€ per year Work Location: Hybrid remote in 66111 Saarbrücken

items.desc: Our Future Health is building the UK’s largest health research programme. To grow and improve it, we need to understand what works, what doesn’t and why. Our Experimentation & Insights team helps colleagues answer those questions through surveys, experiments, pilots and analysis. We’re looking for a Research Scientist for our Health Questionnaires squad, with strong experience in psychometrics and questionnaire research. You’ll help validate and improve screening and health research questionnaires, working closely with a questionnaire scientist developing new measures. We’re interested in more than whether a questionnaire meets standard measures of reliability and validity. We want someone who looks closely at the evidence: how people respond, where patterns emerge, which questions may be working differently for different groups, and what the data suggests should happen next. You’ll bring curiosity and sound research judgement to questionnaire testing, with the ability to choose the right methods and explain what the findings mean in practice. The role You’ll take research projects from initial question through to insight and recommendations. This includes shaping research plans and protocols, selecting appropriate methods and samples, programming and quality assuring surveys, analysing results and communicating findings to stakeholders. Questionnaire validation and psychometrics will be an important part of your work. You’ll also contribute to wider experimentation and test-and-learn activity, helping teams understand outcomes, refine success measures and decide what to do next. The role suits someone with substantial research training and a strong applied track record. You may have a PhD or MSc with significant relevant industry experience, particularly in pharmaceuticals, clinical trials, health research or a related field. We welcome candidates whose expertise has developed in academic or commercial settings. Are you excited by the challenge of combining data, simulation, and policy to tackle the world’s biggest health problems? The Centre for Health Economics & Policy Innovation (CHEPI) at Imperial Business School is seeking a Research Associate / Research Fellow in Computational Health Policy Modelling to play a central role in developing Health-GPS — our state-of-the-art microsimulation model for non-communicable disease (NCD) policy analysis. Appointment will be made at Research Associate or Research Fellow level, depending on experience. Why This Role Matters Chronic diseases such as diabetes and cardiovascular disease remain leading causes of illness and premature death worldwide. Yet, the tools available to evaluate and design effective prevention policies are still evolving. Health-GPS provides a framework to explore how changes in diet, physical activity, and related risk factors affect long-term population health and economic outcomes. Health-GPS represents the gradual accumulation and interaction of individual-level risk factors — such as BMI, diet, and income — offering insights into the potential impact of different policy interventions over time. You will help develop and apply this model across major international projects including: GOLDFINCH – estimating the effects of fiscal policies on ultra-processed food consumption. JA Prevent NCD – a European Joint Action on integrated strategies for NCD prevention. JACARDI – a European initiative to reduce cardiovascular and diabetes risk. Working with economists, epidemiologists, and data scientists, you’ll push the boundaries of policy simulation and shape real-world decision-making. This is a hands-on computational role. Alongside using Health-GPS for policy analysis, you will write, test and review code in its C++ codebase, working within the team’s collaborative development workflow (version control, pull requests and code review). C++ experience is highly desirable, but we also welcome strong programmers in other relevant languages who are willing to work in C++. What you would be doing Contribute to the architecture, development, optimisation, and maintenance of Health-GPS, writing and reviewing code in its C++ codebase and ensuring its continued scientific and policy relevance. Work with colleagues to plan and deliver modelling work across multiple projects, producing high-quality outputs on time. The successful candidate will contribute to the preclinical evaluation of novel therapeutic agents in animal models of cerebral ischemia, with particular emphasis on the middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) model. items.desc: At OneSpan, we specialize in digital identity and anti-fraud solutions that create exceptional and secure experiences. We are looking for the first ML research hire on the team. Your job will be to turn our telemetry into new detection and prevention capabilities: from understanding the problem alongside the Security team, to ideating, prototyping, and validating models and algorithms on real data. We are not looking for someone who applies recipes. We are looking for someone who enjoys tackling an open problem with an adversary that adapts, and who can move comfortably between the paper and the working prototype. Here Is a Little Taste Of Your Challenge Work side by side with the Security team to understand current and emerging attack techniques against mobile apps, and translate them into well-framed data problems. Explore and analyze our telemetry (datalake on ClickHouse and S3) to uncover signals, patterns, and anomalies with detection value. Design, prototype, and evaluate attack detection and prevention models: anomaly detection, classification with scarce labels, behavioral models, event time-series analysis. Define how success is measured: detection metrics, acceptable false-positive rates, and evaluation methodology when complete ground truth doesn't exist. Take validated prototypes toward production in collaboration with the engineering team, and lay the foundations (features, datasets, labeling processes) for the team's ML capability to grow. Stay current with research in ML applied to security (anomaly detection, adversarial ML, fraud) and bring actionable ideas. Who are you? Proven experience (5+ years, or PhD plus applied experience) researching and developing ML models on real-world problems, ideally in security, fraud, anti-bot, anti-malware, or similar adversarial domains. Strong command of anomaly detection and unsupervised / semi-supervised learning: labeled data is scarce in this domain, and that shapes the entire approach. Experience with large-scale telemetry or event data: logs, time series, user or device behavior data. Full autonomy with raw data: solid Python (pandas/polars, scikit-learn, PyTorch or similar), advanced SQL, and comfort working directly against a datalake without prepared datasets. Product mindset: the ability to go from a research idea to an evaluable prototype in weeks, not months, and to communicate results to non-technical stakeholders. Genuine curiosity about cybersecurity and the drive to learn the domain in depth alongside the team's experts. Nice to have Prior experience in mobile security, EDR, banking anti-fraud, or intrusion detection systems. Knowledge of adversarial machine learning (model evasion, robustness). Experience with AWS S3, ClickHouse or other high-volume analytical databases. Publications, open-source contributions, or talks in applied ML or security. Experience deploying models to production (basic MLOps). Practically Speaking, What's In It For You The chance to define the company's ML strategy from scratch, with direct product impact and full visibility. A technically fascinating problem: a real adversary that evolves, massive untapped data, and freedom to research. Daily collaboration with a Security team with deep domain expertise. Optimized onboarding – for your optimal start and customized induction. Technical ownership – take responsibility for key components and shape how we build our platform. Enthusiastic team – waiting to help you succeed and collaborate with experienced engineers. Beautiful office spaces – in the heart of Barcelona, 200m from Sants Estació with regular team/community events (breakfast, lunch…). Good transport connections – easy to reach by public transport. Flexible working hours & Hybrid working!

items.desc: À propos de nous L’IRT Jules Verne est le centre de recherche industriel et collaboratif au service du manufacturing, qui œuvre pour renforcer la compétitivité des usines en France. L’équipe de Recherche Technologique « Monitoring, Inspection & Contrôle procédés » (ERT MIC) est composée d’une quinzaine de collaborateurs, docteurs(es), ingénieurs(es) et techniciens(nnes), en charge de développer des solutions d’inspection innovantes et de les déployer en production et en maintenance dans l’industrie aéronautique, navale, l’énergie et le transport. Son objectif est de réduire les coûts d’inspection. Pour cela, l’équipe MIC développe des technologies innovantes en surveillance des procédés (PHM), contrôles non destructifs (CND) et contrôle santé intégré (SHM). Enfin, l’ERT MIC propose autour de ces trois activités les outils numériques indispensables à l’analyse automatique en temps réel des données collectées pour réduire le facteur humain, rétroagir sur les procédés, faciliter le travail des opérateurs… et assurer la continuité numérique de l’ensemble des opérations d’inspection. Les projets menés dans l’équipe sont de natures variées : des projets collaboratifs multi partenaires industriels de l’IRT JV, de la prestation de recherche et des projets européens. Mission L'équipe MIC recherche un(e) Ingénieur(e) R&D Data Scientist, pour un CDD de 12 mois , dans le cadre du développement de nos activités autour de l'exploitation et de l'analyse des données par Intelligence Artificielle (IA) des données CND, SHM et PHM. items.desc: About this opportunity This role is being recruited by Calyptus on behalf of one of our clients. Calyptus is a specialist recruitment partner helping startups and high-growth technology companies hire across engineering, product and design. What to expect We’ll review your application and, if your experience is a strong match, one of our team will be in touch We’ll support you throughout the interview process and keep you updated at each stage If this particular role isn’t the right fit, we may consider you for other relevant opportunities with our clients ______________________________________________________ A new open-source model is released and you are compelled to reach inside and understand how it actually works. You instinctively try to push it beyond what most people say is already impressive. You observe model behavior and don’t think, “What’s a better prompt?”, but “How do I improve its fundamentals?” Our Senior Machine Learning Engineer will operate deep within the model stack, working directly with weights, activations, and architectures to build the systems that make AI governance deterministic. Your work powers the Policy Engine, the core technology that gives enterprises real-time, auditable control over model behavior in production. Your mandate is ostensibly simple but difficult in execution: determine how a model can be improved for a specific purpose and build the systems that operationalize that within our platform. As opposed to simply using models, you will probe the mechanics of their cognition. What You Will Do Take ideas from mechanistic interpretability and related work and turn them into code that runs in production, making research into reality. Work directly with model internals to improve behavior and performance across commercial and open-source models. Leverage techniques like activation patching, control vectors, and feature extraction to achieve targeted, repeatable improvements in model output. Build the evaluation and deployment loops needed to ship changes reliably into enterprise environments. Design and optimize the feature-level intervention systems that enable deterministic policy enforcement at inference time. Who You Are Strong understanding of Transformer architectures, PyTorch internals, and the mathematical foundations of deep learning. Have trained, fine-tuned, or optimized models beyond superficial augmentation. Can read a paper, decide what matters, and implement it. Notice when something is not working and take ownership of fixing it. Motivated by the challenge of making large language models reliable and controllable enough for the highest-stakes enterprise applications. Our Stack Languages: Python, Rust, and Node/TypeScript, with React on the frontend Data: Postgresql, vector, and graph databases Infra: Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform, across several cloud providers and customer VPCs ML: Self hosted models on multiple GPU providers and frontier APIs ______________________________________________________ Genuine opportunities Every role advertised by Calyptus is a live position we’re actively recruiting for. Access opportunities with ambitious startups and high-growth technology companies Direct support from experienced specialist recruiters Honest feedback and clear communication throughout the hiring process Long-term career support, not just a single job application We look forward to hearing from you.
