items.desc: About The Role About ElevenLabs ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology. We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always. We have expanded from voice into three main platforms: ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale. ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages. ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models. Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you. How we work High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy. Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you. AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations. Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models. Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location. What we offer Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible. Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities. Learning & development : ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend. Social travel : We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose. Annual company offsite: Each year, we bring the entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia and Italy. Co-working : If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend. About the role We are looking for a Research Engineer to join the research team at ElevenLabs, focused on large-scale web crawling for our frontier AI models. The quality of our models is bounded by the quality and scale of the data behind them, and you will own the crawling systems that source world-class data from the open web. You will thrive in this role if you enjoy: Building and operating large-scale, distributed web crawlers that discover, fetch, and extract data across billions of pages reliably and efficiently. Solving hard crawling problems such as content extraction from messy HTML, deduplication at web scale, freshness and recrawl strategies, and politeness and rate-limit handling. Designing targeted crawling pipelines that find high-value data sources, including audio, video, and multilingual content, and turn them into clean training-ready datasets. Creating tooling and infrastructure that lets researchers request, monitor, and explore newly crawled web data quickly and reliably. Requirements We do not require any formal certifications or degrees. Instead, we are seeking enthusiastic engineers who can showcase solving impressively hard problems with artifacts such as past projects, designs, or GitHub contributions. Ideally, you bring: Hands-on experience building and scaling web crawlers or scraping systems, ideally in support of machine learning training data. Strong engineering skills in distributed systems at scale (e.g., Kubernetes, queue-based architectures, or custom pipelines processing billions of documents). The capacity to autonomously evaluate the quality, coverage, and compliance of crawled data, and to build the tooling to measure it. Location This role is remote and can be executed globally. If you prefer, you can work from our offices in London, New York, San Francisco, and Warsaw. We are an equal opportunity employer and do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability or other legally protected statuses. The system would detect colorimetric images and predict with a high level of accuracy discrete pH values, delivering lab-quality diagnostic precision to women and doctors - anytime, anywhere! Personalize results using Bayesian hierarchies and time-series methods to learn individual baselines and detect meaningful changes. Pair model outputs with concise, evidence-backed explanations using LLMs with retrieval and citation grounding. Establish evaluation, monitoring, and privacy-minded data workflows suitable for a regulated context. Requirements Already based in Berlin (non-negotiable) Eager to work in an early-stage, science-driven, female health startup Comfortable with ambiguity, self-directed, and proactive Benefits Hybrid work environment with office space in Berlin A competitive salary for 1 year with the possibility of extension pHera is closing the gender health gap! Most existing vaginal pH test strips are analog, low-resolution, visually subjective, and poorly suited for women’s health applications. Doctors need fast, reliable tools to help with complicated diagnoses. Women deserve clarity, not guesswork when managing their vaginal health from home. A high-resolution pH test can catch imbalances early, making it easier to monitor issues like bacterial vaginosis, recurring vaginal infections, sexually transmitted infections, ovulation, PCOS, and menopause. By building pHera, you would be building a tool that would advance women's health .

It has to be right often enough, and explain itself well enough, that an experienced operator will act on it. In time it will drive setpoints directly, so it also has to know when it does not know. Getting the recommendation right is only half the job. The other half is understanding how and when a recommendation can safely become an actual setpoint change on the machine, and building the supervisory control layer that makes that happen without fighting the line's existing controls or its operators. You will also be responsible for version one of the product around that algorithm: the data platform, the models, the deployment and the application operators use. This is a senior, hands-on role with ownership of the technical stack. You will make the architectural calls, write the code, spend time on customer sites and help hire the engineers who follow. What you will do The decision-making algorithm Design and build the core algorithm that turns live sensor data into decisions: which setpoints to change, by how much and when. Frame the problem properly. Decide whether it is best treated as prediction plus optimisation, model predictive control, Bayesian optimisation, contextual bandits, offline reinforcement learning or a combination, and justify the choice with evidence. Build process models that link settings and operating conditions to quality, scrap, throughput and energy, and that respect the dynamics of the process, including time delays, dead time and variation in raw material. Learn from historical data in which settings were rarely varied deliberately. Deal with confounding, operator interventions and changes of regime, and design safe experiments on live lines to fill the gaps. Quantify uncertainty and build in the ability to make no recommendation when conditions fall outside what the model has seen. Evaluate decisions properly: offline policy evaluation before anything goes live, and controlled trials against real production outcomes afterwards. Sensor data and features Build the pipeline from raw sensor data to model-ready features, covering synchronisation, resampling, lag alignment, filtering, missing data and faulty sensors. Develop soft sensors for quality measures that are only taken occasionally or offline. Link process data to production context such as product, recipe, material batch and shift. Detect anomalies, sensor faults and model drift, and retrain as lines, materials and products change. From recommendation to setpoint change Work out, for each adjustable variable, when a recommendation can safely be applied, taking account of process state, operating envelope, rate of change, interaction with other variables and the time the process needs to settle. Design the supervisory layer that sits above the line's existing PLC control loops, adjusting their setpoints while those loops continue to regulate the process, and make sure it never works against them. Define the conditions under which the system must hold or hand control back to the operator, such as start-up, product changeovers, alarms, sensor faults or unfamiliar material, and make handover between manual and automatic operation smooth. Monitor the effect of every change and reverse it automatically if the process does not respond as expected. Design the staged route from advisory to closed-loop operation, with clear, measurable criteria for when a line, or an individual variable, is ready for the next stage. Specify how setpoints are written back to the PLC (range checks, rate limits, reversibility and fallback to the last known good state), working with our integration partner and the customer's engineers. Machine safety functions stay in the PLC's safety layer and are never overridden by our software. Present recommendations with the reasoning behind them, in a form operators can check quickly and trust. Engineering and product Set the technical architecture for version one and make the build-or-buy decisions. Put proper machine learning operations in place: versioned data and models, testing, monitoring, deployment on edge hardware and in the cloud, and rollback. Spend time on customer sites to understand the process and earn the confidence of plant engineers. Help …

items.desc: Job number: BUS00904 Salary or Salary range: £50,733 - £67,351 per annum Posting End Date: 22 Nov 2026 About the role Build the Next Generation of Health Policy Simulation Models Do you want your research to influence how governments design policies to prevent chronic disease? Are you excited by the challenge of combining data, simulation, and policy to tackle the world’s biggest health problems? The Centre for Health Economics & Policy Innovation (CHEPI) at Imperial Business School is seeking a Research Associate / Research Fellow in Computational Health Policy Modelling to play a central role in developing Health-GPS — our state-of-the-art microsimulation model for non-communicable disease (NCD) policy analysis. Appointment will be made at Research Associate or Research Fellow level, depending on experience. Why This Role Matters Chronic diseases such as diabetes and cardiovascular disease remain leading causes of illness and premature death worldwide. Yet, the tools available to evaluate and design effective prevention policies are still evolving. Health-GPS provides a framework to explore how changes in diet, physical activity, and related risk factors affect long-term population health and economic outcomes. Health-GPS represents the gradual accumulation and interaction of individual-level risk factors — such as BMI, diet, and income — offering insights into the potential impact of different policy interventions over time. You will help develop and apply this model across major international projects including: GOLDFINCH – estimating the effects of fiscal policies on ultra-processed food consumption. JA Prevent NCD – a European Joint Action on integrated strategies for NCD prevention. JACARDI – a European initiative to reduce cardiovascular and diabetes risk. Working with economists, epidemiologists, and data scientists, you’ll push the boundaries of policy simulation and shape real-world decision-making. This is a hands-on computational role. Alongside using Health-GPS for policy analysis, you will write, test and review code in its C++ codebase, working within the team’s collaborative development workflow (version control, pull requests and code review). C++ experience is highly desirable, but we also welcome strong programmers in other relevant languages who are willing to work in C++. What you would be doing Contribute to the architecture, development, optimisation, and maintenance of Health-GPS, writing and reviewing code in its C++ codebase and ensuring its continued scientific and policy relevance. Work with colleagues to plan and deliver modelling work across multiple projects, producing high-quality outputs on time. Help integrate new methodologies, including AI and machine-learning approaches, into simulation design. Conduct quantitative analyses to estimate the health and economic impact of proposed policies. Identify and manage relevant datasets in collaboration with internal and external partners. Communicate findings through academic papers, policy briefs, and stakeholder workshops. Contribute to funding proposals and the expansion of CHEPI’s modelling activities. What we are looking for We’re seeking a creative and technically strong individual with: A PhD (or equivalent, or near completion) in health economics, epidemiology, computer science, or a related field. Experience building or using microsimulation models or other quantitative policy tools. Strong programming skills in at least one language (e.g. Python, R, or C++), and experience contributing to a shared codebase using version control (e.g. git). Experience working with large or longitudinal datasets. The ability to translate complex model outputs into actionable policy insights. Curiosity, independence, and enthusiasm for multidisciplinary collaboration. Experience with C++ is highly desirable. Experience applying AI or ML methods to health or policy modelling is also desirable. Candidates for appointment as Research Fellow should also demonstrate a strong publication record, experience contributing to funding proposals, and the ability to design and lead original research. items.desc: Your job Do you want to contribute to the innovations shaping the future of sustainable horticulture and agriculture? As a Research Software Engineer, you will develop applications, data solutions, and software building blocks that support our research and innovation projects. You could be working on autonomous greenhouse control, ranging from climate management to robotics for crop scouting or crop maintenance. You will also help improve the standardization, accessibility, and reuse of data from greenhouses and field experiments, enabling stronger insights across projects. Working closely with researchers and industry partners, you will help transform ideas into practical digital solutions while ensuring they remain reliable, scalable, and reusable. Your duties and responsibilities as a research software engineer include: develop software tools and applications for research, experimentation, and decision support both for colleagues and growers; build and maintain data infrastructures, databases, and integrations between control systems and sensors; develop dashboards and analytics solutions that turn research data into actionable insights for colleagues and our customers; collaborate with researchers and project partners to translate scientific and operational needs into software solutions; enable the long-term reuse, scalability, and quality of software and data solutions across multiple projects. Your team You will be part of the Greenhouse Automation and Robotics team, a multidisciplinary group that combines expertise in AI, sensor technology, and robotics. The team develops innovative solutions for both greenhouse horticulture and open-field agriculture. You will work in an environment where collaboration, knowledge sharing, and innovation are at the core, with plenty of opportunities to take initiative and turn new ideas into reality. This provides an inspiring and supportive workplace with a strong connection between technology and real-world agricultural applications. Your primary workplace will be Wageningen, where you will be based for most of your work. Depending on project needs, you may also spend time at other locations, such as Bleiswijk or field sites where experiments and trials are conducted. Your qualities We are looking for a versatile Research Software Engineer who enjoys working at the intersection of software development, data engineering, and applied research. You are able to understand the needs of researchers and project partners and translate them into practical, robust, and user-friendly software solutions. You enjoy working in multidisciplinary teams and are comfortable switching between project-specific developments and more generic software components that can be reused across multiple projects. You Also Possess a bachelor's or master's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Data Science, or a related field; several years of experience in software development, data engineering, or a similar role; strong programming skills in Python; experience with C++ and/or C# is an advantage; experience with databases, data pipelines, and modern data engineering practices; familiarity with tools such as Airflow or TimescaleDB is a plus; experience with robotics software, ROS 2, machine learning, or related technologies is an advantage. items.desc: The University of Southampton is inviting applications for a postdoctoral position (Research Fellow) in numerical relativity. The successful candidate will undertake research as part of the recently awarded STFC grant Simulating realistic neutron-star mergers. Southampton's School of Mathematical Sciences is home to a large research group in gravitational physics, currently comprising 7 staff members and a number of postdocs and PhD students. Research in the group includes black-hole and neutron-star physics, gravitational-wave source modelling and data analysis, numerical relativity and gravitational self-force modelling. Members of the group are actively involved with the LIGO Scientific Collaboration, the Einstein Telescope Collaboration and the LISA Consortium. The successful applicant will contribute to work aimed at carrying out numerical simulations of neutron star mergers with realistic physics, with particular focus of resistive magnetohydrodynamics. The ideal candidate will have a track record in numerical relativity and ideally some understanding of neutron star modelling, gravitational-wave astronomy and data analysis. Applicants will have, or be about to obtain, a relevant PhD degree in physics or mathematics. This is a fixed term post until 30th September 2027. A complete application should include (i) a CV, including a list of publications, and (ii) a statement of research interests (no more than 1 page). Lenovo is a global leader in AI infrastructure, high-performance computing, and data centre technologies, helping customers build and scale next-generation accelerated computing environments. As part of the Lenovo Infrastructure Deployment Services (LIDS) team, you will support the validation, benchmarking, and optimisation of large-scale HPC and AI solutions for some of Lenovo's most strategic global customers. In this role, you will execute performance testing, analyse benchmark results, and provide optimisation recommendations across cutting-edge HPC and AI environments, working closely with customers, architects, consultants, and engineering teams. You will be part of a global team supporting EMEA and worldwide projects and will report directly to the Global HPC Delivery Leader. What You Will Do Validate, benchmark, and optimize large-scale HPC and AI platforms, ensuring systems meet performance targets, customer expectations, and acceptance criteria. Design and execute benchmarking and performance test plans across compute, storage, networking, GPUs, and AI workloads, then analyze and present results. Profile applications, identify performance bottlenecks, and provide practical optimization recommendations for HPC, AI, and GPU-accelerated environments. Work with industry-standard HPC benchmarks, AI training and inference workloads, MPI-based applications, storage testing tools, and large-scale cluster validation processes. Partner closely with customers, solution architects, technical consultants, delivery teams, and technology partners to support successful solution deployment and operational readiness. Contribute to the development of benchmarking methodologies, best practices, technical documentation, training materials, and knowledge-sharing initiatives that strengthen Lenovo’s global HPC and AI capabilities. What You Will Bring Strong experience with High Performance Computing (HPC) environments, including cluster architectures, Linux administration, job scheduling, and distributed computing. Proven ability to execute, analyse, and optimise HPC benchmarks and performance validation tests across compute, storage, and networking infrastructure. Solid knowledge of parallel computing technologies, including MPI, OpenMP, CUDA, NCCL, and GPU-accelerated applications. Experience benchmarking and tuning scientific, engineering, AI, and data analytics workloads on large-scale HPC platforms. Strong understanding of NVIDIA GPU technologies and architectures, including H100, H200, B200, and GB200/GB300. Hands-on experience with high-performance networking technologies such as InfiniBand and RoCEv2. The research will explore how engineered optical resonances and nonlinear light-matter interactions can enable new approaches to near-infrared detection, optical
items.desc: Build a Rewarding Career. Doing things differently. Research Fellow in Nonlinear Photonics £39,984 - £44,977 p.a. pro rata Full time/Fixed Term - 2 years starting on 1st January 2027 (with the potential of extension). About The Role We are seeking a Research Fellow to join an exciting European Research Council funded project focused on nonlinear nanophotonics and nonlinear metasurface-enabled spectroscopy and imaging in the Advanced Optics and Photonics (AOP) Group. The research will explore how engineered optical resonances and nonlinear light-matter interactions can enable new approaches to near-infrared detection, optical frequency conversion and computational imaging. You will undertake innovative experimental and simulation-based research, contributing to the development of new knowledge in nonlinear nanophotonics, metasurfaces and optical spectroscopy. Key activities will include electromagnetic modelling, developing optical setups, measuring linear and nonlinear optical responses, and implementing imaging and image-reconstruction techniques. The work will investigate resonantly enhanced nonlinear processes, including harmonic generation and frequency mixing, and their application to wavelength conversion and the recovery of spatial and spectral information. You will contribute to research planning, data analysis, publications, conference presentations and future funding applications. You will also support the wider research environment through collaboration with academic partners, supervision of student projects and occasional teaching of research methods and techniques. This is an excellent opportunity to develop your research profile while contributing to a cutting-edge area of photonics research. items.desc: Company Description Join iLOF to turn challenging scientific questions into implemented analyses, reproducible workflows and useful results. With a primary focus on clinical projects and contributions to preclinical work, you will take ownership of analytical deliverables, investigate unresolved problems and help move projects from exploration to completion. You will work closely with other Data Scientists and scientific colleagues, translating project needs into concrete analytical solutions and communicating what the results mean. Job Description Translate clinical and preclinical project questions into clear analytical tasks, approaches and deliverables. Apply strong mathematical expertise in signal processing, probability and statistics to develop and evaluate robust algorithms. Prepare, explore and analyse experimental and associated clinical datasets, investigating quality issues and inconsistencies. Implement and evaluate statistical and machine learning methods appropriate to the question and available data. Take ownership of unresolved analytical problems, diagnose their causes and develop practical solutions. Produce reproducible code, analyses, visualisations and documentation that colleagues can review and reuse. Apply appropriate validation procedures and communicate uncertainty, limitations and alternative interpretations. Work with colleagues from other teams and disciplines to interpret findings in their experimental and clinical context. Collaborate with specialist Data Scientists to apply new methods within project workflows. Support reports, publications and project milestones through clear, timely analytical contributions. You can understand an existing analysis, identify what is preventing progress and take responsibility for resolving it. You bring mathematical discipline, strong implementation skills and a collaborative approach. You are comfortable working in an evolving environment while keeping your work structured, reproducible and focused on the project’s needs. Qualifications Degree in Mathematics, Applied Mathematics, Statistics or a related quantitative discipline, supported by relevant applied experience. Professional experience delivering Data Science or quantitative analysis projects from problem definition through implementation. Strong scientific programming skills and the ability to write clear, maintainable analytical code. Practical knowledge of statistics, machine learning, data preparation and model evaluation. Ability to investigate unfamiliar datasets, troubleshoot analytical workflows and assess whether results are credible. Experience managing your own deliverables and communicating progress, dependencies and findings. Experience in a startup or another environment requiring ownership and adaptability is particularly valuable. Experience analysing biomedical, clinical or experimental data is advantageous. The opportunity Make a visible contribution to iLOF’s scientific programmes by solving difficult analytical problems and delivering work that colleagues can use to make decisions and advance projects. Recognized by CB Insights and Financial Times as one of the most promising Digital Health companies in the world, iLOF is building an AI-powered platform capable of transforming precision medicine. Our goal is to become the platform that democratizes access to personalized medicine for millions of people living with complex diseases around the globe. Thanks to our proprietary optical fingerprint library of disease biomarkers and biological profiles we can offer personalized patient screening and stratification in a faster and more affordable way, saving up to 40% of the cost and 70% of the time while enabling a more human patient experience. Supported by leading institutions like Microsoft Ventures, Mayfield, and the Oxford University, iLOF is currently focusing on validating its platform technology in one of the biggest challenges of our times: Alzheimer's, while maintaining ongoing verticals on Digestive Cancer, Stroke, and Infectious diseases. Organisé sous forme de projets à durée limitée, la mission de cette task-force européenne distribuée consiste, en collaboration avec d’autres centres européens d'excellence, à travailler sur des actions transverses de support applicatif de haut niveau pour les communautés scientifiques développant des méthodes d’IA à l’échelle d’infrastructures de calcul nationales. L'Activité Assurer un support technique en distanciel ou présentiel aux projets du programme MINERVA, organiser son travail sur une durée limitée afin d’atteindre les objectifs fixés, et communiquer régulièrement sur l’avancée du projet. items.desc: At Snowflake, we are powering the era of the agentic enterprise. To usher in this new era, we seek AI-native thinkers across every function who are energized by the opportunity to reinvent how they work. You don’t just use tools; you possess an innate curiosity, treating AI as a high-trust collaborator that is core to how you solve problems and accelerate your impact. We look for low-ego individuals who thrive in dynamic and fast-moving environments and move with an experimental mindset — who rapidly test emerging capabilities to discover simpler, more powerful ways to deliver results. At Snowflake, your role isn't just to execute a function, but to help redefine the future of how work gets done. We’re at the forefront of the data revolution, committed to building the world’s greatest data and applications platform. Our ‘get it done’ culture allows everyone at Snowflake to have an equal opportunity to innovate on new ideas, create work with a lasting impact, and excel in a culture of collaboration. We're looking for a talented and motivated Software Engineer to join the Cortex AI Functions Platform team. AI functions are how Snowflake customers call AI directly from SQL, running models over their own tables without moving data out of the platform. Our team builds the platform that makes this work at data warehouse scale, where a single statement can expand into a large volume of inference requests that must complete predictably, within expected cost, and without compromising the query when a dependency degrades or fails. Current projects include a new architecture for multi-modal inference, quality gates that let us ship new functions and models with confidence at batch scale, and support for input data beyond plain text. Alongside these, we work continuously on throughput, cost and reliability as customer usage grows, and on making failures in the inference path easier to detect, diagnose and recover from. For this role, you don’t need to have a research background, including pre-training or fine-tuning models. Your journey as a Software Engineer Working in our team you will: Think creatively to find optimal solutions to our complex, often ambiguous problems Participate in all stages of building and running the platform behind Snowflake’s AI functions, from design and implementation through rollout and production support Work closely with research teams, as well as product and engineering partners, to understand and shape the short and long-term product development strategy Serve as a mentor to less experienced engineers Ideal candidate 4+ years of experience building production backend or distributed systems in C++, Java, Go, Python, or a comparable language BSc in a technical field (CS, EE, Physics, Math, etc), MSc/PhD is a plus Experience designing and operating high-throughput services, including handling concurrency, backpressure, partial failures, and observability Experience designing service or RPC APIs, such as REST or gRPC Experience with software engineering best practices (programming, testing, version control, CI/CD, containers, agile development, etc) Experience with building distributed systems that guarantee high throughput without compromising on reliability High levels of curiosity and eager enthusiasm for open-ended problems, and the ability to turn a loosely defined problem into a scoped, testable design Ability to articulate results and complex concepts to leadership Must be able to produce solutions independently in an organized manner, as well as work in a team Experience with SQL engines, query execution, or other large-scale data systems is a strong asset Hands-on experience in the MLOps field (e.g., deploying ML models) is a plus Snowflake is growing fast, and we’re scaling our team to help enable and accelerate our growth. items.desc: À propos de nous Établissement Public à caractère Scientifique, Culturel et Professionnel (EPSCP), l’université de Tours est la première université de la région Centre-Val de Loire. Elle propose une offre de formation large, pluridisciplinaire, et interdisciplinaire et une recherche d’excellence reconnue. C’est aussi un établissement inscrit dans un environnement régional dynamique, connu pour la qualité de vie qu’il offre à ses habitants. Dans ce cadre, l’université de Tours se présente comme une université citoyenne, aux valeurs humanistes, socialement engagée, éthiquement responsable. L’université accueille 30 000 étudiantes et étudiants, et emploie aujourd'hui plus de 1200 personnels et plus de 1400 enseignants chercheurs. Pour accompagner son développement, l'université de Tours recrute chaque année de nouveaux talents. Ce poste, comme tous les postes de notre université, est ouvert aux candidats et candidates en situation de handicap. Mission Contexte Le projet de recherche européen PRIMA réexamine la façon dont la culture a été produite et diffusée en Europe moderne, entre 1575 et 1800. Hypothèse centrale : l'imprimé n'a pas été la technologie dominante de publication, le manuscrit est resté un support de publication massif pour les littérature, science et musique, notamment en Italie. Le projet cherche à établir qui produisait ces manuscrits, pour qui, en quelle quantité, selon quelles pratiques d'écriture, et les cas d'hybridation entre manuscrit et imprimé. Il combine méthodes qualitatives, approches quantitatives, traitements computationnels pour les fouille, production, recherche de données. Ses résultats incluent la constitution d'un centre d'études du manuscrit moderne et des publications en accès ouvert. L'ingénieur·e rejoindra le volet computationnel du projet, travaillera en interaction étroite avec les historien·ne·s, paléographes, littéraires. Pas de connaissance en paléographie exigée (formation interne). Goût du dialogue interdisciplinaire indispensable. Missions Segmentation, prétraitement des images : Reprendre, évaluer, améliorer l'outil de segmentation existant, analyse du papier. Concevoir les prétraitements adaptés aux documents anciens. Automatiser la chaîne pour la rendre exploitable sur des corpus de grande taille. Caractérisation des formes de lettres : Définir, implémenter des descripteurs. Évaluer comparativement ces représentations sur les corpus du projet. Classification, modélisation : Moissonnages des images et métadonnées des filigranes, mettre en œuvre des approches pour identifier et regrouper les allographes d'une même lettre et le motif du filigrane. Modéliser la dépendance de la graphie au contexte : position dans le mot, lettres voisines, ligatures. Comparer approches classiques et connexionnistes . Datation, localisation : Construire les distributions de référence à partir des documents datés et localisés fournis par l'équipe. Concevoir et valider les mesures de comparaison entre distributions, avec quantification de l'incertitude. Produire des résultats interprétables et discutables par les historien·ne·s du projet. Ingénierie, diffusion : Développer un code documenté, testé, versionné, reproductible. Constituer et documenter les jeux de données annotés dans une perspective de science ouverte. Participer à la rédaction des publications, présenter les travaux. Contribuer à l'encadrement technique de stagiaires/doctorant·e·s sur les aspects computationnels. Profil Savoir Requis : Domaine / Attendus : Traitement du signal et des images. / Filtrage, morphologie mathématique, segmentation, extraction et description de contours, analyse de formes, mise en correspondance Apprentissage automatique. / Classification supervisée et non supervisée, clustering, réduction de dimension, sélection de modèles, protocoles d'évaluation et validation croisée Modèles probabilistes. / Modèles graphiques et réseaux bayésiens, modèles de mélange, modèles séquentiels Apprentissage profond. / CNN pour la vision, architectures à attention et transformers , apprentissage auto-supervisé et par transfert, apprentissage métrique et few-shot Développement. / Python et son écosystème scientifique, Git, environnements reproductibles, calcul sur GPU Génie logiciel. / Code structuré, testé, documenté ; conception maintenable, évolutive Langues. / Français ou anglais courant ; lire, rédiger en anglais scientifique Le corpus est déséquilibré et faiblement annoté : maîtrise des méthodes adaptées aux données rares et bruitées appréciée Appréciés : Expérience en humanités numériques, travail avec des chercheur·se·s en sciences humaines ; Reconnaissance d'écriture manuscrite, familiarité avec des outils comme Transkribus, eScriptorium, Kraken ; Traitement automatique des langues : modèles de langue, modèles n-grammes, plongements lexicaux, correction et normalisation de textes bruités, langues anciennes ; Connaissance des standards de description et d'échange du patrimoine écrit ; Curiosité pour les …

You'll shape the analytical approach for a team that sets the terms on iwoca's biggest acquisition channel. The team is young, with many unexplored opportunities. The Company Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don’t wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that’s as flexible and responsive as they are. That's why we built iwoca. Our smart technology, data science and five-star customer service ensures business owners can act with the speed, confidence and control they need, exactly when it's needed. We’ve already cleared the way for 100,000 businesses with more than £4 billion in funding. Our passionate team is driven to help even more SMEs succeed, through access to better finance and other services that make running a business easier. Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they ildrive. The team Broker Terms is a growing team that sits within iwoca's third-party acquisition department. It owns the full offer terms strategy for customers referred through the broker network – both first-time customers and repeat. The team sets pricing, loan amounts, durations, and broker commissions, and owns the UX that presents them to brokers and customers. The team is small and interdisciplinary, combining commercial strategy, engineering, and data science. The work translates business questions into quantitative problems, and findings into actionable decisions. Active projects include: Model-based pricing – creating a sophisticated model to offer bespoke pricing to each customer A no-fee test – examining how our product performs when we remove all drawdown fees, and how that influence customer repayment behaviour Testing longer-duration flexi-loan products with particular customer segments. Reintroductions - exploring the right offer terms to give returning customers The team is small and cross-functional – commercial strategy, engineering, design, and data science – and works across the full application stack, from the Broker API to the Introducer Portal brokers use. The role You'll model expected customer take-up rates, design experiments, and translate findings into pricing and product decisions for the acquisition channel that drives the most customer lifetime value (CLTV). Because the Broker Terms team is a young team, you'll influence how its analytical approach develops, not just what it produces. The work has direct commercial consequences: brokers act on what the team builds and tests, and that shapes which customers iwoca wins and on what terms. Offer terms and experimentation. You'll model how customers respond to offer terms and how brokers make decisions under uncertainty. You'll design experiments where causal inference is central: you'll need to know where standard A/B testing breaks down and what to reach for instead. Commercial translation. You'll work with commercial and strategy colleagues and see your analysis applied directly in day-to-day decisions. That includes meeting brokers in person – gaining context that shapes how you frame and interpret results – and coordinating with adjacent teams responsible for underwriting decisions, repeat lending, and offer construction. CLTV and customer journey. You'll think across the full broker-referred customer journey – from first funding to repeat – identifying what drives CLTV and what changes to offer terms or UX improve it. You own both the strategy and the mechanism, so your findings feed directly into what the team builds and tests. AI and ways of working. You'll use AI to accelerate and automate your analytical work – not occasionally, but as a default. You should have a view on where it genuinely helps and where a different approach is better. The Requirements Essential: Statistical foundations. You have a background in probability and statistics from a quantitative field such as mathematics, physics, or statistics. You're comfortable with Bayesian reasoning, and have applied hierarchical models or formal decision-making under uncertainty in real work. Causal inference and experimentation. You've separated signal from noise in observational and experimental data. You know where A/B testing breaks down and what to reach for instead. You have experience with careful experimental design to facilitate clean, trustworthy results. Analytical ownership. You take loosely defined problems from start to finish – framing the question, choosing the method, and landing the answer with the people who act on it. Data tooling. items.desc:
Introduction to the job 
 Do you enjoy solving algorithm design problems for the semiconductor metrology industry, with demanding time, accuracy, and memory requirements? Do you like to use your creativity, your in-depth knowledge of physics principles, numerical math's and machine learning, and your hands-on experience with practical problem solving, being part of a highly talented group of algorithm experts?
 Role and responsibilities 
 In this role you will focus on scanner modeling and optical and mathematical models and methods required to infer physical model parameters from optical metrology data. Relevant new metrics, calibrations and algorithms as well as new measurement functions, with optimum performance characteristics, are identified, designed and implemented. The availability and development of fast and accurate machine learning models and metrology inference strategies is essential.
 As a Mathematics Machine Learning Engineer you will be doing the following:
 Development of models for scanners and optical metrology solutions with statistically correct parameter inference, deep learning and optimization algorithms, and system calibrations, to improve semiconductor high-volume fab control solutions.
 Implement machine learning and deep learning scanner models and metrology applications, with a mindset for scalable data-intensive and distributed software architectures, at the interface with colleague physics, data science, and software groups at ASML.
 Communicate crystal clearly on physical principles, mathematical solutions and design decisions to stakeholders, without omitting the essentials.
 Drive for data and code quality, and collaborate and help to implement along industry coding best practices.
 Work as a team with similar-minded people, benefitting from each other’s specific competences.
 Design and realize fully functional proof-of-concept subsystems on the edge of system specifications, costs and project planning, thereby contributing directly to products for B2B customers world-wide.
 Review technical analyses from the team, and structure team contributions keeping the overview.
 Consolidate technical-team identity in communication with other departments.
 Contribute to technical product roadmaps and generate intellectual property protecting ASML products, while developing the best metrology solutions and a well-founded vision on semiconductor metrology.
 Keywords: Mathematical optimization, optical modeling and calibration, mathematics, inverse problem, parameter inference, (non-)convex optimization, machine learning, deep learning, neural network, regression, information theory.
 Education and experience 
 Ph.D. in Applied Mathematics, Physics, Computer Science, or Electrical Engineering.
 0-3 year of working experience.
 Skills 
 Excellence in numerically stable modeling and inference strategies, using sound physical-mathematical principles and insights
 Ability to explain physical principles and algorithmic solutions in a crisp way, without omitting the essentials
 Excellence in numerical mathematics, and affinity with machine learning methods, data-intensive and distributed software architecture (cloud) as environment for metrology applications
 Drive for structuring the scripting code base in the cluster, and be energized by helping colleagues in this
 Fluency in the languages Python, C++, MATLAB, or Julia, and awareness of compatibility with other software
 Sound understanding of the fundamentals such as optics, linear algebra, probability theory, robust optimization and (deep) learning methods
 Drive creative solutions within the bigger picture, with the product and customer in mind
 Initiating, self-propelling and decisive in an ambiguous environment
 Team worker, and ability to influence without power
 Pragmatic approach and pro-active attitude, with result focus and a ‘can do’ spirit
 Other 
 We would like to receive a letter of motivation in which it is clearly stated how you have applied your knowledge and experience in practice. 
 Please note that applications will only be reviewed starting in week 35 due to the holiday period

items.desc:
Job Description: 
 Airbus Defence & Space recrute un(e) Artificial Intelligence & Image Processing Engineer for Space Systems (f/h) à Toulouse.
 Au sein de l'unité « Ground, Image & Navigation Solutions », le département « Image Engineering & Solutions » conçoit, développe et maintient les chaînes de traitement d’images pour les missions d'observation de la Terre, de surveillance de l’espace et d'exploration spatiale.
 Vous rejoindrez l'équipe « Vision & Image Processing » , un collectif de plus de 25 ingénieurs et docteurs alliant expertise de pointe en traitement d'images, vision par ordinateur, architecture et développement logiciel. Notre périmètre couvre également l’architecture des systèmes et sous-systèmes imageurs spatiaux, répondant à de fortes exigences d'opérabilité, de volumétrie et de qualité métrique.
 Pionniers du déploiement industriel du deep learning en production spatiale depuis 2021 (notamment sur Pléiades Néo HD15), nous exploitons l'apprentissage automatique pour repousser les limites de la qualité géométrique et radiométrique. Votre rôle consistera à concevoir et intégrer ces technologies d'IA au cœur des performances des systèmes actuels et futurs d’Airbus Defence and Space.
 Votre environnement de travail : 
 Capitale mondiale de l'aéronautique et capitale européenne de la recherche dans le spatial, Toulouse est une ville dynamique du sud-ouest de la France desservie par un aéroport international. Idéalement située entre la mer Méditerranée et l' océan Atlantique et à proximité des Pyrénées, elle offre de nombreuses possibilités d'activités de plein air !
 Parce que nous prenons soin de vous : 
 Avantages financiers: Salaire attractif, accords d’intéressement et de participation, plan d'épargne salariale abondé par Airbus, plan d’actionnariat salarié sur la base du volontariat, avec attribution d'actions gratuites en fonction du nombre d’actions souscrites.
 Équilibre vie privée / professionnelle: Des jours de congés supplémentaires pour occasions spéciales et des options de transfert de congés, un comité d'entreprise proposant de nombreuses activités socio-culturelles et sportives et d’autres services.
 Bien-être / santé: couverture complémentaire des frais de santé et de prévoyance (incapacité, invalidité, décès). Selon le site : centre de services de santé, services de conciergerie, salle de sport, application de covoiturage.
 Développement individuel: des opportunités d’évolution et des possibilités de formations nombreuses (catalogue de plus de 10.000 e-formations disponibles en libre accès pour développer votre employabilité, certifications, programmes de développement accéléré, parcours expert, mobilité nationale et internationale).
 Chez Airbus, nous vous aidons à travailler, à vous connecter et à collaborer plus facilement et de manière plus flexible. Partout où cela est possible, nous favorisons la flexibilité dans nos modes de travail afin de stimuler l'esprit d'innovation.
 Vos missions principales : 
 Ingénierie système & cadrage : analyser les exigences client, contribuer à la définition architecturale des solutions et assurer l'interface technique avec les équipes système, instrumentation optique et segment sol.
 R&D & conception algorithmique : concevoir et prototyper des algorithmes avancés pour optimiser la qualité radiométrique et géométrique des instruments imageurs (projets opérationnels et R&D, du simulateur aux briques logicielles qualifiées).
 Industrialisation & qualification : définir les métriques de performance, piloter les campagnes d'évaluation (qualification, photo-interprétation) et fiabiliser le passage à l'échelle des modèles au sein des chaînes de traitement opérationnelles.
 Veille technologique : évaluer l'état de l'art algorithmique et adapter les innovations externes aux contraintes des systèmes spatiaux.
 Documentation technique : rédiger les dossiers de justification, spécifications fonctionnelles, plans de validation et rapports de performance.
 Développement transverse : contribuer progressivement au montage d'offres techniques et diffuser l'expertise en ingénierie guidée par la donnée sur l'ensemble de la chaîne de valeur spatiale.
 Votre profil : 
 Formation supérieure (Bac+5 ou doctorat) en traitement d'images, vision par ordinateur, informatique ou mathématiques appliquées.
 Expérience confirmée en conception d'algorithmes de traitement d'images par apprentissage automatique ( deep learning appliqué aux problèmes inverses, super-résolution, débruitage, recalage), au-delà des seules tâches classiques de classification ou segmentation.
 Maîtrise avancée du développement sous Linux via l'écosystème Python scientifique ; la maîtrise du C++ et la pratique du calcul haute performance (HPC/GPU) constituent des atouts majeurs.

 Une expérience dans le domaine spatial (qualité image, systèmes imageurs, segment sol) ou dans des domaines proches à fortes …

items.desc:
Job Description: 
 Airbus Defence and Space is looking for a
 Mission Systems Equipment Design Responsible (d/f/m) 
 Your Mission 
 As Equipment Design Responsible, you will be the technical authority for airborne equipment throughout its entire lifecycle, for various weapon systems. You will transform operational and system-level needs into robust, certifiable equipment solutions, working closely with international suppliers and multidisciplinary engineering teams. You will ensure that equipment designs meet demanding performance, qualification, and certification requirements while supporting integration, testing and in-service operations. This role offers a unique combination of design responsibility, technical depth and direct influence on the successful delivery of advanced airborne capabilities.
 Your location (Manching) 
 Located about an hour’s drive north of Munich, Manching is an up-and-coming market town that offers a wide range of leisure and cultural activities. Here, you can enjoy the quality of life in the countryside while the pleasures of near-by cities are still within easy reach.
 Your benefits 
 Attractive salary and special payments
 30 days holidays and extra days-off for special occasions
 Excellent upskilling opportunities and great international, group wide development prospects
 Special benefits: employer-funded pension, employee stock options, discounted car leasing, special conditions for insurances, subsidies for public transport, employee benefits at cooperating companies
 On-site-facilities: Medical officer for check-ups and other health-related services, canteen and cafeterias, kindergarten close to the site 
 Compatibility of family & work (part-time models, flexible working hours, individual timeout)
 Networking and connection: Employee events, groups and initiatives
 Working in a diverse environment, with more than 140 nationalities, where every voice is heard
 Your Tasks and Responsibilities 
 Own the technical responsibility of airborne mission systems equipment throughout the full development lifecycle, including in-service support activities.
 Preparation and validation of Equipment technical specification and other contractual documents. Managing equipment requirements from higher-level system architecture and customer specifications down to equipment-level allocation.
 Technical management of suppliers of airborne equipment: technical evaluation, design and qualification follow up, milestones management, stages of involvement, validation and acceptance of deliverables, management of limitations and deviations, support to defect investigations and repairs, harmonization and control of supplier and program plans.
 Review technical solutions, challenge design decisions when necessary, and support issue resolution during development and integration phases.
 Ensure compliance with applicable aeronautical and contractual standards and certification requirements (e.g. DO-254) during the design and qualification, repair, obsolescence and re-design activities.
 Coordinate multidisciplinary engineering activities with internal specialists (safety, EMC, environmental qualification, RM&T, Quality, ILS, Airworthiness,…).
 Interface with customers, partner companies and certification authorities for technical matters related to equipment functionalities, design, qualification and problem resolution.
 Monitoring and support of the subsequent Equipment Integration including Sub-system, system verification and flight tests.
 Support requests concerning Equipment queries, in service occurrence reports and defect investigations.
 Your Profile: 
 (Master) Degree in electronics/electrical engineering, aerospace engineering, or equivalent
 At least 3-5 years of professional experience
 Strong technical background in electronic equipment development: embedded electronics (Microcontrollers, FPGAs, ASICs,... ), mission computers, high-speed digital interfaces, video or data processing systems, real-time embedded architecture,...
 Knowledge and practical expertise with airborne equipment:
 Qualification and certification
 Hardware development/design and verification (e.g. DO-254, ARP4754A, AMC 20-152A, DO-160, MIL-STD-810)
 Software development (DO-178) is considered a plus
 Ability to technically assess supplier solutions and support problem-solving activities during development
 Experience in technical supplier management is a plus
 Experience in requirements engineering and requirements management tools (DOORs) is a plus
 Comfortable taking ownership and making technical decisions
 Strong communication skills and ability to interact with suppliers, customers and authorities in an international environment
 Teamplayer and comfortable in international and multidisciplinary engineering environment: demonstrated skills to work independently and in a collaboratively manner within an international team, including the ability to coordinate and influence people
 Business-fluent English, German is …

items.desc:
WHY FACULTY? 


We established Faculty in 2014 because we thought that AI would be the most important technology of our time. Since then, we’ve worked with over 350 global customers to transform their performance through human-centric AI. You can read about our real-world impact here https://faculty.ai/impact.



We don’t chase hype cycles. We innovate, build and deploy responsible AI which moves the needle - and we know a thing or two about doing it well. We bring an unparalleled depth of technical, product and delivery expertise to our clients who span government, finance, retail, energy, life sciences and defence.



Our business, and reputation, is growing fast and we’re always on the lookout for individuals who share our intellectual curiosity and desire to build a positive legacy through technology.



AI is an epoch-defining technology, join a company where you’ll be empowered to envision its most powerful applications, and to make them happen.

 


ABOUT THE TEAM 

 

Our Energy, Transition and Environment business unit is pioneering meaningful change in the clean energy revolution. Our vision is to accelerate the transition to net-zero emissions and drive efficiencies for a new era of utility companies.

 

We believe that the responsible, and intelligent, deployment of AI is critical to the success of this mission. We partner with a wide range of clients - from major energy operators, to GreenTech startups, and national infrastructure providers - to build solutions which return measurable impact and move us towards a smarter, cleaner, and more sustainable world.

 



ABOUT THE ROLE

 

As an Associate, you’ll be part of a close-knit team - scoping, building and delivering impactful AI projects for our clients in the industry. 

We’ll look to you to build trusted client relationships, analyse requirements and feedback, stay on top of workflows and help to ensure our bespoke AI tools are optimised for real-world operations.

This is an exciting, new role for an individual motivated to build their knowledge of AI transformation in the Energy value chain. 

 
 


WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

 

 - Managing individual work streams to support the successful delivery and implementation of bespoke AI solutions

 - Working side-by-side with Government stakeholders to understand critical mission challenges and user needs

 - Conducting open-source analysis to support the development of cutting-edge AI tools

 - Translating complex operational requirements into clear user stories for delivery and engineering teams.

 - Designing and testing workflows that support user-centric decision-making in high-stakes environments

 - Collaborating closely with technical teams to ensure projects run smoothly and solutions meet customer needs

 - Contributing to internal thought leadership, strategy, and capability development across the team
   
    


WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 

 - You demonstrate analytical thinking, can clearly communicate ideas, and synthesise complex information

 - You have some experience working on AI/data intensive projects in the Energy sector

 - You have external client-facing experience and have built trusted relationships which have contributed to the overall success of projects/products

 - You’ve worked with technical teams

 - You understand Agile and related methodologies and the basis of iterative development and continuous delivery

 - You are thoughtful and proactive in ambiguous situations, with examples of when you’ve taken initiative and owned finding solutions to challenges

 - You’re excited and knowledgeable about the possibilities for innovation in  Government technology 

 
 


OUR INTERVIEW PROCESS



 1. Talent Team Screen (30 mins)

 2. Introduction Interview (60 mins)

 3. Case Study Interview (60 mins)








OUR RECRUITMENT ETHOS




We aim to grow the best team - not the most similar one. We know that diversity of individuals fosters diversity of thought, and that strengthens our principle of seeking truth. And we know from experience that diverse teams deliver better work, relevant to the world in which we live. We’re united by a deep intellectual curiosity and desire to use our abilities for measurable positive impact. We strongly encourage applications from people of all backgrounds, ethnicities, genders, religions and sexual orientations.



If you don’t feel you meet all the requirements, but are excited by the role and know you bring some key strengths, please don't hesitate in applying as you might be right for this role, or other roles. We are open to conversations about part-time hours. 



A note on AI: we're happy for you to use it for research and interview prep, but please don't use it to generate answers during live interviews. We also use an AI note-taker (Metaview) in interviews so interviewers can stay present (which you can opt out of just let us know,) and every application is reviewed by a human, never decided by AI.

Job Description: 
 Your impact 
 Are you ready to launch your career and make an impact on real-world projects from day one? 
 At Leonardo, we’re looking for graduates who want to be part of something bigger—shaping innovation, advancing technology, and enhancing global safety. 
 We are committed to developing our graduates into leading technical or business professionals, and as such we will also support you through your preferred route for professional development. 
 Our 18-month Graduate Programmes give you the opportunity to work on exciting and challenging projects alongside subject matter experts. 
 ​Systems Engineers are involved in all aspects of design and development; from initial product design through to in-service support. 
 They look at the big picture, determine how the system needs to operate and collaborate to produce the required overall operational behaviours. They also dive into the deepest level of detail – taking the system piece-by-piece and defining its design to the finest point. Our Systems Engineers can also actively engage in R&D, developing new concepts and conducting fundamental research into our future technologies. 
On joining, you will receive a starting salary of £34,000 per annum, plus a £1,000 welcome bonus. You’ll also be eligible for a £1,000 exit bonus upon successful completion of the programme. In addition, you may be eligible for a Temporary Accommodation Allowance (TAA), subject to specific criteria. 
 We encourage you to spend at least three days each week on site to integrate with your team and maximise your learning experience. 
 During the programme, you will: 
 Work on real engineering problems and have the opportunity to be involved in supporting a wide range of tasks across multiple projects/products, which covers Sea, Land, Air and space domains. 
 Be part of a dynamic and innovative team who will provide day-to-day guidance and on-the-job training, introducing you to systems engineering processes, methods, technology and tools. 
 Receive targeted training, developing the engineering skills and necessary domain knowledge required to achieve technical excellence and be a successful Systems Engineer. 
 What you’ll bring 
 All of our Graduate roles require (a) a minimum of an lower Second class Bachelors/Integrated Master’s degree, or (b) a higher degree, such as an MSc or PhD. In all cases the subject should be engineering, mathematics, physics or another STEM discipline. 
 In addition to this, we would be interested in hearing from you if you have experience in: 
 Coding/programming. 
 Relevant project work and/or placements in industry. 
 Solving problems as part of a team 
 Applying your science and technology knowledge to solve a real world problem 
 Security Clearance 
 Many of our roles are subject to security and export control restrictions set by UK Government Security requirements and customer obligations. As a result, and in line with the UK Government Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) requirements, all successful applicants will be asked to provide evidence of identity, eligibility to work in the UK, criminal record declaration information and employment and/or education history verification for the previous five years. 
 For staff operating in more sensitive posts, there is an additional range of personnel security controls referred to as National Security Vetting (NSV). As part of this process, a range of factors may be considered, including an individual's background, travel history, nationality, previous nationalities held and other information relevant to the vetting assessment. 
 To be eligible for National Security Vetting at SC level, applicants will generally be expected to have continuously resided in the UK for the previous five years. For DV clearance, this is typically ten years. In some circumstances, time spent overseas may be accepted, with additional overseas checks. Additional vetting requirements may apply upon appointment. 
 For more information and guidance please visit: https://careers.uk.leonardo.com/gb/en/security-and-vetting 
 Why join us 
 At Leonardo, our people are at the heart of everything we do, key contributors in shaping innovation, advancing technology, and enhancing global safety. 
 We offer a comprehensive, company-funded benefits package that supports your wellbeing, career development, and work–life balance. Whether you're looking to grow professionally, care for your health, or plan for the future, we’re here to help you thrive. 
 Time to recharge: Enjoy generous leave with the opportunity to accrue up to 12 additional flexi-days each year. 
 Secure your future: Benefit from our award-winning pension scheme with up to 15% employer contribution. 
 Your wellbeing matters: Free access to mental health support, financial advice, and employee-led networks championing inclusion and diversity (Enable, Pride, Equalise, Armed Forces, Carers, Wellbeing and Ethnicity). 
 Rewarding performance : All employees …

items.desc: Description The purpose of this role is to shape the public and political debate around data centre expansion and cloud sovereignty in Europe. The consultant will lead strategic communications across two connected areas: supporting campaigns challenging unsustainable data centre construction and building support for stronger sovereignty requirements in cloud procurement. A successful outcome would see a stronger European debate around sustainable and sovereign digital infrastructure, with campaign narratives focused on constructive policy solutions rather than polarising culture-war arguments. It would also build greater political and public support for reducing dependency on dominant hyperscalers and strengthening sovereignty requirements in cloud procurement. How you'll contribute Engage with and support organisations campaigning for democratic pacing and more stringent safeguards on data centre construction, helping to shape communications and campaign narratives towards constructive policy outcomes. Develop and deliver strategic communications to build public and political support for stronger democratic and sustainability requirements for data centre construction in Europe. Develop and deliver strategic communications to build public and political support for stronger sovereignty requirements in cloud procurement, challenging dependency in sensitive public and private sectors. Develop messaging, campaign framing and media strategies to support TBIP’s wider sustainable and sovereign data centres work, helping to build a compelling narrative around sustainable and sovereign digital infrastructure. Work closely with relevant TBIP and FOTI policy, advocacy and campaign colleagues, as well as external stakeholders, to ensure communications activity supports and strengthens wider policy and advocacy objectives. Our ideal candidate has Must haves: Demonstrable experience developing and delivering strategic communications and campaign strategies, ideally in a policy, advocacy or public affairs context. Strong understanding of the European political and policy landscape, with the ability to translate complex issues into clear, compelling public-facing narratives. Experience shaping campaign messaging, influencing public debate and identifying opportunities for media and political engagement. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate complex technical or policy issues to non-specialist audiences. Experience working collaboratively with campaigners, policy experts, advocacy organisations and external stakeholders. Ability to work independently, respond flexibly to emerging opportunities and manage competing priorities Fluency in written and spoken English, our working language; Nice to haves: Knowledge of European digital policy, particularly digital sovereignty, cloud infrastructure, data centres or competition in digital markets. Experience working on environmental sustainability, technology policy or corporate accountability campaigns. Established relationships with European media, policymakers, civil society organisations or relevant campaign networks. Experience developing communications strategies across multiple European markets. Additional languages are an asset. Why join us? Time period: expected start date Nov/Dec 2026. Rate: Up to €106,000 About Meliore Foundation (FUP) A place to thrive! We’re an international network that values genuine diversity. We know that tackling the climate emergency will need all of society and we want our network to be reflective of the richness of that society. We are looking for people who bring their best, most professional and effective selves to work. People who are respectful, kind and have a sense of fun. If that sounds like you, we’d love to hear from you. Your ideas, perspectives, and lived experiences are key to how you go about your work. We encourage people from historically disadvantaged or underrepresented groups to apply. About the Meliore Foundation Our vision is for a world where science-based facts on climate help guide the public debate. The Meliore Foundation endeavours to put just, inclusive and equitable solutions to global issues at the core of the world's political, social, environmental and economic discourse. To help achieve this vision, Meliore provides operational support and regranted funding for aligned programmes engaged in strategic communications and campaigns.

items.title: Fullstack Software Engineer (x/f/m) - Agentic Platform
items.card: What you'll do Own some of the problems above end to end, from design to production, with significant influence on architecture and code quality Work closely with the people who use what you build: Alaners, product teams, ops Own reliability, cost and security in production Mentor engineers, contribute to our product and engineering culture, and help build the team Experience we value 3+ years in software
items.desc: Health can’t wait . Not for symptoms to get worse. Not for a six‑month appointment. Not for a system to catch up. But that’s exactly how healthcare works today. You wait, until you can’t. Alan exists to end the wait. Health is a universal right, and we believe this right can only become real when it’s coupled with prevention. We need to stop treating health as something we repair and start treating it as something we build, every day. It’s not solely a question of willpower. It’s the healthcare system itself that needs to work for everyone, in a sustainable way. So we are building the new standard in prevention insurance. Alan is the first company that integrates insurance, prevention, and care into a single, acclaimed user experience. We are on an incredible journey to build a global leading company, with a unique culture . We already partner with 40K+ companies of all sizes, serving more than 1M+ members, and have reached €800M+ in ARR. Prevention as the new norm. That's what we're building with our team of 1000+ people. If it speaks to you: we're hiring across France, Spain, Belgium, and Canada. And beyond. The Engineering team In our engineering team, we build the infrastructure, interfaces, and applications to provide first-class service to our members, health professionals, and even ourselves! Being an engineer at Alan means joining a team of talented, committed and passionate engineers, with a lot of product interaction. We move fast, with a lot of ownership, and are proud to tackle big problems! Our process is very simple: those who make product decisions are the same ones who build them. Want to know more? Read this article if you want to discover how life as an Engineer at Alan and this article on our Engineering career pat The stack Python services on FastAPI, async SQLAlchemy and PydanticAI, Temporal for durable execution, PostgreSQL, MCP, Daytona sandboxes, various LLM model providers, Terraform on AWS, React with Vite. Our main backend is a Flask monolith. We deploy daily and believe in distributed ownership: you build it, you own it. The Agentic Platform area In 2027, we expect to run more AI agents than we have employees . Agents already do real work at Alan. They answer members' health questions, resolve support requests, read medical documents, detect fraud, automate operational tasks, and write a large share of our code. But every team building an agent ends up solving the same hard problems again: how to call models safely with health data, how to give an agent tools and the right permissions, how to know whether a prompt change made it better or worse, how to debug what it did. The result: several agent frameworks and evaluation stacks, each with its own security and compliance story. The Agentic Platform area was created to fix that. Our mission: make it cheap, fast and safe for every Alaner or crew to build, run and improve agentic products and workflows. We own the environment agents run in (infrastructure, runtime, evaluation, observability, skills lifecycle), with security, privacy and compliance by design, and the generalist products on top: Hopper and the Agent Studio. Product teams and all Alaners own their agents, skills, and their outcomes. We give them the paved road. Two crews, one team: Hopper is every Alaner's AI companion. Five months after it started, 80% of Alaners use it, 3k sessions are created each day, and about 30% of our pull requests are opened from it (watch how we built it). items.desc: Type de recrutement : Poste ouvert en CDD Quotité de travail : 100% Niveau d'emploi : A - IGR - Ingénieur de Recherche / Attaché principal Durée du contrat : 1 an Localisation : UFR STAPS APS A 1741 Rue de la piscine 38610 Gières Présentation de la structure Le MIAI (Multidisciplinary Institute in Artificial Intelligence) est l'un des quatre instituts 3IA français. Labellisé « Cluster IA » dans le cadre de France 2030 avec un financement de 70 millions d'euros jusqu'en 2029, il développe une recherche interdisciplinaire de classe mondiale, soutient l'innovation et propose des formations en IA. En synergie avec le réseau national 3IA, l'UGA porte le projet EFELIA-MIAI ( École Française de l'IA ), visant la labellisation de formations, la mise en place de plateformes de calcul, ainsi que la création de cours pilotes et de contenus pédagogiques (MOOC/SPOC) partagés au niveau national. Dans ce cadre, l'UFR STAPS (Sciences et Techniques des Activités Physiques et Sportives) développe des actions de formation innovantes intégrant l'Intelligence Artificielle à l'analyse du mouvement humain et au sport-santé. Découvrez le MIAI : https://miai.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/ Missions principales Sous l’autorité du Directeur de l’UFR STAPS et en coordination avec la cheffe de projet Pédagogies de MIAI Cluster, vous contribuerez à la conception, au déploiement et à la valorisation de dispositifs de formation innovants en IA appliquée aux domaines du sport, de la santé et de la performance. Vous travaillerez en étroite collaboration avec les enseignants-chercheurs, les ingénieurs pédagogiques du réseau EFELIA et les partenaires académiques régionaux (USMB, UCA). Activités principales Concevoir et déployer des modules de formation en IA pour les parcours de Licence (ES, APAS) et Master (EOPS, APAS, Management Sportif), incluant la création de ressources pédagogiques no-code (reconnaissance de gestes, analyse vidéo, suivi GPS, visualisation 3D). Développer des travaux pratiques et dirigés (TP/TD sous Python et R, Jupyter Notebooks) axés sur le traitement des données du mouvement humain pour les étudiants de Master. Former et accompagner les enseignants de l'UFR STAPS pour garantir leur autonomie dans l'enseignement des outils d'IA. Produire, organiser et évaluer les ressources multimédias et supports pédagogiques (tutoriels vidéo, guides pratiques, jeux de données annotés, exercices interactifs). Animer des ateliers pratiques, séminaires et constituer une communauté de pratique au sein de l'UFR. Participer à la création de modules de formation continue pour les professionnels, en lien avec la Direction de la Formation Continue (UGA / Grenoble INP-UGA). Intervenir lors d'ateliers de sensibilisation (Summer Schools, grand public) et représenter MIAI Cluster lors de congrès et salons. Constituer, gérer et mener à jour l’inventaire des ressources éducatives du projet EFELIA-MIAI et alimenter la librairie en ligne du cluster. Assurer une veille scientifique et technologique continue sur les innovations en IA appliquée à l'analyse du mouvement. Contraintes liées au poste : Déplacements ponctuels à prévoir pour la représentation de MIAI Cluster sur des salons/congrès ou des interventions lors de Summer Schools. Compétences attendues Solides connaissances des outils et méthodes d'IA (traitement du signal, apprentissage profond / deep learning, préparation et annotation de jeux de données). Maîtrise avancée de la programmation en Python (la maîtrise de R et des notebooks Jupyter est vivement souhaitée). Ingénierie pédagogique : scénarisation d'activités multimédias et interactives pour publics spécialistes et non-spécialistes. Maîtrise ou appétence pour la configuration et le traitement des données issues de capteurs de mouvement (EMG, centrales inertielles, plateformes de force, GPS, caméras, drones) et logiciels d'analyse du mouvement. Maîtrise des techniques de conduite de projet et de travail collaboratif pluridisciplinaire. Aisance rédactionnelle et capacités de présentation orale (français et anglais technique courant). Rigueur scientifique, esprit d'analyse et sens de la synthèse. Aisance relationnelle, pédagogie et qualités d'écoute pour l'accompagnement des utilisateurs (enseignants, étudiants). Autonomie, proactivité et sens des initiatives. Esprit d'équipe, adaptabilité et goût pour la transmission des savoirs. Expérience professionnelle souhaitée : 2 à 5 ans. Formation / Diplôme : Diplôme d'Ingénieur ou Master 2 (Bac+5) en informatique, sciences de données, sciences de l'ingénieur ou bio-mécanique/STAPS avec forte composante numérique. Un Doctorat (Ph.D.) est apprécié pour le niveau Ingénieur de Recherche (IGR). Conditions de diplômes Bac + 5 Rémunération A partir de 2289€ mensuel brut et en fonction de l’expérience. Vous percevrez en plus de votre salaire un régime indemnitaire d'un montant mensuel brut de 716€ ainsi qu'une prime informatique 330 €.
