items.desc: Le pôle Nutrition végétale joue un rôle central dans la mise en œuvre des projets de recherche et développement au sein du Centre Mondial de l’Innovation Roullier, en étudiant et en proposant des solutions innovantes pour la nutrition des plantes et la santé des sols. Au sein de ce département, l’Unité Nutrition des Plantes et Stress Abiotiques contribue à la conception de solutions visant à optimiser l’efficacité d’utilisation des nutriments, la tolérance aux stress et la productivité des cultures. Afin de renforcer notre expertise, nous recrutons un(e) : Ingénieur de Recherche en Sciences Végétales / Nutrition des Plantes F/H , en CDI à Saint-Malo. Rattaché(e) au Chef de projet Nutrition des Plantes et Stress Abiotiques, vous participerez à des projets de recherche portant principalement sur la nutrition des plantes mais également sur la tolérance des plantes aux stress abiotiques. À ce titre, vous devrez démontrer de solides connaissances en physiologie végétale, nutrition des plantes et agronomie. Missions : - Identifier et mettre en œuvre les méthodes clés permettant d’évaluer l’état nutritionnel, la croissance et le développement des plantes. - Étudier les mécanismes impliqués dans l’acquisition et l’efficience d’utilisation des nutriments. - Gérer et analyser les données expérimentales. - Participer à la rédaction de rapports, de publications scientifiques et de propositions de projets de recherche. - Collaborer avec des partenaires académiques, industriels et institutionnels. The Plant Nutrition department plays a central role in the implementation of research and development projects at the Centre Mondial de l’Innovation Roullier, by studying and developing novel solutions for plant nutrition and soil health. Within this department, the Plant Nutrition and Abiotic Stress Unit supports designing solutions aimed at optimizing Nutrient Use Efficiency, stress tolerance and crop productivity. To strengthen our expertise, we are hiring a : Plant Nutrition Research Scientist in St Malo (Brittany, France). Reporting to the Plant Nutrition and Abiotic Stress Project Manager, you will take part in research projects focusing primarily on plant nutrition but also on plant tolerance to abiotic stresses. In this role, you will be expected to demonstrate a solid understanding of plant physiology, plant nutrition and agronomy. Responsibilities : - Identify and implement key methods to assess the nutritional status, growth and development of plants. - Study the mechanisms involved in nutrient uptake and use efficiency. - Manage and analyse experimental data. - Participate in writing reports, scientific publications, and research project proposals. - Collaborate with academic, industrial, and institutional partners. - Vous êtes titulaire d’un doctorat en physiologie végétale, sciences de l’environnement, nutrition des plantes ou dans un domaine connexe. - Vous maîtrisez les méthodes et techniques d’analyse appliquées aux plantes (phénotypage, analyses physico-chimiques, biochimie, biologie moléculaire, métabolomique, etc.). - Vous disposez de solides compétences en biostatistiques, analyse et interprétation des données. - Vous faites preuve d’excellentes capacités de rédaction scientifique et de communication. - Vous parlez couramment anglais. - Vous démontrez de l’autonomie, de la rigueur scientifique, un fort esprit d’équipe ainsi qu’une capacité à travailler sur des projets multidisciplinaires. Qu’avons-nous à offrir ? - Une prise en charge de l’abonnement transport en commun à hauteur de 75% - Un comité interentreprise - Des accords de participation et d’intéressement - Une participation aux repas - Un bâtiment dédié aux activités du sport et de la culture - Une vie interne dynamique : Afterwork, teambuilding… About you : - Ph.D. in Plant Physiology, Environmental Sciences, Plant Nutrition, or a related field. - Strong understanding of plant physiology, plant nutrition and agronomy, with the ability to investigate nutrient acquisition, utilization and nutrient use efficiency mechanisms. - Experience with analytical methods and techniques applied to plants, including phenotyping, physico-chemical analyses, biochemistry, molecular biology and metabolomics. - Solid skills in biostatistics, data analysis and interpretation. - Excellent scientific writing, communication and presentation skills. - Fluency in English. - Autonomous and rigorous approach to research, combined with a collaborative mindset and the ability to work effectively in multidisciplinary projects. What do we offer? - 75% reimbursement of public transportation subscription costs - Access to an intercompany employee benefits committee - Profit-sharing and incentive schemes - Meal contribution allowance - A dedicated facility for sports and cultural activities - A vibrant company culture with regular events such as after-work gatherings and team-building activities.

items.desc:
Job Description Summary 
Join GE HealthCare's Research Alliances team and help bring new diagnostic innovations from research to patients. You will coordinate the day-to-day operations of our research programs, from early investigator-led research to Investigator-Sponsored Trials (ISTs): studies led by external academic investigators using GE HealthCare imaging agents that are still in development.
Working with colleagues across Legal, Finance, Supply Chain, Medical and Compliance, you will keep studies moving smoothly from application through to close-out and help us improve how our programs run.
What you will gain
• Structured onboarding and training, including Good Clinical Practice (GCP).
• Broad exposure to the full clinical research lifecycle in a global medical technology and diagnostics company.
• Close collaboration with leading academic institutions worldwide and senior internal stakeholders.
• The opportunity to shape and improve how our research programs are run, using digital tools such as Smartsheet and AI.
This position will be hired hybrid in Munich, Germany or Chalfont St Giles, UK. Other european locations might be considered remotely. 
At GE HealthCare, our machines, our software, our solutions, our services, and our people make a genuine difference to medical professionals and patients all over the world. That’s because we never lose sight of what healthcare really needs—the human touch. 
 Job Description 
 Join GE HealthCare's Research Alliances team and help bring new diagnostic innovations from research to patients. You will coordinate the day-to-day operations of our research programs, from early investigator-led research to Investigator-Sponsored Trials (ISTs): studies led by external academic investigators using GE HealthCare imaging agents that are still in development.
 Working with colleagues across Legal, Finance, Supply Chain, Medical and Compliance, you will keep studies moving smoothly from application through to close-out and help us improve how our programs run.
 What you will gain: 
 Structured onboarding and training, including Good Clinical Practice (GCP).
 Broad exposure to the full clinical research lifecycle in a global medical technology and diagnostics company.
 Close collaboration with leading academic institutions worldwide and senior internal stakeholders.
 The opportunity to shape and improve how our research programs are run, using digital tools such as Smartsheet and AI.
 Key Responsibilities: 
 Study administration Coordinate the intake, review, approval, and ongoing administration of applications for early investigator-led research programs and ISTs.
 Contracts, supply and payments: Initiate and track study agreements, milestones, product supply, invoices and payments, working with Legal, Finance and Supply Chain in line with approved terms and internal processes.
 Maintain complete, accurate, inspection-ready records across the study lifecycle, from application and approval through reporting and close-out.
 Stakeholder communication: Act as the day-to-day contact for investigators, research sites, suppliers and internal partners. Track study deliverables such as progress reports, publications and final reports, and flag missing information, risks and delays early.
 Meetings and events: Prepare agendas and materials, record decisions and actions, and follow up with action owners. Support advisory boards, symposia, alliance summits and related travel and logistics.
 Process improvement: Maintain and improve templates, process guides, trackers, Smartsheet solutions and dashboards, and contribute ideas to make our operating model more scalable, consistent and data-driven.
 Standard processes: Work in line with GCP, internal SOPs and GE HealthCare policies on interactions with healthcare professionals, data privacy and transparency reporting.
 Other duties as reasonably assigned to support the Research Alliances team.
 Qualifications: 
 Bachelor’s degree in life sciences or a related field.
 Exposure in clinical research operations, healthcare project coordination, research administration, or a comparable regulated environment, including managing structured records, trackers, and controlled documents.
 Proficiency in Microsoft 365 (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Outlook, Teams, SharePoint)
 Working knowledge of AI tools and an interest in applying digital solutions to improve operational efficiency.
 Strong planning and prioritization skills, with the ability to manage multiple studies, stakeholders, and deadlines.
 Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English.
 High attention to detail, sound judgment, and a proactive approach to identifying gaps and driving follow-up.
 Desired qualifications and experience: 
 Master’s degree in life sciences, healthcare, clinical research, or similar.
 Experience using Smartsheet for trackers, workflows, dashboards, or reports.
 Basic knowledge of clinical research principles and Good Clinical Practice (GCP).

items.desc:
Job Description: 
 Your impact 
 Do you want to work on real-time projects, alongside leading scientists and engineers, within a globally renowned company, based on our Edinburgh or Newcastle sites?
 Are you ready to make an impact and gain hands-on experience working on real-world projects from day one?
 Students currently in the final or penultimate year of a degree in Electronic Engineering (MEng) have the opportunity to experience a 6-month paid MEng placement working as an Electronics Engineer within Leonardo. At Leonardo, based on our Edinburgh or Newcastle sites, we’re looking for MEng placement students who want to be part of something bigger - shaping/ innovation, advancing technology, and enhancing global safety.
 Our placements are designed to help you apply your studies in a practical setting, develop your technical skills, and gain valuable insight into how our business operates. You will be given the opportunity to undertake an individual project in support of their academic course of study in an area of electronics design relevant to radar or electro-optic products. You will be introduced to the electronic development processes and utilise state-of-the-art methods, technology and tools. You will report to an experienced engineer who will provide day to day guidance and on the job training.
 Our MEng Placement Programme 
 Our 6-month MEng Placement Programme gives you the chance to work on meaningful projects alongside subject matter experts, within multidisciplinary teams, and across the product lifecycle. Throughout your paid placement you’ll receive coaching and support from a dedicated team, with the potential to progress onto our Graduate Development Programme. You will gain experience on some aspects of the development lifecycle via the individual project. This could include requirements analysis, design, implementation, integration, applied research and test. You will be given the opportunity to learn about the Leonardo products via the project. The MEng project will be based around solving of real-life engineering problems on state-of-the-art avionics sensor systems.
 The programme will run from 1st June to 3rd December 2027. 
 You are required to spend at least three or four days each week on site, to integrate with your team and maximise your learning experience by designing, testing or integrating electronic circuits and components on the Edinburgh or Newcastle sites.
 As an Electronic Engineering MEng Placement student, you will: 
 Contribute to solving real life engineering problems on state-of-the-art avionics sensor systems. Particular emphasis will be placed on learning practical skills that may not be easily gained or experienced in the academic environment of university.
 Apply your academic knowledge to real projects, including design, testing, qualification and/or technology support
 To learn the skills required for hardware development, you will develop practical skills in design techniques for aerospace applications, understand key technologies, and develop your experience using ECAD tools and test equipment
 Develop your skills with the guidance of an experienced supervisor and the wider engineering community
 Deliver technical reports and presentations on you work assignments to your supervisor and fellow MEng students.
 Deliver plans and reports to the required academic standard of your university.
 What you’ll bring: Entry Requirements

items.desc:
Mission
 At the Laboratory for Quantum Magnetism (LQM) we perform fundamental research in magnetism and correlated electron materials. Our core activities span from synthesis of novel materials over in-house experimental techniques in combination with low temperature, high pressures and high magnetic fields, neutron and X-ray scattering to theory and modeling. The LQM is part of the École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne (EPFL), a world-renowned research and education center, offering an ideal academic environment as well as an excellent connection to industry. 
 The available PhD position is centered around microwave spectroscopy of rare-earth quantum magnets, with a focus on entanglement between electronic and nuclear degrees of freedom, transitions between electro-nuclear states driven by external magnetic field, and how the occupancy of those states can be manipulated by external perturbations. Examples of published work can be found in Scientific Reports and Physical Review B . Alongside the above-mentioned experimental technique, our laboratory, and EPFL, offers state-of-the-art laboratories and equipment to facilitate the research. The project will be supervised by Prof. Henrik Rønnow and Dr. Ivica Živković. 
 Main duties and responsibilities
 As a PhD Student, you will be expected to: 
 Take responsibility for the development and completion of your doctoral research project 
 Make regular visits to large-scale facilities for Neutron, X-ray and Muon-based experiments. 
 Experiment design and execution 
 Analyze and interpret experimental results 
 Write scientific articles for publication in peer-reviewed journals 
 Present at international conferences 
 Supervise student projects and basic administrative support 
 Contribute to teaching 
 Profile
 We are looking for a highly motivated candidate with a Master’s degree in Physics or a related field. The successful candidate should have a strong background in solid-state physics and quantum mechanics, excellent communication skills in English (spoken and written), and a willingness to learn and engage in challenging research. 
 We offer
 A challenging and exciting PhD project in experimental quantum magnetism, supervised by Dr. Ivica Živković and Prof. Henrik M. Rønnow. 
 Access to state-of-the-art experimental facilities for microwave spectroscopy of rare-earth quantum magnets. 
 Opportunities to perform measurements under low-temperature and high-magnetic-field conditions. 
 A stimulating and collaborative research environment within the Laboratory for Quantum Magnetism and the broader EPFL community. 
 Opportunities to present your research at international conferences and develop collaborations within the quantum magnetism community. 
 Informations
 Applications should include grade transcript, CV, motivation letter and three contact persons for references. For any further information, please contact Dr. Ivica Živković ( ivica.zivkovic@epfl.ch ). We encourage applications from candidates of all genders and diverse cultural and personal backgrounds . 
 The selected PhD student will need to enroll in the physics program of the EPFL doctoral school. After one year of successful probation, the initial contract will be extended up to a total of four years. Doctoral school information and employment conditions at EPFL are described at: 
 https://www.epfl.ch/education/phd/programs/edpy-physics 
 https://www.epfl.ch/education/phd/doctoral-studies-structure/doctoral-students-salary 
 https://www.epfl.ch/about/working/working-at-epfl/employment-conditions

items.desc:
Location 
ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands 
 Description 
 End-to-End Navigation System Engineer in the Navigation Systems Implementation and Validation Section, End-to-End Systems Division, Systems Department, Directorate of Technology, Engineering and Quality.
 Our team and mission: 
 You will belong to the Navigation Systems Implementation & Validation Section (TEC-SEI). The Section provides expert technical support and consultancy to ESA projects, programmes, and general studies in the field of radio navigation systems and techniques (PNT, in particular GNSS). Our core mission focus lies in the critical project lifecycle Phases C and onwards, bridging the gap between detailed design, physical implementation, and operational deployment. To successfully deliver on this mandate, the Section requires strong expertise in system design and validation (engineering).
 Duties 
 As an End-to-End Navigation System Engineer specialising in SI&V, your primary responsibilities will focus on the end-to-end integration, testing, and validation of complex navigation architectures. You will support established programmes like Galileo, as well as new and emerging ESA PNT missions such as the Celeste LEO-PNT In-Orbit Demonstrator and OpStar. Your duties will include:
 defining, guiding, and executing comprehensive System Assembly, Integration and Validation (SI&V) strategies and test campaigns across Phase C, D, and E lifecycles for Galileo (G1 and G2), Celeste LEO-PNT, and OpStar;
 providing expert system design and validation engineering support to subsystem-level and system-level Assembly, Integration, and Testing (AIT) and AIV processes, ensuring correct flow-down of system requirements to the segment and payload levels;
 operating and exploiting ESTEC Navigation Laboratory facilities—including System Test Beds (e.g., G2STB), Radio Frequency Constellation Simulators (RFCS), and Test User Receivers (TURNs)—to conduct Signal-in-Space (SIS) compatibility testing and end-to-end performance verification;
 supporting commissioning and in-flight operations, including Launch and Early Orbit Phase (LEOP) and In-Orbit Testing (IOT) activities, actively investigating system anomalies, and managing the resolution of non-conformances;
 supporting the performance monitoring of Systems in operation, investigation of system anomalies and the design, development and validation of related tools;
 participating as a technical expert in formal project reviews (e.g., Critical Design Reviews [CDRs], Test Readiness Reviews [TRRs], and Acceptance Reviews [ARs]), evaluating industrial data packs to ensure integration readiness and system design maturity;
 defining test scenarios, coordinating data dissemination analysis, generating test vectors, and executing hardware-in-the-loop laboratory activities to evaluate and verify new PNT subsystems and equipment;
 contributing to the continuous improvement of SI&V engineering best practices, standards, and tools, actively capturing and sharing validation methodologies across the Agency.
 Technical competencies 
 Deep understanding of system design and verification processes for space missions (focusing on Phase C and onwards), specifically for GNSS and emerging PNT architectures (e.g., LEO-PNT)
 Proven hands-on experience defining test plans and executing hardware/software test campaigns in laboratory environments using system test beds, signal simulators, and advanced receivers
 Familiarity with the Galileo system architecture, signals (e.g., OS, HAS, PRS), and its specific SI&V operational processes
 Experience in preparation of procurement activities for technology development and innovation (statements of work, proposal evaluation)
 Experience in the management and technical monitoring of industrial activities, including resolving complex integration non-conformances and driving formal technical reviews

 Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking
For more information, please refer to ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook 
 Education and professional experience 
 A master's in telecommunication engineering or another relevant domain is required for this post, together with 4 years of relevant professional experience.

 experience of working with satellite navigation in particular and PNT in general;
 knowledge of and proven experience in machine learning or data analysis applied to PNT, end-to-end navigations systems performance analysis, GNSS receiver signal processing, advanced positioning algorithms are all considered assets;
 strong technical, analytical, organisational and reporting skills, with a proactive attitude to solving problems;

 understanding of the ESA procurement process.

items.desc: We are seeking to appoint a Research Assistant (AI Scientist & Computational Cancer Biology) to join the Nuffield Department of Medicine, University of Oxford, working on an state of the art project funded by Advanced Research & Innovation Agency. Reporting to Dr Lennard Lee, Programme Director, you will serve as an AI Scientist & Computational Cancer Biology Research Assistant for the UK Cancer Vaccine AI Scientist & Supercomputing Project. The UK Cancer Vaccine AI Scientist & Supercomputing Project is a government-supported national flagship research initiative hosted by the University of Oxford. The project brings together sovereign AI supercomputing, AI Scientists, automated laboratories, and immunology to develop and manufacture safer, more precise and more effective personalised cancer vaccines. To accelerate the development of personalised cancer vaccines for NHS patients, we seek to create an AI scientist capable of reviewing scientific discovery, generating hypotheses, designing experiments, controlling laboratory workflows, and analysing results. By integrating advanced machine learning with robotic laboratory automation, experimental findings are rapidly fed back to the AI scientist, enabling increasingly accurate predictions and accelerating the pace at which new scientific discoveries can be translated towards patient benefit. The project has been recognised as one of the UK’s leading strategic research initiatives, having been referenced within both the Government’s AI for Science Strategy and the 10-Year National Cancer Plan. It is supported by major UK research funders and government organisations, including ARIA, the Medical Research Council, UK Research and Innovation, Cancer Research UK and the Department for Science, Innovation and Technology, alongside a consortium of more than 2,500 scientists, clinicians, engineers, patient representatives and technology experts. The successful candidate will join a highly collaborative multidisciplinary team working at the interface of artificial intelligence, computational biology, cancer immunology, robotics, software engineering and clinical research, contributing to research that aims to establish new approaches for the discovery and development of personalised cancer vaccines. You will provide computational research support within the programme, working with large-scale cancer, genomic and immunological datasets and applying established and emerging artificial intelligence approaches to cancer vaccine research. They will use frontier and open-source AI models and agentic coding tools, contribute to the development and evaluation of AI models and scientific agents, and support computational analyses alongside cancer biologists, immunologists and AI researchers. The post holder will manage their own research and administrative activities within agreed guidelines and contribute to project planning, data analysis, research outputs and collaborative research . It is essential that you hold a degree in computer science, computational biology, bioinformatics, genomics, cancer biology or a related discipline and possess sufficient specialist knowledge in computational biology, bioinformatics, artificial intelligence or data science to work within established research programmes. You will have experience analysing biological, genomic, biomedical or other large-scale research datasets using computational methods, practical experience using modern AI models or AI-assisted coding tools, with an ability to apply them appropriately to research tasks and some experience developing, adapting or evaluating computational models, machine-learning approaches, AI agents or reproducible computational workflows. Applications for this vacancy should be made online and you will need to upload a supporting statement and CV. Your supporting statement must explain how you meet each of the selection criteria for the post using examples of your skills and experience. Please restrict your documentation to your CV and supporting statement only. Any other documents will be requested at a later date. This position is offered full time on a fixed term contract until 30 September 2030 and is funded by ARIA. Only applications received before 12 midday on Monday, 9 November 2026 will be considered. Please quote 189247 on all correspondence.

items.desc: The AIT Austrian Institute of Technology is Austria’s largest Research and Technology Organisation (RTO) . We aim to transform scientific excellence into innovation with impact. Together with our partners, we develop technologies and solutions for a sustainable, resilient, and digitalised future, strengthening Europe’s competitiveness and technological sovereignty. Our international teams combine cutting-edge research with strong implementation expertise to create measurable value for industry and society. Our Center for Energy is looking for new Ingenious Partner for our location in Vienna (Giefinggasse, 1210). In the Center for Energy , we develop sustainable, resilient energy systems to drive the green transition. As part of our digital transformation strategy, the AIT Research Acceleration Platform (ARA) integrates cutting-edge process automation, digital infrastructure, and data governance to accelerate scientific breakthroughs across disciplines such as novel battery materials, energy conversion and storage materials, microbiome engineering in agriculture or light-metal alloys. Our team Energy Conversion and Hydrogen Technologies (ECHT) is a critical part of this platform, specifically with Energy Conversion and Storage Materials platform (ARA-ESM) dedicated to developing novel materials for clean energy technologies like water electrolysis and CO 2 conversion . A major focus lies on combining high-throughput synthesis, advanced fast-track characterisation, and digitalised research workflows to accelerate the discovery of sustainable, durable, and high-performance solutions. Data Steward (f/m/d) - AIT Research Acceleration Platform for Energy Conversion and Storage Materials CENTER FOR ENERGY You will support the ECHT team in its mission of transforming traditional materials research into a fully digitalised, data-driven pipeline for rapid energy technology innovation . Your tasks involve implementing standardised data structures , metadata schemas, and domain ontologies for material deposition, characterisation, and electrochemical testing to ensure full compliance with FAIR data principles and enable downstream automated analytics. You will design, build, and maintain robust data pipelines to automate the ingestion, processing, and curation of complex experimental datasets directly from synthesis systems and analytical instruments. You will create interactive dashboards and data visualisation tools that empower domain researchers to easily explore, query, and interpret multi-dimensional material properties. You will collaborate with domain experts to prepare high-quality, interoperable datasets and support the deployment of machine learning models for predictive material discovery. Solid background in software engineering principles, including scalable architecture, automated testing, version control workflows (Git), and CI/CD pipelines. Hands-on experience with semantic web technologies, knowledge representation , and ontologies (e.g., RDF, OWL, JSON-LD, EMMO) is an advantage. Principal understanding of laboratory data from material synthesis, characterisation, or electrochemical testing is an advantage. Familiarity with interactive visualisation tools (e.g., Plotly, Dash) and foundational machine learning frameworks (e.g., PyTorch, TensorFlow, Scikit-Learn). High level of commitment , strong team spirit, and an enthusiasm for continuous learning and professional development. Very good command of English (spoken and written) is essential, German language skills are an asset. items.desc: Engineering - Leuven | Just now We are looking for Process Engineers for bevel management who will be a member of the Chemical Mechanical Planarization team (CMP) within the R&D Unit Process and Modules organization (UPM), which is responsible for developing processes requested by the process integration departments running imec’s CORE and CMORE programs. What you will do Miniaturization of system size is a driving force in most electronics applications. The continuous scaling of integrated circuits, and the advent of more compact system integration technologies make this possible. Within its affiliation programs and bilateral initiatives, imec contributes to the state-of-the-art in a significant manner. Thanks to recent advances in 3D integration, wafer-level packaging and MEMS, novel types of components with small form factors and an increased number of functionalities are emerging. These novel components also require new and advanced packaging solutions. To support the growing interest in these activities, we are looking for a process Engineer for Bevel management. You are member of the Chemical Mechanical Planarization team (CMP) within the R&D Unit Process and Modules organization (UPM) which is responsible for developing processes requested by the process integration departments running imec’s CORE and CMORE programs. You work in a group of about 20 people with whom you interact daily. You will work in a dynamic multidisciplinary and multicultural environment in close cooperation with Researchers, Scientists, Hardware Engineers, Operations, Equipment Vendors, Industrial Assignees, Device and Process experts. You will be a member of a dedicated interdisciplinary team that is setting up a strategy for wafer bevel management. In this team the wafer edge or bevel is reshaped by trimming, deposition, etching or polishing techniques. For this, you work mainly in the cleanroom, and you are supported by experienced technical staff. Secondly, you are involved in research activities where precise control of the wafer bevel is required (3D integrated systems, 3D memory, image sensors, photonics, biomedical devices, quantum computing...). More specifically, you will: Start-up state-of-the-art semiconductor equipment with a key role in bevel management. Develop a training plan for mastering both equipment and process. Gain understanding on the interactions between your process and the up- and downstream process steps. Work cross-functionally with the integration/process support/hardware teams and industrial partners. Define, organize and validate material & processes during development. Learn and apply specific metrology solutions to characterize these materials. Actively contribute to the research programs and joint development programs with external partners. Report about your work to internal and external partners, and via conference / journal publications. Support fundamental research activities on new materials and integration approaches and perform characterization and failure analysis. Monitor industry trends and innovations, applying scientific knowledge and adapting this to imec research programs and activities. Interface with fellow engineers and researchers to identify future needs and trends. Coordinate and implement the non-standard work in IMEC’s fab organization together with fab process engineers and the pilot line. This includes coordination of the transfer of developed processes and tools to supporting and operational teams. You will be coached on-the-job by senior engineers. What we do for you We offer you the opportunity to join one of the world’s premier research centers in nanotechnology at its headquarters in Leuven, Belgium. With your talent, passion and expertise, you’ll become part of a team that makes the impossible possible. Together, we shape the technology that will determine the society of tomorrow. We are committed to being an inclusive employer and proud of our open, multicultural, and informal working environment with ample possibilities to take initiative and show responsibility. We commit to supporting and guiding you in this process; not only with words but also with tangible actions. Through imec.academy, 'our corporate university', we actively invest in your development to further your technical and personal growth. We are aware that your valuable contribution makes imec a top player in its field. Your energy and commitment are therefore appreciated by means of a market appropriate salary with many fringe benefits. Who you are You have a master’s degree in engineering technology, mechanical engineering, chemistry, physics or material Science. Relevant experience within a research or industrial environment is an advantage. Knowledge of nano technology, chemical or mechanical process technology, or more specific CMP, plasma etch or deposition processes are a plus. Foundry or OSAT experience and semiconductor materials background including characterization / FA is beneficial. …

items.desc: Chez IVIDATA Life Sciences , nous accompagnons les plus grands acteurs de l’industrie pharmaceutique et biotechnologique dans la valorisation de leurs données de recherche et de développement clinique. Nos consultants interviennent au cœur des laboratoires d'innovation pour accélérer la découverte thérapeutique grâce aux technologies data, bio-informatiques et IA les plus avancées. Le Contexte & Vos Missions Dans le cadre du renforcement de l’écosystème digital d'un acteur pharmaceutique de référence situé sur le plateau de Paris-Saclay, nous recherchons un(e) Consultant(e) en Chémo-informatique et Intelligence Artificielle . Intégré(e) au département Chimie Computationnelle et en collaboration directe avec l’Associate Director et les chimistes médicinaux, vous aurez pour mission de fiabiliser, moderniser et automatiser les flux de données chimiques et les outils d'IA prédictive et générative. Vos principales responsabilités : Workflows & Flux de données : Concevoir, optimiser, tester et maintenir des protocoles de traitement de flux de données chimiques Gestion de collections de composés : Assurer la connectivité, l'intégrité et la mise à jour des bases de données de structures chimiques et de données biologiques/physico-chimiques (ADME, Toxicologie), avec interfaçage vers des outils collaboratifs Plateforme de prédiction & Machine Learning : Développer et maintenir les modèles prédictifs de propriétés moléculaires, concevoir des études de référence et suivre la performance des algorithmes au fil du temps. IA Générative & Automatisation : Participer à la maintenance de la plateforme d'IA générative (conception moléculaire de novo , Reinvent, agents IA) et automatiser la réinjection des résultats vers les outils de visualisation des chimistes. Bonnes pratiques logicielles & Cloud : Restructurer et documenter les dépôts GitHub de l'équipe (qualité de code, tests, CI/CD) et accompagner le déploiement de services dans l’environnement Google Cloud Platform (GCP). Profil Recherché Formation : Bac+5 (Master 2, diplôme d’ingénieur) ou Doctorat (PhD) en Chémo-informatique , Bio-informatique ou informatique appliquée aux sciences du vivant. Compétences techniques : Maîtrise avancée de la manipulation de structures moléculaires et de descripteurs chimiques (SMILES, SDF, RDKit). Pratique courante du scripting Python (Pandas, Scikit-learn, PyTorch) et des environnements Shell / Linux. Expérience solide dans la conception de flux de données scientifiques : Pipeline Pilot (un atout majeur) ou KNIME. Connaissance des méthodes de Machine Learning de pointe appliquées à l'ADME/Tox ou au criblage virtuel. Connaissance des plateformes de modélisation (LiveDesign / Schrödinger) et des technologies Cloud (GCP / Docker) appréciée. Bonnes pratiques logicielles indispensables : gestion de versions sous Git/GitHub, code modulaire, documentation et reproductibilité. Langues : Français : lu, écrit, parlé (niveau professionnel opérationnel). Anglais : lu, écrit, parlé (courant / indispensable pour le contexte international de recherche). Savoir-être : Rigueur scientifique, autonomie, sens de l'écoute et du service pour faire le lien entre la data science et la chimie de laboratoire. Pourquoi nous rejoindre ? IVIDATA Life Sciences place l’expertise au cœur de nos actions. Aux côtés des grands acteurs du secteur (laboratoires pharmaceutiques, biotech, dispositifs médicaux, santé animale, cosmétique, nutrition…), nos consultants interviennent sur l’ensemble du cycle de vie des produits : de la recherche préclinique à l’industrialisation. Nos 140 consultants déploient leurs compétences dans 3 domaines clés : Biométrie & Data, Opérations & Développement cliniques, Affaires réglementaires & Vigilances. En rejoignant notre équipe, vous évoluerez dans un environnement stimulant, collaboratif et en constante évolution , où vos idées et votre expertise auront un impact réel.

items.desc: We’re looking for a Business Performance & Margin Analyst to join our team in Madrid and play a key role in shaping the future of neuro-contextual advertising at a global scale. Who We Are Seedtag is the leading Neuro-Contextual Advertising Company. We are redefining how advertising works in a privacy-first world by moving beyond keywords and cookies, towards understanding human emotion, intent, and context. Powered by advanced AI and neuroscience, our proprietary technology, Liz, delivers a deep, human-like understanding of content and attention. This enables brands to connect with audiences at the right moment, in the right mindset, with ads that are relevant, engaging, and respectful of the user experience. Founded in 2014 by two ex-Googlers, Seedtag has grown into a global company with 500+ Seedtaggers across 17 countries, backed by €250M in funding, and expanding rapidly across the open web and Connected TV. We’re not just building technology, we’re rewriting the rules of advertising. Your Challenge As Business Performance & Margin Analyst, you will: Client Intelligence (your biggest lever) Analyse our client portfolio end to end — revenue, margin contribution, delivery quality and growth trajectory — and turn that into a clear point of view on where we should invest more, where we should renegotiate, and where we're losing money. Build the recommendations that our commercial and operations teams act on: what to change per client, which accounts deserve more resources, which patterns separate our profitable relationships from our unprofitable ones. Use campaign and delivery data to produce concrete operating advice, not just reporting. Trading Deals & Agency Economics Own the analysis of all trading deals and the profitability of our agreements with agencies: what each deal costs us, what it returns, and whether the terms still make sense. Build the framework and the recurring review that keeps every deal honest, and flag renegotiation opportunities before renewal. Joint Deals, Partnerships & Added Value Quantify what we give away: joint business deals, partnerships, free impressions, over-delivery and other value-added commitments. Put a euro figure on each one, assess whether it bought what it was meant to buy, and set the guardrails for what we commit to going forward. Contracts, Platforms & Fees Review our contracts with platforms, technology vendors and partners: fee structures, revenue shares, minimum commitments and hidden cost leakage. Model the impact of alternatives and support renegotiations with clear, defensible analysis. Publisher & Supply Profitability Identify which publishers deliver the strongest economics for us: where our margin is highest, where volume and profitability align, and where we're paying more for inventory than the returns justify. Recommend where to deepen partnerships and where to rebalance, backed by numbers. Guarantees & Commitments Analyse our minimum revenue guarantees and similar commercial commitments, identify the ones that are structurally unprofitable, and design how we optimise or exit them. What You’ll Need to Succeed 2–3 years in strategy or operational consulting, with a track record of structuring ambiguous business problems and turning them into decisions leadership can act on. A strong analytical foundation, ideally a Master's in Data Analytics, Business Analytics, Finance or similar. Genuinely data-driven. You're comfortable living in large datasets, you know the difference between a number and an insight, and you don't form an opinion before you've looked at the data. Strong command of AI tools. You understand how modern AI works, you already use it to multiply your own output, and you're excited about working somewhere that treats it as core infrastructure rather than a side experiment. Excellent business judgment and communication. You'll present to commercial leadership, finance and operations and be the person whose analysis settles the argument. Ownership mentality. This is a first-of-its-kind role here: you'll be defining the frameworks, not inheriting them. Fluent English and Spanish. No technical background required. You don't need to code. Why Join Seedtag? items.desc: Institute of Asian and Oriental Studies Cultural History of India 100 % Start of employment 1 August 2028 The University of Zurich invites applications for a professorship in cultural history of India (open rank) starting on 1 August 2028. Candidates are expected to have produced excellent, internationally visible research in the cultural history of India and to bring teaching experience commensurate with their career stage. A source-based, cultural-historical research profile that engages with India's intellectual, religious, and artistic traditions and their reception, reinterpretation, and continuing impact is central to the position, whether based on textual, material, or both types of sources. Of particular importance is the demonstrated ability to connect historical and cultural-historical research with contemporary questions. Applications from Indology are as welcome as from related disciplines (e.g. Religious Studies, History, Economic History, Art History, Anthropology, Linguistics, or Legal History), provided the research is archivally and textually grounded and supported by demonstrated competence in Indian languages. Candidates must possess excellent linguistic and text-analytical competence in at least one Indian language, ideally a classical one alongside a modern Indian language (such as Hindi, Bengali, Tamil, or Urdu). In teaching, the chair is expected to cover the cultural history of India in a wide sense, including engagement with texts, images, and objects, supported by competence in at least one Indian language. The teaching portfolio will address religion, art and material culture, law and politics, society and gender, and ritual and everyday religious practice, with the rela- tive weight given to each shaped by the profile of the appointee. Beyond innovative contributions to the field, the chair is expected to collaborate in research and teaching with the social-science chair in Indian Studies as well as with other professorships at the Institute of Asian and Oriental Studies, at the Faculty of Arts and Social Sciences, and with national and international institutions, including the Museum Rietberg and the Ethnographic Museum of the University of Zurich. A doctorate in Indology or a related discipline, completed by the time of application, and further excellent scholarly publications are required. Depending on the qualifications of the appointee, the professorship will be filled as a full, associate, or assistant professorship with tenure track. Teaching may be carried out in English. Non-German speaking candidates are expected to acquire a working knowledge of German within the first three years of their appointment. The Institute of Asian and Oriental Studies, the University of Zurich, and Zurich as an academic location offer a stimulating research and teaching environment with rich opportunities for scholarly exchange and collaboration. The university of Zurich is committed to equality and to increasing diversity in research and teaching, and expressly invites applications that contribute to these goals. Applications must be submitted online by 7 December 2026. Access and information for the online application are available on the website of the Faculty of Arts and Social Sciences. items.desc: About CMR Surgical At CMR Surgical , we're revolutionising the future of minimal access surgery with Versius , our next-generation surgical robotic system. We're growing fast, and were on a mission to transform how surgery is delivered globally for the benefit of patients, clinicians, and healthcare systems. Our values Ambitious, Humble, People-Focused, and Fair & Responsible define our approach to innovation, partnership, and growth. If you believe in making a meaningful difference in healthcare and want to be part of a purpose-driven company with bold ambitions, now is the time to join us. CMR is an exciting and evolving company to be joining right now. Our commitment to our goal of building a world-class medical devices company is underpinned by the ground-breaking innovation of our next generation of surgical robots and a diverse team of talented and supportive individuals. Were breaking new ground which makes working here exciting, it provides autonomy, opportunity and makes the things you do visible. Come and join us and see what youre capable of. About the Role We are looking for a Data Labelling Engineer to help build how we label surgical video in our Applied AI team. Youll create high-quality labelled datasets and build tools that make labelling faster, more consistent and easier to scale. This is a hands-on role. Youll label and review surgical video yourself and use Python and existing AI models to automate as much of the work as possible. For example, models can suggest labels, carry them across video frames and point you to the footage that most needs a human check. Youll measure how much time this saves and whether quality holds up. Youll work closely with senior engineers, clinical experts and our Quality and Regulatory team. Youll own well-defined pieces of work and keep clear records of how our datasets are built. Those records support model development and future regulatory submissions, such as to the FDA. You dont need a clinical background. Well help you learn the surgical terms you need, and qualified clinicians will make the final call on clinical questions. This role is offered on a hybrid basis, with a minimum of 3 days a week being based in the office. Responsibilities Labelling and review Label and review surgical video, marking surgical phases and steps, instruments and anatomy. Youll use time-based labels, boxes and outlines, following agreed clinical definitions. Work with clinical experts to keep the labelling guidance and examples up to date, and help colleagues learn the tools. Tooling and automation Write and maintain Python scripts and tool integrations to prepare video, sample frames, check metadata and move labels in and out of our systems. Use existing AI models to suggest labels and carry them across video frames. Check where they go wrong, for example when instruments are hidden, or the view is poor. Work with machine learning engineers to find the examples models struggle with and focus labelling effort there. Quality and measurement Track how fast and how accurately labels are produced, including how often reviewers agree. Compare AI-assisted labelling with fully manual labelling before using it more widely. Summarise what each dataset covers and whats missing, and flag groups or conditions that arent well represented. Data governance and regulatory records Keep datasets versioned and traceable: where each video came from, how it was processed, what changed and which tool and model versions were used. Record training, review decisions and disagreements under approved procedures. Handle surgical video securely and follow our rules on confidentiality, anonymisation and access. Keep test data strictly separate from development data and keep AI suggestions separate from approved labels. Support blinded clinical reviews and prepare evidence for our Quality and Regulatory team. items.desc: The role An exciting opportunity has arisen for a Research Support Assistant to join the multi-institutional PIONEER (Programmable In-Organellar Nucleic-acid Entry, Expression and Retention) programme, funded through the ARIA Precision Mitochondria scheme. The project brings together experts across disciplines to develop innovative approaches for engineering biological systems and organelles. Based in the School of Biochemistry and Biomedical Sciences, you will work closely with Prof. Ross Anderson, Prof. Mark Szczelkun, and a collaborative team of researchers. This position is ideal for a recent graduate or early-career researcher looking to build expertise at the interface of computational protein design and engineering biology. The role is designed to provide training, mentorship and research experience that will support future progression to Research Associate positions. What will you be doing? You will contribute to the delivery of key research objectives within the PIONEER programme by applying computational approaches to protein and peptide design and supporting the generation and analysis of research data. Key responsibilities include: Designing protein and peptide binders using state-of-the-art computational methods and AI-based design tools, including RFDiffusion3, proteinMPNN, Boltzgen and DiffDock. Using structure prediction platforms such as AF3, ESMFold2 and Boltz-2 on high performance computing clusters to develop and optimise computational design pipelines. Performing molecular dynamics simulations to evaluate protein structures and interactions. Working with research software engineers and specialist computational platforms to support project development on the UK’s most powerful supercomputer, Isambard-AI. Collaborating with laboratory-based researchers to experimentally characterise designed proteins and peptides. Analysing and presenting research findings at team meetings and contributing to scientific publications. Maintaining accurate research records and contributing to project reporting and milestone delivery. Supporting and occasionally training students or colleagues in computational methodologies. You should apply if You have a degree in a relevant scientific discipline and are enthusiastic about developing a research career in computational biology, protein engineering or related fields. We are looking for candidates who can demonstrate: Experience with computational protein design methods and associated data analysis. Experience of protein structure prediction tools such as AF3 and Boltz-2. Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to present scientific findings clearly. The ability to work independently while recognising when to seek guidance. Good organisational skills and the ability to manage workloads effectively. A collaborative approach and enthusiasm for working within a multidisciplinary research team. Experience of high-performance computing, gene editing systems, bacterial defence systems, or research laboratory environments would be advantageous but is not essential. This is an outstanding opportunity to contribute to a high-profile, cutting-edge research programme while developing valuable computational and research skills in a supportive and ambitious environment. Additional information Contract type: Fixed Term Contract (Specialist Skills) Work pattern: Full time / 35 hours per week Grade: H Salary: £36,320 - £40,704 per annum School/Unit: School of Biochemistry and Biomedical Sciences This advert will close at 23:59 UK time on Monday 2nd November 2026 Shortlisting will take place on Tuesday 3rd November 2026 Interviews will take place on Tuesday 10th November 2026 For informal queries please contact: Ross Anderson ( Professor of Biological Chemistry) - ross.anderson@bristol.ac.uk / 0117 455 8937 Our strategy and mission We recently launched our strategy to 2030 tying together our mission, vision and values.

items.desc: On the 1 August 2026, The University of Greenwich and the University of Kent formed a pioneering new multi-university group called London and South- East (LASE) University Group. Should you join us, you will be employed by LASE but will work as part of the University of Kent academic division, contributing to its distinct strengths, community and identity while also being part of a wider group that brings together the scale, resilience and shared ambition of both universities. Through LASE we aim to deliver outstanding education, impactful research, and meaningful regional and global impact. Kent and Medway Medical School (KMMS) is an exciting collaboration between Canterbury Christ Church University and LASE which builds on their existing high-quality clinical teaching and research strengths. Our mission is to widen participation, train excellent doctors, and improve health in Kent and Medway. Can you provide expert advice in ethical issues relating to research? If yes, then read on. The Kent and Medway Medical School (KMMS) is seeking a Research Ethics Officer to be responsible for all aspects of administration associated with research ethics and research integrity procedures. You will provide dedicated support to KMMS’ Research Ethics Advisory Group (REAG), facilitating the process via which researchers are required to apply for research ethics review for their research activity. As a Research Ethics Officer you can expect to be involved in: Providing administrative support to the internal research ethics review process, developing and implementing ethics templates, procedures, policies, systems and practices Delivering training in university ethics and governance procedures, providing inductions for new research active staff, members of the REAG and the wider KMMS community Coordinating the business of the KMMS REAG, being accountable for efficient and effective functioning of the REAG including initiating and preparing agendas, distribution of REAG papers, recording and preparing accurate minutes What will you bring to the role? Experience of acting as a source of expert advice and communicating complex or specialised information to colleagues with varying levels of knowledge or experience of the subject Appreciation of ethical issues in relation to research and the requirements of a process to review these issues An ability to rapidly assimilate new and complex information What we can offer in return: As a member of our team, you can expect a friendly, open and collaborative working environment and support in your development and wellbeing. You'll enjoy a range of great staff benefits including: Hybrid working options allowing a flexible blend of office and home working (to be agreed in line with business needs) 43 days' leave per year (personal leave, bank holidays and additional days allocated for the Christmas period, pro rata for part-time staff) Excellent pension scheme with generous employer contributions Corporate employee-funded healthcare plan, in partnership with Benenden Health For more information about what you can look forward to if you join us, visit our dedicated webpage: Working at Kent We are ambitious for our people, our communities and the region we serve – join us in making the world a better place. Visit our website for more on who we are: http://www.kent.ac.uk/about/ Please see the links below to view the full job description and to apply for this post. For further information regarding the application process, please contact peopleserviceshr@kent.ac.uk quoting reference number KMMS-143-26. We particularly welcome applications from black, Asian and minority ethnic candidates as they are under-represented at this level in this area Occasionally we may need to close a vacancy before the published deadline due to a high number of applications being received, therefore we strongly advise you to submit your application as soon as possible. (All vacancies will be open for at least one week.) PLEASE NOTE: We prioritise applications from current University of Kent redeployees. We will let you know if this post is to be filled by a redeployee as, in this instance, your application will unfortunately not be taken forward. We know applicants may use AI tools to help prepare job applications. For guidance on how to use AI responsibly and effectively, see: Using AI in your job application Applications must be made via the University’s online application system; CVs or details sent directly to the department or via email cannot be considered. The University of Kent values diversity and equality at all levels. items.desc: We’re a fast-growing social analytics AI scale-up combining network and behavioural science with modern AI to answer complex questions about how people and groups behave in the real world. Following our Series A, we’re looking for an Agentic AI Engineer to join our team in London. The role has two core parts. First , you’ll work alongside our behavioural science team to build AI systems that solve specific client problems. How might a population respond to an unfolding event? How could the behaviour of a group change when its environment changes? How can large volumes of social data be turned into useful behavioural intelligence? You’ll translate behavioural science into agentic workflows that can reason across data, test hypotheses and produce useful outputs for real users. Second , You will join us in building our own foundational AI capabilities that can be reused across multiple clients. Instead of solving every new problem from scratch, you’ll identify what can be generalised and turn it into robust capabilities within our core platform. That means: Building agentic systems around behavioural science and real-world problems Working closely with scientists to translate research and models into AI capabilities Designing multi-step reasoning and agent workflows Building reusable foundational AI components across client deployments Developing tool-use, retrieval, context and evaluation capabilities Taking experiments from rapid prototypes into reliable production systems We’re particularly interested in engineers who have built real LLM or agentic AI systems and enjoy working directly with domain experts rather than receiving perfectly defined specifications. You’ll be working at the intersection of AI engineering, behavioural science and real-world decision-making. What matters is engineering depth, curiosity, comfort with ambiguity and an AI-native way of working. If building AI that turns behavioural science into real-world capabilities sounds like your kind of problem, please apply here.

Garantizamos la igualdad de oportunidades en los procesos de selección, formación y promoción, ofreciendo un entorno laboral libre de cualquier tipo de discriminación por razón de género, edad, discapacidad, orientación sexual, identidad o expresión de género, estado civil o circunstancias personales o sociales. Esta oferta está dirigida a todas las personas que cumplan con los requisitos del puesto. Se valorará especialmente que la persona candidata cuente con un certificado de discapacidad igual o superior al 33%, conforme a la Ley General de los Derechos de las Personas con Discapacidad (LGD).

items.desc: S vyše 2,3 mil. zákazníkov patríme medzi lídrov v poskytovaní telekomunikačných služieb na slovenskom trhu. Ako prví prinášame prelomové inovácie na trhu, či už to bol prvý mobil za korunu alebo nová generácia siete 5G Standalone a stále ideme ďalej. Dnes poskytujeme komplexné telekomunikačné služby pre domácnosti aj podnikateľov vrátane mobilných služieb, pevného internetu, digitálnej televízie a moderných smart riešení. V prvom rade sme však starostlivý, zodpovedný a ľudský zamestnávateľ, a preto hľadáme rovnakých ľudí do nášho tímu. U nás budete od prvého dňa plnohodnotnou súčasťou firmy a našej komunity. Záleží nám na spoločnosti, v ktorej pôsobíme, vnímame svoju zodpovednosť voči nej, a preto sa angažujeme vo verejnoprospešných aktivitách. Pomáhame nášmu okoliu cez Nadáciu Orange, podporujeme mimovládne organizácie a tiež aktívnych jednotlivcov. Prostredníctvom týchto aktivít sa snažíme meniť svet na lepšie miesto pre všetkých. Záleží nám na tom, aby sa u nás každý cítil dobre. Veríme, že zamestnanie nie je len o hodnote, ktorú prinášate firme Vy, no i o tej, ktorú prináša firma Vám. Váš rozvoj je pre nás rovnako dôležitý ako pre Vás, preto Vás v ňom budeme podporovať. Sme hrdí na to, že sme starostlivý a zodpovedný zamestnávateľ. Pokiaľ Vás naša pozícia zaujala a zdieľate s nami rovnaké hodnoty, budeme sa tešiť na Váš životopis. Zaujíma ťa umelá inteligencia, machine learning a nové možnosti, ktoré prinášajú generatívne AI technológie? V Orange Slovensko rozširujeme tím Data Science a hľadáme kolegu alebo kolegyňu, ktorí chcú svoje analytické a technické schopnosti posunúť na ďalšiu úroveň a pracovať na projektoch, ktoré sa reálne dostávajú do produkcie. Budeš súčasťou tímu, ktorý navrhuje a nasadzuje moderné AI riešenia v prostredí veľkej technologickej spoločnosti. Získaš možnosť pracovať s najnovšími technológiami v oblasti umelej inteligencie, cloudových služieb a spracovania dát, pričom tvoje riešenia budú používať tisíce zákazníkov aj zamestnancov. Hľadáme človeka, ktorý má dobré základy v Data Science, rád experimentuje, neustále sa učí nové veci a chce sa rozvíjať v oblasti AI technológií. Čo Bude Tvojou Náplňou Práce Data Science a Machine Learning: pripravovať, analyzovať a transformovať dáta pre AI a ML riešenia navrhovať, trénovať a vyhodnocovať machine learning modely podieľať sa na nasadzovaní modelov do produkčného prostredia monitorovať kvalitu a výkonnosť modelov podieľať sa na riešení analytických a prediktívnych úloh Generatívna AI spolupracovať na vývoji GenAI a RAG riešení experimentovať s novými AI technológiami a frameworkami pripravovať proof-of-concept riešenia a prototypy podieľať sa na evaluácii a optimalizácii AI riešení sledovať nové trendy a možnosti items.desc: ¿Te apasiona la IA Generativa y el Machine Learning? Desde LHH Buscamos un/a Senior Data Scientist para liderar proyectos estratégicos de Inteligencia Artificial con impacto real en negocio en una de las compañías más importantes del sector asegurador. RESPONSABILIDADES DEL PUESTO Colaborar con los responsables de su propia unidad y con el resto de las áreas de negocio y técnicas en la definición y desarrollo de proyectos analíticos, de Machine Learning y de IA, incluyendo IA generativa, asegurando el cumplimiento de plazos y expectativas, supervisando los entregables comprometidos e informando de avances, bloqueos y riesgos potenciales de forma proactiva. Trabajar de la mano con las distintas áreas del Grupo y la Red Agencial para entender en profundidad los problemas de negocio, aplicando escucha activa y teniendo en cuenta las particularidades de cada unidad en la definición de soluciones basadas en datos e IA. Analizar la información existente y proponer nuevas aproximaciones que permitan enriquecerla, incluyendo el uso de datos estructurados y no estructurados, con el objetivo de resolver retos de negocio mediante soluciones analíticas y de IA tradicional y generativa. Diseñar, evaluar y evolucionar soluciones basadas en Inteligencia Artificial aplicadas a casos de uso reales, asegurando su alineación con los objetivos de negocio y con los estándares técnicos del grupo. Definir cuándo utilizar modelos de IA generativa frente a modelos de machine learning tradicionales, reglas u otros enfoques analíticos, aplicando criterio técnico y de negocio. Diseñar y mantener soluciones de IA integradas con datos corporativos, así como definir diferentes métricas de utilidad para el negocio, y para el equipo de Data Science. Promover el uso responsable y controlado de los datos y de la IA dentro de la compañía, conforme a las políticas internas de seguridad, privacidad, cumplimiento y a los estándares de calidad y legalidad establecidos. Aportar capacidades de tratamiento y preparación del dato cuando sea necesario, como soporte a soluciones analíticas y de IA, garantizando la calidad de la información utilizada. Interpretar los resultados de modelos analíticos, de Machine Learning y de sistemas de IA generativa, identificar oportunidades de mejora y proponer estrategias alternativas, comunicando de forma clara los procesos y conclusiones tanto a perfiles técnicos como de negocio. Definir y supervisar KPIs para monitorizar modelos analíticos y soluciones de IA, incluyendo métricas de rendimiento, calidad, uso, costes, latencia, posibles drifts y métricas de gobierno. Liderar proyectos de Data Science y AI de manera individual o en colaboración con otros miembros del equipo y con equipos de consultoría externos, actuando como referente técnico. Mantener y mejorar soluciones analíticas y de IA ya existentes, asegurando su correcta evolución y operatividad en entornos productivos. Documentar las soluciones desarrolladas, justificando las decisiones técnicas adoptadas y definiendo los procesos operativos asociados. Colaborar en los procesos de identificación, evaluación y negociación con proveedores de soluciones analíticas y de IA tradicional y generativa, participando en la definición de los requerimientos técnicos y de control necesarios para el correcto desarrollo de los proyectos. EXPERIENCIA, CONOCIMIENTOS Y HABILIDADES REQUERIDAS Experiencia deseada: Experiencia profesional de al menos 4 años en departamentos de ciencia de datos, con participación en proyectos de analítica avanzada y soluciones de Inteligencia Artificial. Experiencia práctica en proyectos que incorporen modelos de IA generativa (LLMs), e IA agéntica aplicados a casos de negocio reales. Conocimiento de técnicas de prompting, y de evaluación de sistemas de Gen AI, así como de buenas prácticas para el aseguramiento de la calidad de los sistemas de Gen AI, como pueden ser el uso de guardarraíles. Se valorará positivamente haber participado en proyectos del sector del seguro y haber trabajado en otras compañías aseguradoras. Experiencia en trabajo en equipo. Experiencia en coordinación y liderazgo de proyectos analíticos y de IA. Conocimientos avanzados matemáticos y estadísticos, y en técnicas de preparación de datos en bruto (estructurados y no estructurados, incluyendo texto) y creación de modelos de Machine Learning de diferente tipología tales como series temporales, modelos de regresión y apoyo a soluciones de IA generativa. Experiencia en evaluación, monitorización y mejora de modelos y soluciones de IA generativa, incluyendo métricas de calidad, uso y control de resultados. Se valorará positivamente el doctorado. Conocimientos Requeridos: Conocimientos de Python y PySpark, aplicados al desarrollo de soluciones analíticas y de Inteligencia Artificial. Conocimientos prácticos en el uso de modelos de IA generativa (LLMs) aplicados a casos de negocio. Conocimiento de métricas y técnicas de evaluación, monitorización y control de calidad en …

items.desc: About Us Fuzzy Labs is a fast-growing, Manchester-based tech consultancy that helps a diverse range of clients productionise machine learning using Open Source MLOps. We exist to help our customers harness and channel the power of AI safely and effectively, to make positive change and use AI for good. Our work sits across the whole development lifecycle, from prototyping new machine learning models to building scalable and secure production ML systems, and everything in between. Our work spans disruptive startups, multi-national organisations, policing, and secure government sectors, providing you with the unique opportunity to make a tangible, real-world impact. We've had considerable growth over the last few years and we’re looking to continue with this momentum as we build on our reputation as Open Source MLOps experts, expand our role within the community, and continue to deliver high-quality solutions to our clients. What We’re Looking For The ideal candidate will be motivated to grow and progress in line with the company’s ambitions: we’re looking for passionate engineers with an appetite for keeping up with the cutting edge, an eye for detail, and a knack for creative problem solving. As well as being a great engineer, motivated by the chance to be at the forefront of MLOps adoption, you’ll also enjoy being part of a culture that values: Loving what we do: a real passion for Open Source, MLOps, and taking pride in our work. Just trying it: MLOps is an exciting new field. We love to develop new skills, solve new problems and thrive on a challenge. Being greater than the sum of parts: we are a team, one that isn’t just us but our customers and our community. Positive impact: AI is going to change the world. We choose to use it for good and leave a positive legacy. A typical day Our Engineers Collaborate Closely With Their Team Leads And The Customer To Design And Implement High Quality Solutions. We Encourage Our Engineers To Work With a High Degree Of Autonomy And Own Workstreams Across Every Stage Of The Project Delivery Lifecycle, Including Working closely with clients to understand their needs, build strong relationships, and bring them along on the journey. This includes presenting back our solutions in demos and participating in workshops and training sessions. Designing and implementing features to a high standard of engineering, including good documentation and automated testing. Contributing to sprint planning sessions, retrospectives and code reviews, working with your team lead to plan your project work. Ensuring our high engineering standards are maintained and our clients are delighted. Staying up-to-date with a fast-moving industry, embracing new tools and frameworks, and sharing our learnings with the team. As well as client work, we also set aside time to work on R&D projects and produce content in the form of blogs and videos. These projects are how we keep on top of a fast-moving technology landscape, in addition to being our greatest source of marketing. You’ll have the opportunity to craft your own voice in the MLOps community through R&D content. Skills And Experience Our team is made up of a mix of backgrounds. We are looking for smart, curious people who are always expanding their knowledge and exploring new and emerging technologies. If you get excited about keeping up with the newest machine learning research, or figuring out how to scale generative models in the cloud, then you’ll fit right in. Some of the skills and experience we look for include: An undergraduate degree in computer science, mathematics, or similar, or a relevant postgraduate degree. A passion for coding, machine learning, and open source technologies. Proven experience building production-grade ML software in Python - this could include training models from scratch, serving models as web services, or integrating data stores. Experience with cloud computing, for example AWS, Google Cloud or Azure, along with modern DevOps practices and infrastructure-as-code tools. Experience delivering software using an agile development methodology. Fluency in our core tooling: Git, Unix/Linux, Docker, and common open-source MLOps tools. Plus, a strong opinion on your IDE / editor of choice is welcome ;) You should be aware of the broad landscape of machine learning applications, tools, and technologies and willing to deepen your knowledge. We encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet all of the requirements. MLOps is an emerging field, which sits somewhere in the intersection of data science, machine learning engineering, and DevOps. We’re excited to speak to candidates from any of these backgrounds; you don’t need an explicit MLOps background to apply for this role, as you’ll learn as you go by immersing yourself in this exciting new field. items.desc: We are looking for a Signal Processing & Data Analysis Specialist to join our Data Science team. In this role, you will provide technical guidance to migration, engineering, and clinical teams, ensuring a shared understanding of algorithm behavior and expected output characteristics. If you are passionate about applying your expertise in data science to validate algorithms and support system transitions, this opportunity may be the right fit for you. items.desc: ⚡️About Volter Volter is a top-tier climate VC-backed B2B energy tech platform building the products that make clean, renewable power simple for businesses everywhere. The energy transition is a huge and vital opportunity, but it's currently too difficult for commercial & industrial companies to achieve. Historically, the energy industry has been too opaque, complex and lacking in trust. We’re fixing that. Our aim is to be the “Octopus Energy for industry”: a modern tech platform providing new renewable energy products with radical transparency — accelerating deployment of renewables and helping customers cut cost and carbon without complexity. We’re excited to use technology to help our customers deploy & utilise more renewable energy and fast forward the energy transition - and we need your help! 💼 Role: Data Scientist You’ll lead our data science work, including owning forecasting and pricing optimisation: producing accurate half‑hourly demand and generation forecasts, shaping prices, quantifying uncertainty and translating it into simple decisions for customers and our supply portfolio. You’ll own the full model lifecycle—from problem framing and baselines to productionisation, monitoring and iterative improvement. You are a self-starter who excels both independently and in a team. You dislike corporate structure and bureaucracy, and believe in a "best idea wins" culture. This is why you prefer a growth-oriented, flat, startup environment. A desire to keep learning and having an impact is very important to you. You fear looking back in 10 years time and realising you never made a difference…that you were simply a tiny cog in a large machine that will churn on with or without you. 🛠️ Day-to-day Responsibilities Build, validate and deploy time‑series models (including probabilistic where useful) and matching optimisation algorithms for customer demand and generation and constantly improve model performance Understand customer profiles and develop relevant features from HHD, weather, calendar and price inputs; set up robust back‑tests and error attribution Develop, maintain and improve pricing and trading decision engines to maximise PnL Alongside engineering, create reliable feature/data ETL pipelines, and partner with product to surface insights in the platform Create risk and hedging analytics (e.g., shape/volume error distributions, scenario analysis, what‑if tools) Design monitoring for model/data drift; manage model registries and experiment tracking Be responsible for driving new initiatives to improve business outcomes from a data science perspective and be able to drive and own from idea to scoping, production and maintaining Communicate results clearly to non‑technical stakeholders; build explainability into outputs 🧩 What Experience You Bring 4–8+ years in Data Science/ML with a focus on time‑series forecasting and decision analytics Strong Python (pandas, NumPy, scikit‑learn, statsmodels; PyTorch/TF a plus) and SQL; rigorous evaluation (MAE/RMSE, MAPE, pinball loss) Experience productionising models (APIs/batch jobs), experiment tracking (e.g., MLflow) and basic MLOps Being able to evaluate the right tools for the job given business requirements & experiment with new ways of doing things to continuously improve Comfort combining statistical baselines with ML methods (gradient boosting, GLMs, probabilistic models) We need a hands‑on lead who can ship useful forecasts and iterate quickly without a big platform team. Energy experience accelerates you, but we’ll value evidence that you can master domain context fast and build pragmatic, explainable models that survive contact with production. 💥 Stand‑out Candidates Will Have Experience In… GB energy markets (half‑hourly settlement, weather‑driven load, network tariffs) and portfolio risk analytics Experience with AWS and infrastructure (eg Terraform) Experience and willingness to surface insights in relevant UIs/products Forecast explainability, uncertainty quantification and decision tooling for non‑technical users Optimisation (LP/MIP) for hedging or tariff design 🤘Who You Are Curious, pragmatic and outcome‑driven. You love shipping models that make decisions better today rather than making them better tomorrow. You are energised by early-stage businesses, are adaptable and thrive within startup environments. You have a strong bias toward action and having an impact quickly. You want to get sh*t done. You are a self-starter and autonomous in your way of working, but ultimately believe a team can get further together than any individual. You communicate clearly and keep things as simple as possible. 🌱 What You Can Expect From Us A dynamic and fast-changing environment with incredible responsibility and autonomy Working directly with and learning from experienced startup founders who’ve invested in and scaled businesses up to several billion dollars in valuation The ability to build and own something from the very beginning Working on …
